Control Number: SWF-26-0001

JUSTIFICATION REVIEW DOCUMENT

FAR Part 6 Justification and Approval for Other than Full and Open Competition PROGRAM/EQUIPMENT: Design Build of the New World Screwworm (NWS) Sterile Fly Production Facility AUTHORITY: 10 United States Code 3204(a)(2) as implemented in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency

ESTIMATEDAMOUNT:

PREPARED BY CONTRACTING OFFICER TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS SIGNATURES ARE REQUIRED BELO..

I have reviewed this justification and find it adequate to support Other Than Full and Open Competition.

PROGRAM MANAGER SMALL BUSINESS SCO OFFICE OF COUNSEL SENIOR CONTRACTING OFFICIAL HQ OFFICE OF COUNSEL COMMAND ADVOCATE FOR COMPETITION HEAD OF THE CONTRACTING ACTIVITY (HCA) 1 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 FAR Part 6 Justification and Approval for Other than Full and Open Competition

1. Requiring Activity: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Animal and Plant Inspection Service.

2. Contracting Activity: United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District (SWF), 819 Taylor Street, Fort Worth, Texas, 76102.

3. Description of Action: This Justification and Approval authorizes the use of Other than Full and Open Competition---Unusual and Compelling Urgency-- to limit issuance of the Phase I design build competition to 5 contractors, as follows:

The firm-fixed-price Design-Build standalone contract is for the immediate design and construction of a new domestic New World Screwworm (NWS) Sterile Fly Production Facility at Moore Airfield, Hidalgo County, Texas. This facility, funded by USDA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) appropriations, is urgently needed to support the USDA's efforts to prevent a devastating NWS outbreak in the United States. While the standard solicitation period is 30 days, the Government has determined that issuing the Phase I solicitation will be accelerated but allow for competitive proposals and will balance the limited responses in the sources sought with the unusual and compelling urgency of the mission. USACE expects more than one offeror even with the shortened Phase I solicitation period.

4. Description of Supplies/Services: The USDA requires, with extreme urgency, a design-build standalone "C" type contract for a specialized, complex facility dedicated to the mass rearing and sterilization of NWS flies. This facility will produce up to 300 million sterile flies per week. This production capability is essential for the USDA's Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) program aimed at preventing the spread of NWS into the U.S. and protecting the nation's livestock and wildlife. The facility must be designed and constructed to meet stringent biosecurity and containment requirements to ensure effective production of sterile flies for the eradication program. Execution of the project may require appropriate brand name equipment for the irradiation technique and diet mixer and/or installation of such items by directed subcontractors who can deliver equipment in an expedited manner and perform any required commissioning necessary to meet mission requirements.

Secretary Rollins has determined that the overall goal is to have a complete facility that can produce 300 million sterile flies per week. Given the urgency of the threat, USDA is open to a phased approach to achieve this goal. The anticipated period of performance Control Number: SWF-26-0001 to construct a facility to produce 100 million sterile flies per week is 12-18 months. The work on the remaining 200 million flies per week capacity would be conducted in parallel, as either an expansion of the original facility or as a second facility. Design and construction of the remaining production capabilities beyond the first 100 million may take up to 48 months. The estimated value of this procurement is ███████████

5. Authority Cited: 10 United States Code 3204(a)(2) as implemented in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

6. Reason for Authority Cited: a. Background: The NWS is a parasitic fly larva that infests warm-blooded animals, causing severe pain, tissue damage, and potentially fatal secondary infections. Historically, NWS infestations have devastated livestock industries across the Americas, resulting in significant economic losses and disrupting local economies. The United States successfully eradicated NWS in the 1960s through the innovative SIT, which involves releasing sterile male flies to disrupt the reproductive cycle. Following the lead, Mexico also eradicated the fly, and this led to the Panama–United States Commission for the Eradication and Prevention of Screwworm (COPEG), an organization created to stop the screw worm from going north of Panama. After the eradication, economic and health effects became a direct benefit to society.

After decades of successful eradication, recent NWS outbreaks in Mexico and Central America now present a serious threat as of late September 2025. Just 70 miles from the U.S. border a cow had a confirmed case. These outbreaks have prompted the USDA to suspend live animal imports from Mexico and launch containment plans, including sterile fly production and dispersal facilities. To combat this threat, Secretary of Agriculture launched a comprehensive five-pronged plan, one aspect of which is what this proposal enables. The competition limitation supported by this J&A directly supports the fourth prong of the USDA’s plan: "Take the Fight to the Screwworm," and protects US economy and public health. Limiting the Phase I solicitation to the 5 highly qualified contractors and providing a response time of up to twenty-one days, ensures the prompt delivery of actionable proposals that will greatly increase success, while also providing sufficient time to meaningfully prepare quality phase 1 proposals. Additionally, the proposals will likely need to incorporate long lead brand name equipment for the irradiation technique and diet mixer and/or to be installed by directed subcontractors that manufactured the equipment and specialized biolab security commissioning agents. These measures enable the Government to meet the urgent need for this facility by minimizing evaluation time, focusing resources on the most capable firms, and expediting contract award. b. Alternatives: Several alternatives to this justification were considered:

1) Conducting a Competitive Acquisition: The most obvious alternative is full and open competition. However, the time required for preparing the solicitation, issuing a solicitation, evaluating proposals, and documenting the down select from an unlimited 3 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 pool of potential offerors would result in unacceptable delays. Any delays to this acquisition would increase the risk of a widespread NWS outbreak, causing significant economic and public health damage (as discussed below). Specifically, a full and open competition with unlimited potential offerors would require a minimum of 45 days for proposal submission (15 days for presolicitation and 30 days for Phase 1 solicitation) and 90 days for evaluation and down-select documentation, resulting in a total delay of approximately 135 days. Any delays to this acquisition would increase the risk of a widespread NWS outbreak, causing significant economic and public health damage (as discussed below). Conversely, limiting the Phase 1 offerors to 5 qualified contractors ensures that the evaluation time is limited and spent on quality proposals. Limiting competition to these qualified contractors, considered technically equipped to provide beneficial results to the government, is anticipated to reduce the 135-day time span to only 90 days. This is why only a limited number is required.

2) Extension of an Existing Contract: There are no existing contracts suitable for the rapid design and construction of a facility with the specific biosecurity and production requirements of the NWS sterile fly production facility. There are no contracts currently in place that could meet the size and scope of this requirement.

3) Use of In-House Resources: The USACE does not have sufficient in-house resources to design and construct a facility of this magnitude within the required timeframe. This would require hiring new personnel and developing the necessary expertise, resulting in unacceptable delays. c. Impact if not approved: Disapproval of this J&A would have catastrophic consequences for the U.S. economy and public health, leaving the nation vulnerable to a devastating outbreak of NWS in the US. The implications extend far beyond the state of Texas and represent a significant threat to the entire country. As mentioned in the Background section, Texas already experienced significant risk due to its proximity to Mexico. Other risks include the following:

1) Economic Devastation, Nationwide1: A widespread NWS infestation would cripple the U.S. agricultural sector. While the potential $1.8 billion loss to the Texas economy is alarming, it only represents a fraction of the potential nationwide impact. Texas is a major producer of beef, cotton, and other agricultural commodities. A disruption to Texas agriculture would ripple through national supply chains, impacting food prices, availability, and the profitability of countless businesses. Texas is the largest cattle producing state. If the screwworm decimated Texas herds, the price of beef would skyrocket nationwide. Restaurants would face higher costs, consumers would pay more at the grocery store, and the entire beef supply chain would be thrown into chaos. Other agricultural sectors are similar. An NWS outbreak would lead to increased prices for everything from dairy products and wool to cotton, impacting 1 USDA. (n.d.). NWS Economic Impact Report. USDA Animal and Plant Inspection Service. https://www.aphis.usda.gov/sites/default/files/nws-historical-economic-impact.pdf 4 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 clothing manufacturers, textile mills, and the retail sector.2 Beyond direct agricultural impacts, an NWS outbreak would negatively impact related industries, such as transportation, processing, and retail. Rural communities that rely on agriculture would be particularly hard hit, potentially leading to job losses and economic hardship. Additionally, consider the tourism industry. Hunting, fishing, and other outdoor activities are vital to many state economies. Wildlife infestations would devastate ecotourism, impacting guide services, hotels, restaurants, and other businesses.

NWS Losses: 1976 Results 2016 Results 2024 Results Texas Data (Adjusted for inflation only) Cattle Population 7,224,515 - Cattle Infestation Rate 20.60% - Cattle Cost/Case $81.51 $346.28 $452.14 Sheep & Goat Population 3,654,945 - Sheep & Goat Infest. Rate 9.10% - Sheep & Goat Cost/Case $32.38 $137.56 $179.61 Total Cattle Cost $121,307,258 $515,351,210 $672,897,355 Total Sheep & Goat Cost $10,769,588 $45,752,456 $59,738,286 Texas Producers Losses $132,076,846 $561,103,666 $732,635,641 Texas Economy Loss $329,598,005 $1,400,235,237 $1,828,293,838 2) National Public Health Crisis: While less common in humans, NWS infestations can be a serious threat, particularly to vulnerable populations (children, the elderly, individuals with compromised immune systems). The maggots burrow into open wounds, causing intense pain, tissue damage, and potentially life-threatening secondary infections. An outbreak would overwhelm the public health system, requiring increased medical surveillance, diagnostic testing, and specialized treatment facilities. It would also necessitate widespread public awareness campaigns to educate people about the risks and how to prevent infestations. The resulting surge in medical costs, coupled with lost productivity due to illness, would further strain the U.S. economy.

3) Erosion of International Trade and Reputation: An NWS outbreak would damage the reputation of the U.S. as a reliable exporter of agricultural products, leading to trade restrictions and economic losses. Trading partners would be hesitant to import U.S. goods, fearing contamination. This would negatively impact the U.S. trade balance and undermine its position as a global leader in agriculture.

4) Threat to National Security: A widespread disruption to the U.S. agricultural sector would threaten the nation's food security and economic stability, posing a national security risk. Access to safe and affordable food is essential for maintaining a stable society. An NWS outbreak could lead to food shortages, price increases, and social unrest.

2 New World Screwworm outbreak in Central America and Mexico. Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service. (n.d.). Accessed September 26, 2025, https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultrydisease/cattle/ticks/screwworm/outbreak-central-america 5 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 5) Animal Welfare: Animals would experience suffering for extended periods of time. Farmers would be forced to take action including euthanizing the animals, to help alleviate the issue. d. The design-build approach with the appropriate brand name equipment to be installed by directed subcontractors, combined with restricting competition, is the only viable strategy to address this unusual and compelling urgency and avert these potentially catastrophic consequences. Failure to approve this J&A would directly impede the USDA's ability to implement its NWS eradication plan. The immediate construction of the sterile fly production facility is essential for producing the volume of sterile flies needed to effectively suppress the NWS population along the U.S.-Mexico border. Without this facility, any delay in award will continue to expose the cattle industry to the risk of NWS infestation, resulting in economic devastation for producers and significant financial obligations for the Government related to outbreak response, containment, and potential trade disruptions. Therefore, an unusual and compelling urgency exists, requiring the expedited completion of this acquisition to mitigate these risks and enable the USDA to begin eradicating the NWS threat to the U.S. economy.

7. Efforts to Obtain Competition: To balance the urgent need for a NWS Sterile Fly Production Facility with the requirement to obtain competition to the maximum extent practicable, USACE Fort Worth will issue a request for proposal to the 5 contractors. As discussed in the market research section below, USACE and USDA used concerted efforts to ensure requirements were not unduly restrictive while still meeting the key aspects of the requirement. The market research determined that 5 contractors were technically capable and expressed interest in the project during the market research process. The notice required at FAR 5.201 will not be published based on the exception at FAR 5.202(a)(2), Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

8. Actions to Increase Competition: SWF is mindful of the requirement in FAR 6.302-2 to request offers from as many potential sources as is practicable under the circumstances, and therefore conducted a robust search and evaluation of potential sources following the procedures outlined in Paragraph 9, Market Research. However, to expedite the design build procurement with the appropriate brand name equipment to be installed by directed subcontractors to address the USDA identified National Emergency there is a need to limit an offer from more than 5 sources under Phase I or enter into negotiations with more than three in Phase II.

9. Market Research: In accordance with FAR Part 10 and DFARS 210.001, thorough market research was conducted to identify all qualified sources capable of fulfilling the urgent requirement for the design and construction of a domestic NWS Sterile Fly Production Facility. USACE worked with the USDA Contracting office, they were able to help identify potential firms based on historical knowledge of contractors they've worked with. However, USDA has limited recent knowledge of construction firms. a. Small Business Database: A search of the Dynamic Small Business Search Database shows no small business firms capable of executing the requirement in Texas 6 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 at sufficient bonding capacity. There are 29 small businesses registered in Texas under the appropriate NAICS but none had a bonding capacity over $100M. b. Sources Sought: To maximize awareness of this opportunity, USACE and USDA directly reached out to over 400 vendors to notify potential offerors of the sources sought announcement. This action also included the USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS)contact list that has vendors who are likely able to handle projects of these sorts. The Sources Sought was posted to SAM.gov on 2 October with a response date of 14 October 2025. c. There were 11 responses to Sources Sought Notice W9126G26R1AS7, as shown in the table below. Of the 11 responses, two firms were not construction contractors, one firm was a small business who did not possess the required bonding capacity or specialized experience, and one firm did not demonstrate enough recent and relevant experience for further consideration. While market research shows many firms performing design or construction projects, the offerors were experienced in either design or construction, not both, and not at biosafety level (BSL) 2 or BSL 3.

1) USDA APHIS BSL guidelines establish procedures for handling infectious agents that pose risks to animals, plants, and the environment. APHIS utilizes these biosafety levels, which range from BSL-1 to BSL-4, and a specialized version called BSL-3-Ag (for agricultural research), to regulate laboratory work and ensure public and environmental safety. The level of biosafety required depends on the risk of the agent. This can include specific requirements for personal protective equipment (PPE), laboratory design, decontamination procedures, and waste management. The production of sterile flies for research or pest control, often requiring BSL2 or BSL3 containment, demands particular attention to these guidelines, especially regarding facility design and construction.

2) Due to the intricate design and specialized construction requirements of a BSL2/BSL3 sterile fly production facility, including stringent containment and environmental controls, experience with both design and construction under a single entity is critical. This integrated approach minimizes communication gaps, reduces coordination challenges, and ensures seamless execution, ultimately mitigating risks to project success. Most vendors were also more experienced with subcontracting; or were responsible for construction management services only.

The market research, including extensive outreach and analysis of submitted responses, identified 5 firms ( that appear to possess the capabilities and experience most likely to successfully execute this technically complex and time-sensitive project. These firms demonstrate the necessary bonding capacity, relevant experience in design-build projects, and a track record of successful construction within regulated environments.

10. Interested Sources: To date, no other sources have written to express interest.

11. Other Facts: a. Procurement history. This action is a novel requirement for the United States and more specifically USACE. While the SIT has been used to combat the NWS, and while the USDA has been contributing to the effort for a number of years, there has never been a domestic production facility constructed and operated within the United States for this purpose. The primary NWS production facility is located in Pacora, Panama. This facility is operated by the Panama-United States Commission for the Eradication and Prevention of Screwworm (COPEG) and funded by the USDA and Panama's Ministry of Agriculture.

However, as COPEG is a bi-national commission, the facility in Panama was not established or operated under U.S. Federal contracting law and regulations. Therefore, there is no directly applicable procurement history within the U.S. Federal system for a facility of this type. b. Other facts. None 9 Control Number: SWF-26-0001

12. Technical Certification: I certify that the supporting data under my cognizance, which are included in the justification, are accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.

[redacted] Program Manager

13. Requirements Certification: I certify that the supporting data under my cognizance, which are included in the justification, are accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.

14. Fair and Reasonable Cost Determination: I hereby determine that the anticipated price to the Government for this contract action will be fair and reasonable. The Contracting Officer will determine the price fair and reasonable through limited competition and a negotiation process focused on maximizing value within the established budget. The Government will leverage the budget as a basis to negotiate enhancements and betterments, ensuring they align with project requirements and offer a demonstrable return. A detailed price analysis, using independent government estimates, will validate the value of proposed enhancements. This competitive negotiation approach ensures the final contract price reflects the optimal balance of price and performance within the budget constraints, thus establishing a fair and reasonable price.

[redacted] Contracting Officer

47PB5326C0001.text:
U.S. General Services Administration Public Buildings Service Acquisition Project Delivery Capital Construction Division Office of Acquisition Management

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION (FAR 6.103)

Emergency Demolition of Multiple Buildings at the St. Elizabeths West Campus, Washington, DC

1. Agency and Contracting Activity (Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.104-1(a)(1)) The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), plans to contract by means of other than full and open competition.

Vendor Name: Clark Construction Group, LLC (Clark) UEI: QQBXQR679KM9

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved (FAR 6.104-1(a)(2)) GSA intends to award a sole-source contract to Clark Construction Group, LLC, for the controlled demolition of multiple vacant, dilapidated buildings located within the secure perimeter of the St. Elizabeths West Campus, Washington, DC. These buildings pose significant security and safety risks as identified by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

The Secretary of the DHS wrote GSA on 12/19/25 to invoke the Emergency Undertaking Authority under the St. Elizabeths Programmatic Agreement (PA) with GSA. The PA governs the redevelopment of the St. Elizabeths West Campus. Her invocation was supported by DHS’ Office of the Chief Security Officer (OCSO), in coordination with the Federal Protective Service (FPS) and the Office of the Chief Readiness Support Officer (OCRSO).

The FPS’ assessment of the St. Elizabeths Campus identified significant security and safety risks posed by the vacant buildings located on campus. These risks impact personnel safety, campus operations, and emergency response capabilities. The assessment’s conclusion was that immediate attention is required to address the security and safety vulnerabilities associated with vacant buildings on campus. Its recommendation was that the buildings should be removed; if these buildings are not removed, the identified security and safety concerns will persist, increasing the risk of potential undesirable events, which cannot be permitted at the DHS Consolidated Headquarters at St. Elizabeths Campus.

The OCSO’s threat assessment of the St. Elizabeths Campus identified Key Vulnerabilities and Risks posed by the seventeen (17) vacant buildings. Its conclusion was that the vacant buildings create significant insider threat vulnerabilities to include physical, technical, and procedural concerns which negatively impact the Department’s security posture. Their reduced oversight, incomplete integration into existing security programs, and physical proximity to leadership and critical operations create opportunities for malicious, negligent, or compromised insiders to plan and execute harmful activities with a lower risk of detection. By removing these unoccupied buildings, the Department can materially reduce the risks associated with these spaces and better protect its leadership, personnel, information, and mission.

3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs (including the estimated value) (FAR 6.104-1(a)(3)) Docusign Envelope ID: C0965D58-3CC5-4C69-AE53-C431C098AC3B Accordingly, demolition of these buildings is necessary to eliminate documented life-safety and national security risks and to meet the Government’s minimum needs. The required demolition services include, but are not limited to: • Emergency demolition planning and execution • Hazardous materials abatement (including asbestos, lead, PCBs, mold, and related materials) • Utility isolation, removal, and demolition • Environmental controls, site stabilization, and restoration • Full compliance with applicable GSA, DHS, OSHA, EPA, NHPA, NEPA, and local permitting requirements These services are required immediately to mitigate the life-safety and national security risks documented by DHS assessments and cannot be delayed without an unacceptable risk to personnel and campus operations.

Estimated Dollar Value: The Independent Government Estimate for this effort is $23 - $30 million dollars.

4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition (FAR 6.104-1(a)(4)) 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2) Unusual and compelling urgency, implemented by FAR 6.103-2.

5. A demonstration that the proposed contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires using the authority cited (FAR 6.104-1(a)(5)) Nature of the Acquisition An FPS assessment entitled “Assessment of Security and Safety Risks Associated with Vacant Buildings on the St. Elizabeth Campus”, dated 12/19/2025, identified the vacant buildings as active threats.

Key Threats identified included: Insider Threat, Hostile Surveillance, Hazardous Materials Release, Explosive Devices, Cyber Threats, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and Explosives Threats, and Ballistic Attack. Other Security and Safety Considerations identified included: Officer Safety, Access Control and Intrusion Detection, Occupant Emergency Plan, Progressive Collapse and Facade and Building Protection.

Please refer to Attachment II for complete details.

The OCSO’s Threat Management Operations (TMO) office completed an assessment entitled “Insider Threat Risk Assessment” on 12/19/25 identifying the following Key Vulnerabilities and Risks.

Key Vulnerabilities and Risks identified included: Physical Access Control, Logical and IT Access, Surveillance, Monitoring and Observation, Technical Security, Staging.

Please refer to Attachment III for complete details.

Considering all these factors, the DHS Secretary formally declared an emergency condition at the St. Elizabeths West Campus. She found the vacant deteriorated buildings, within the level V campus, amounted to imminent threats to life, safety, and national security.

Contractors Unique Qualifications Clark Construction Group, LLC is the only contractor capable of executing the demolition within the required emergency timeframe due to the following non-replicable conditions:

• Immediate On-Site Presence and Mobilization Docusign Envelope ID: C0965D58-3CC5-4C69-AE53-C431C098AC3B o Clark is the prime contractor for the ongoing DHS Building 1 construction project and maintains a continuous, credentialed workforce and heavy equipment already inside the secure perimeter. o No other contractor can mobilize without weeks or months of security processing, badging, escort coordination, and access approvals. • Permit and Campus Familiarity o Clark holds active permits, established utility coordination, and demonstrated experience working under St. Elizabeths specific security, environmental, and historic preservation constraints. o Introduction of a new contractor would require duplicative permitting and coordination, materially delaying risk mitigation.

For these reasons, Clark is the only contractor that can satisfy the Government’s minimum needs within the required timeframe. The government considered whether requesting offers from multiple sources would be practicable under the circumstances. Based on market research and direct outreach to available contract vehicles and contractors, the Government determined that limited competition would not satisfy the emergency invocation by DHS. While other contractors may possess general demolition capability, none can meet the Government’s minimum need to begin work within days. Any competitive or limited-source approach would require solicitation issuance, proposal preparation and evaluation, award, contractor mobilization, and completion of security processing, badging, site access approvals, and permitting. These steps would extend the award and start of performance into a timeframe measured in weeks or months rather than days.

6. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is possible, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by FAR Part 5 and, if not, which exception under FAR Part 5 applies (FAR 6.104-1(a)(6)) Since receiving the DHS Secretary’s emergency invocation on 12/19/25, GSA and DHS have conducted coordination and market awareness activities, including: • Review of available demolition contractors capable of operating within a Level-V secure campus. • Engagement with DHS and GSA construction leadership regarding available procurement alternatives. • Consideration of internal and interagency competitive options, to include: GSA Indefinite Delivery Vehicles (IDVs) and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) and Demolition Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), all of which were determined incapable of meeting the emergency timeline due to access, mobilization, and security constraints.

Given the immediacy of the risk, synopsis under FAR Part 5 is waived pursuant to FAR 5.101(b)(2).

7. A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the government will be fair and reasonable (FAR 6.104-1(a)(7)) The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated price will be fair and reasonable based on a comprehensive price analysis that will consider both standard demolition costs and the premium associated with immediate, emergency performance. The analysis will include comparison to recent demolition costs for similar structures within the GSA Public Buildings Service inventory, adjusted as appropriate to account for accelerated mobilization, after-hours and weekend work, constrained site logistics, and inefficiencies inherent to performing work within an active Level V secure campus.

The Government will rely on the Independent Government Estimate developed by GSA and DHS that includes escalation factors for urgent mobilization, compressed schedules, and security-driven sequencing constraints. Phased pricing tied to discrete building groups will be evaluated to ensure transparency and traceability of costs to specific scopes of work.

The contractor will be required to submit a detailed price proposal supporting its approach and level of effort. Where the contractor proposes alternative phasing, sequencing, staffing plans, or means and methods intended Docusign Envelope ID: C0965D58-3CC5-4C69-AE53-C431C098AC3B to further accelerate completion or reduce risk, the Government will evaluate such proposals as part of the price analysis to determine whether the proposed pricing reflects a reasonable correlation between cost, schedule, and performance. The Government may also consider optional or alternative submissions that present different execution strategies, provided they meet the Government’s minimum emergency requirements.

An initial price analysis will be completed and documented in the contract file with award of the letter contract, with a full price analysis to be completed and documented in accordance with the letter contract definitization schedule.

8. The market research conducted (see FAR Part 10) and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted (FAR 6.104-1(a)(8)) Review of available demolition contractors with federal experience and the demonstrated ability to operate within secure, restricted-access facilities.

• Review of applicable contract vehicles, including the GSA Region 7 Complex Construction IDIQ, GSA National Construction IDIQs, and USACE Demolition and MATOC IDIQs, to assess availability of contractors capable of meeting the emergency execution timeline and access requirements. • Coordination with DHS and GSA subject-matter experts, including facilities, security, historic preservation, and acquisition personnel, to evaluate feasible execution approaches under emergency conditions. • Review of prior demolition efforts at the St. Elizabeths Campus and comparable secure federal campuses to assess mobilization timelines, access constraints, and execution risks.

Based on the results of this market research, the Government determined that only Clark possesses the combination of existing on-site presence, security access, permitting familiarity, and immediate mobilization capability necessary to meet the Government’s minimum needs within the required emergency timeframe.

9. Any other facts supporting using other than full and open competition, such as: (FAR 6.104-1(a)(9)) (i) When 6.103-1 is cited for follow-on acquisitions as described in 6.103-1(c)(2), an estimate of the cost to the Government that would be duplicated and how the estimate was derived.

N/A

(ii) When 6.103-2 is cited, data, estimated cost, or other rationale as to whether and how much the Government would be harmed.

N/A

11. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services required (FAR 6.1041(a)(11)).

Control No: 2025-102 Justification Review Document FAR Part 6 Justification and Approval for Other than Full and Open Competition Program/Equipment: The Fort Leonard Wood Directorate of Public Works (DPW) Facilities Maintenance Support Services. Authority: 1 O U.S.C. 3204(a)(2) as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 6.302-2 -- Unusual and Compelling Urgency. Amount: $32.2M Prepared by: Contracting Officer: Technical: Requirements: Reviews: I have reviewed this justification and find it adequate to support other than full and open competition. 1 2 Control No: 2025-102 Control No: 2025-102 FAR Part 6 Justification and Approval for Other than Full and Open Competition

1. Requiring Activity: Directorate of Public Works (DPW), Fort Leonard Wood, MO.

2. Contracting Activity: U.S. Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC)-Fort Leonard Wood, 8112 Nebraska Avenue, Building 11400, Fort Leonard Wood, MO 65473.

3. Description of Action: Requests approval to award a 12-month bridge contract to continue services with TSAY Professional Services, Inc. (TSAY). The Government projects award for 01 December 2025 using fiscal year (FY) 2026 Operations and Maintenance funds.

4. Description of Services: The contractor shall provide all services, materials, supplies, transportation, plant, supervision, labor and equipment, except as specified as Government furnished, to operate, maintain, alter and repair real property facilities and appurtenant structures at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri and the Lake of the Ozarks Army Recreation Area (LORA). The contractor shall provide the above as well as related services in accordance with (IAW) terms, conditions and specifications. Period Period of Performance Estimated Value Base 01 DEC 2025 — 30 NOV 2026 $32.2 M

5. Authority Cited: 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(2), as implemented by FAR 6.302-2 — Unusual and compelling urgency.

6. Reason for Authority Cited: IAW FAR 6.302-2, the Government would incur significant adverse effects if a bridge contract is not awarded by 30 November 2025. The combination of a lapse in appropriations for FY 26 and delays in the solicitation of a new contract caused by the furlough has created a situation that necessitates the issuance of a sole source contract to the current contractor. This action is critical to the maintenance of the base and loss of services would result in severe injury to the Government. Facilities maintenance services cover emergencies and all maintenance, for the “entirety” of Fort Leonard Wood infrastructure. a. Background: W911S7-20-C-0004 expired on 31 May 2025 and FAR Clause 52.217-8 was executed for six months beginning 01 June 2025 and ending on 30 November 2025. The MICC – Installation Readiness Center (IRC) was tasked with completing a new facilities maintenance award by 31 May 2025. In March 2025, it was apparent to MICC and the Requiring Activity (RA) there would not be a new requirement awarded by the expiration of the current contract. The Contract Management Support Officer (CMSO) sent a request for a bridge contract meeting stating that IRC was not 3 Control No: 2025-102 4 projected to have a new contract awarded until August 2026. This delay in award would result in Fort Leonard Wood being without a facilities maintenance contract for nine months at minimum. While competition is generally beneficial, the costs and logistical challenges associated with multiple transitions of services within this timeframe outweigh the potential advantages. TSAY currently possesses the established infrastructure and personnel necessary to provide both emergency and routine maintenance services. This puts TSAY in an exclusive position to continue these services currently, making them unique and the sole entity capable of fulfilling the expiring contract. The performance work statement (PWS) requires a phase-out/phase-in period of no less than two months. The contract expiring prevents another company from receiving the phase-in period they are supposed to be guaranteed in according to the PWS. In addition to not being able to provide a phase-in period for a new contractor, it is not reasonable to expect a new contractor to have time to hire and on-board new employees for a contract that is expected to last less than 12 months. This would drastically increase the costs incurred by the Government as this is a cost reimbursement contract with the full burden of expense being charged to the Government. Other alternatives were researched after discussions with the Small Business Administration (SBA) but the lapse in appropriations has made all other feasible solutions impossible to implement. With the current contract expiring on 30 November 2025, the available time remaining dictates that a bridge contract with the incumbent will avoid injury to the Government or installation caused by a lapse in services. We are entering into the winter season in Missouri and Snow and Ice Removal (SNAIR) and emergency repairs are exclusively covered by the facilities maintenance contract. A lapse without these services would risk serious injury to those who live and work on the installation. It would also delay all training and missions, impacting Army readiness. Facilities maintenance is mission essential to the Army. b. Alternatives. 1) Multiple Stand-Alone Contracts: Awarding individual stand-alone contracts is not a feasible option. The process of awarding a new contract to a contractor other than the incumbent would jeopardize response times for critical emergency projects during the transition and break in services. Furthermore, the consistent volume of small projects required for routine installation maintenance would be inefficiently managed through numerous individual contract awards. 2) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC): Utilizing a MATOC is not a viable solution due to the time required to award individual task orders. While the Fort Leonard Wood MATOC would introduce competition, its firm-fixed-price structure could potentially increase the overall costs associated with providing maintenance services. Control No: 2025-102 5 The MATOC ceiling would also not support the additional work required by facility maintenance. 3) Job Order Contracting (JOC): JOC is also not a feasible option. Accurately scoping and defining quantities for each project under a JOC framework would be a lengthy process and further delay maintenance. This approach could also result in increased costs for the Government due to the complexities of project definition. c. Impact if justification is not approved. A lapse in the current facilities maintenance services will significantly hinder the Fort Leonard Wood DPW’s ability to maintain the installation effectively. DPW relies on this contract to ensure timely repairs and minimize disruptions caused by lengthy solicitation processes. Without the approval, Fort Leonard Wood would cease to function and become unsafe to both the servicemembers and civilians that live and work on the installation. Reliance on alternative contracting methods such as using stand-alone awards, a MATOC, or a JOC, would likely increase both the time required to initiate projects and the overall cost to the Government. Facilities maintenance services cover emergencies and all maintenance, for the “entirety” of Fort Leonard Wood infrastructure. These alternatives introduce complexities and administrative burdens that could compromise the efficiency of essential maintenance operations.

7. Efforts to Obtain Competition: IAW FAR 5.202(a)(2), this action will not be synopsized since the proposed contract action is made under the conditions described in FAR 6.302-2. a. Effective Competition: Because this is a sole source action, effective competition is not applicable. b. Subcontracting Competition: IAW FAR 19.702(b)(1) a subcontracting plan is not required from small business concerns. TSAY (CAGE Code 7PQA8) has re-represented as a small business under NAICS Code 561210 IAW FAR Clause 52.219-28. The incumbent contractor will be required to obtain as much competition as possible for any part of the requirement that is subcontracted and will give maximum opportunity to small businesses. The incumbent contractor is required to adhere to Class Deviation 2021O008, Revision 1, Limitations on Subcontracting.

8. Actions to Increase Competition: While this bridge contract will be awarded as a sole source, limiting immediate competition, the follow-on contract will be a competitive 8(a) procurement.

9. Market Research: IAW Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 205.205-71, DFARS 206.302-1(d), and DFARS Procedures, Guidance and Information (PGI) 206.302-1(d), a request for sources sought was posted to SAM.Gov on 20 July 2025 for 17 days and 10 vendors responded. The results support there is enough small business participation to provide adequate competition and keeping the Control No: 2025-102 requirement in the 8(a) program. However, there was no evidence that a solicitation would result in a timely award that is more advantageous to the Government than awarding a 12-month bridge to the incumbent (TSAY) considering their unique position with infrastructure, personnel, and knowledge of the contract.

11. Other Facts: a. Procurement History. The current facilities maintenance contract was procured as a 100% 8(a) set-aside competition. Ten offers were received in response to the solicitation, and one offeror was selected for contract award. The source selection process was completed in 2020. TSAY was awarded this contract as an 8(a). b. Explanation of comparative pricing between current contract and proposed bridge contract. United States Department of Agriculture Justification to Restrict Competition Identification Number: 12639526R0005 Rev. 11/6/2025 In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 12.102 (b), the following justification documents the decision to restrict competition for this acquisition.

(1) Mission Area and Contracting Activity. The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS), proposes to enter into a contract on a basis other than full and open competition.

(2) Nature and/or description of the action being approved. This J&A authorizes and approves the award of a sole-source, firm-fixed price contract for the aerial release of sterilized screwworm flies to support the New World Screwworm (NWS) response effort. This procurement is essential for the targeted dispersal of sterile flies to support the Secretary of Agriculture's five-pronged plan of the NWS Readiness and Response Policy Initiative.

These services are commercial in nature and will be procured utilizing the procedures listed in FAR Part 12 and FAR Part 15.

The suggested contractor is: Dynamic Aviation Group, Inc. 1402 Airport Road Post Office Box 7 Bridgewater, Virginia 22812-0007

UEI: FQ9BRLCMRLN5

USDA has received priority rating authority under the Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS) regulation (15 C.F.R. part 700) for contracts and orders for the construction and operation of the New World Screwworm (NWS) Sterile Fly Production Facility, and is authorized to use the “DX-H8” priority rating on its contracts and orders for all industrial resources needed for the construction and operation of the NWS Sterile Fly Facility, including facility construction and construction materials, production and construction equipment as defined in the DPAS regulation, and items to be used for the manufacturing of production equipment.

(3) A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs (including the estimated value). This contract provides aircraft and crew services for aerial release of sterilized NWS to support the APHIS New World screwworm program. The contract also allows for the ferrying of sterile pupae from production facilities in Panama and Mexico to the United States. The Panama – United States Commission for the Eradication and Prevention of Screwworm (COPEG), located in Pacora, Panama produces sterile NWS flies. COPEG continues to operate at maximum production capacity in support of eradication efforts, producing approximately 100 M pupae per week. The sterilized pupae are ferried from Panama to a designated base of operations. APHIS continues to evaluate and shift the dispersal polygon and flight grids according to NWS detections. The contractor w ill work in partnership with APHIS to receive weekly updates regarding the flight grids/patterns flown. At any time during the execution of the contract, the number and/or the size of existing grids, as well as the number of municipalities under treatment, may change, as determined by the COR or his/her designated representative.

United States Department of Agriculture Justification to Restrict Competition Identification Number: 12639526R0005 Rev. 11/6/2025 (6) Provide a description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as possible, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by Part 5 and, if not, which exception under Part 5 applies. Due to the unusual and compelling urgency of this requirement, no additional sources are planned to be solicited prior to award.

While a sources sought notice was not posted for this requirement, as exempted by RFO 5.101(b)(2), the USDA anticipates competing similar procurements for NWS aerial release in the future, as described in section 11.

(7) A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable. The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to the Government of the supplies/services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable based on a thorough comparison of historical pricing data from prior and current aerial dispersal contracts, and the development of an Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE) using current market rates.

(8) A description of the market research conducted, and the results or a statement of the reason Market Research was not conducted. Limited market research was conducted for this requirement considering the unusual and compelling urgency of the need. When considering possible companies, USDA technical experts took into consideration the required specifications, historical procurement experience for similar contracts, known companies to be licensed for and capable of providing aerial dispersal, and current contracts utilized for NWS aerial release.

(9) Any other facts supporting use of other than full and open competition, such as: Delay in the award of this contract will seriously impact the ability of USDA to meet the Secretary of Agriculture’s Readiness and Response Policy Initiative. This contract will increase the USDA’s ability to control and contain further spread of the NWS into the United States and infecting the Texas cattle and overall agricultural industry.

As of January 2025, Texas is estimated to have approximately 12.2 million head of cattle, the leading state in beef production in the U.S. The industry contributes approximately $10 billion in revenues annually. The next potential impact, New Mexico, has an estimated 9,000 beef cattle ranches and contributes over 16,000 jobs, generating $1.68 billion in output.

Economic/Societal Impacts – From the USDA news release, “New World Screwworm (NWS) is a devastating pest. When NWS fly larvae (maggots) burrow into the flesh of a living animal, they cause serious, often deadly damage to the animal. NWS can infest livestock, pets, wildlife, occasionally birds, and in rare cases, people. This is a serious concern to the U.S. economy and the U.S. food supply and the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is co mmitted to combatting the spread of NWS to protect American agriculture.” (10) A listing of the sources, if any, that expressed an interest in the acquisition in writing. No other sources expressed an interest in this acquisition.

United States Department of Agriculture Justification to Restrict Competition Identification Number: 12639526R0005 Rev. 11/6/2025 (11) A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition of the supplies or services required. This contract action is being awarded under unusual and compelling urgency as a response to the detection of NWS within the United States border. This action will provide immediat e response efforts to combat the NWS for the initial 6-12 months. During that time, the USDA will work to advertise and compete one or more aerial dispersal contracts for these services. United States Department of the Interior NATIONAL PARK SERVICE DENVER SERVICE CENTER CONTRACTING SERVICES 1 DENVER FEDERAL CENTER, BUILDING 50 P.O. BOX 25287 DENVER, COLORADO 80225-0287 File Code: A16 Sole Source Justification Park/PMIS NAMA 291052 PR Number TBD Date: March 31, 2026 Reference: Construction Services, NAMA 291052 Pool Lining Subject: Sole Source Justification Other than Full and Open Competition In accordance with FAR 6.103-2, the following information is provided:

1. Identification of the Agency and the Contracting Activity:

Department of the Interior (DOI), National Park Service (NPS), Denver Service Center (DSC), Contracting Services (CS) Division on behalf of DOI NPS DSC, Design and Construction (D&C) Division.

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved:

This action is for the award of a firm-fixed-price construction contract to perform concrete surface repairs and install a high-performance, fully submersible, waterproof, anti-microbial, and anti-algae polyurea coating system at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. The work includes surface preparation, crack and joint repair, and installation of a multi-component Rhino Linings coating system consisting of Rhino CCW Polyurea, Rhino 11-35 Polyurea, Rhino 406 Epoxy Primer, and Rhino Pipeliner 5000, in accordance with the revised Statement of Work.

3. A Description of the Supplies or Services Required to Meet the Agency’s Needs, Including the Estimated Value:

The work includes the following:

• Shot blasting the pool floor to ICRI CSP 3–5 and sandblasting vertical surfaces and joints • Crack repair using manufacturer-approved sealants • Complete joint removal, cleaning, backer rod installation, and refilling with Rhino CCW Polyurea • Application of Rhino 11-35 Polyurea as the joint cap/elastic layer • Application of Rhino 406 Epoxy Primer at ~5 mils DFT • Installation of Rhino Pipeliner 5000 polyurea system to a final thickness of 100 mils ± • Sealing of the horizontal coping joint using manufacturer-approved sealants • Thickness verification, adhesion testing, and spark (holiday) testing • Mobilization from April 1–3, in-pool work beginning April 6, and substantial completion by May 22 These services are required to produce a seamless, monolithic, waterproof, antimicrobial, and anti-algae system suitable for continuous submersion.

These services are essential to restore structural durability, prevent microbial growth, ensure public-safe conditions, and maintain the integrity and appearance of a nationally significant landmark.

The IGE for this project is $10,256,576, based on historical coating-system costs, labor and material pricing for similar structural-concrete repairs, market pricing for Rhino Linings polyurea and associated system components.

JOFOC Over SAT

4. Identification of the Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition:

FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency. This authority applies when the Government’s need is of such an unusual and compelling nature that delays in award would seriously injure the Government.

FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency, applies because delaying the award long enough to conduct a competitive procurement would prevent the National Park Service from completing the work in time to reopen the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool for the Nation’s 250th anniversary event series. This delay would result in serious injury to the Government, including failure to meet statutory visitor-safety responsibilities and operational commitments for the 250th.

A competitive acquisition would introduce an unavoidable 10–15-week delay for solicitation, proposal development, evaluation, and award. Such delay would push the start of construction beyond the narrow spring environmental window required for concrete curing and multi-stage coating installation. Missing this window would mean the Reflecting Pool could not be refilled and made operational for the 250th anniversary, which constitutes mission failure and exposes the Government to public-safety, resource-protection, and event-support risks.

The technical process (concrete repairs, cure cycles, pretreatment chemistry, and coating installation) can only be executed within strict temperature and humidity conditions. Any shift in schedule pushes these phases into weather conditions where the system cannot cure performance requirements, making delays unacceptable. Thus, fully competing the requirement would directly prevent the Government from executing essential operations tied to a major national commemoration, satisfying the GAO-recognized standard for “unusual and compelling urgency.” Delaying award to conduct a full and open competition would cause serious injury to the Government, as defined under FAR 6.103-2. If Government were required to conduct a traditional competitive procurement cycle estimated at 10-15 weeks the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool would not be able to reopen in time to meet the NPS’s affirmative operational obligations for the 250th anniversary commemoration.

The Reflecting Pool is a central feature of the National Mall’s visitor experience and is an essential component in NPS’s planned programming and crowd-management posture for the 250th. Failure to complete the concrete repairs and coating installation before the required curing window closes would result in the Pool remaining drained or partially inoperable during the event period. This outcome constitutes mission failure, as the NPS has explicit responsibilities for public safety, resource protection, and visitor services tied to the 250th.

The technical nature of the repairs requires strict environmental conditions and multistage curing cycles that can only occur within the narrow spring installation window. Thus, competition would directly prevent the Government from meeting a mandated, time-certain mission requirement.

5. Minimum Quantity and Why the full scope is Urgent.

The NPS evaluated whether the requirement could be divided into urgent and non-urgent components and whether a partial award could satisfy only the minimum quantity necessary to meet the immediate need.

This analysis concluded that the entire project scope is inherently urgent for the following reasons. The Rhino Linings polyurea system is an integrated, monolithic waterproofing assembly requiring continuous sequencing from joint repair through primer and polyurea installation. Phasing or partial execution is not technically feasible, would compromise adhesion and system integrity, and would void the manufacturer’s warranty. All work elements—surface preparation, crack repair, joint treatment, primer, and polyurea application—are interdependent. The environmental window for installation is limited, and dividing work would require re-staging, repeated shutdowns, and additional weather exposure, which would risk system failure and prevent timely reopening for the 250th anniversary.

Based on this evaluation, limiting the award to a minimum subset of work would fail to achieve the Government’s urgent need and would still result in operational failure during the 250th anniversary. Therefore, the full scope constitutes the minimum quantity necessary to meet the urgent mission requirement.

JOFOC Over SAT

6. A Demonstration that the Proposed Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or the Nature of the Acquisition Requires Use of the Authority Cited. The NPS intends to award this contract to Atlantic Industrial Coating Limited Liability Company.

The contractor’s unique qualifications include: The work requires a contractor with demonstrated experience installing Rhino Linings multi-component polyurea systems, including joint fillers, elastic joint-cap membranes, epoxy primers, and high-build (100 mil ±) polyurea waterproofing applied using heated plural-component spray equipment. The installation requires precise sequencing, temperature-controlled plural-component application, and validated capability to achieve uniform monolithic thickness without holidays, pinholes, or adhesion failures. The contractor must demonstrate the ability to perform all surface preparation, joint treatment, polyurea application, and quality-control testing required by the manufacturer for warranty compliance. Immediate mobilization capability is necessary to meet the compressed installation schedule and environmental curing requirements. The Government determined these qualifications are essential, not merely beneficial, because improper installation of any single material system results in delamination, blistering, discoloration, microbial growth, or premature failure — all of which compromise public safety and the operational readiness of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

7. A Description of Efforts Made to Ensure that Offers are Solicited from as Many Potential Sources as is Practicable, Including Whether a Notice Was or Will be Publicized as Required by FAR 5.2 and, if Not, Which Exception Under FAR 5.202 Applies: While multiple contractors may perform general concrete repair, the revised SOW requires specialized experience with thick-build polyurea systems, manufacturer-approved materials, and heated plural-component application equipment. Only a limited pool of contractors possess the qualifications and equipment necessary to install Rhino CCW Polyurea, Rhino 11-35 Polyurea, Rhino 406 Epoxy Primer, and Rhino Pipeliner 5000 as a unified system. Furthermore, the schedule constraints and strict environmental window preclude a competitive procurement cycle, as any delay would prevent project completion before May 22. Why a Competitive Cycle Cannot Meet the Timeline: 4–6 weeks for solicitation preparation and posting 3–4 weeks for proposal development 2–3 weeks for evaluation and award 1–2 weeks for GC subcontract solicitation, evaluation, and award to the system manufacturer Thus, a competitive procurement is incompatible with the critical path dictated by long-lead system fabrication.

8. A Determination by the Contracting Officer that the Anticipated Cost to the Government Will be Fair and Reasonable: The Contracting Officer has determined pricing to be fair and reasonable based on historical pricing for comparable systems, proprietary manufacturer pricing, and market research in accordance with FAR 15.401. Pricing will be evaluated by the Contracting Officer using: • Historical pricing for similar coating and repair work • Comparison with prior NPS and DOI awards of similar complexity • Market research of proprietary manufacturer pricing

9. A Description of the Market Research Conducted and the Results or a Statement of the Reason Market Research Was Not Conducted:

Market research indicates that although multiple firms perform concrete preparation and repair, only a subset possesses the equipment, manufacturer affiliation, and demonstrated experience in installing multi-component JOF0C Over SAT polyurea waterproofing systems such as Rhino Pipeliner 5000. Due to the schedule constraints and required specialized material performance, full and open competition remains impracticable.

10. Any Other Facts Supporting the Use of Other than Full and Open Competition:

Future acquisitions will benefit from early planning to allow time for complete competition cycles and expanded market engagement ahead of fixed public-event deadlines.

While multiple firms expressed interest during market research, the NPS determined that pursuing competition under the available timeline would itself prevent the NPS from meeting its mission obligations during the 250th anniversary. GAO case law requires agencies to demonstrate how delay not priority status causes injury. Here, the consequences of delay are concrete, time-bound, and unavoidable.

Competing the requirement introduces a minimum 10–15 week delay, which would: push the start of work beyond acceptable environmental conditions for concrete curing; prevent the NPS from restoring the Pool to operational status before the 250th activities commence; and create public-safety and resource-protection risks associated with an empty or partially repaired Pool during a major national event.

11. A Listing of the Sources, if any, that Expressed in Writing, an Interest in the Acquisition:

Multiple contractors expressed interest in the project, however due to the time constraints listed in above a competitive acquisition is not the best route for the Government.

12. A Statement of the Actions, if any, the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome any Barriers to Competition Before any Subsequent Acquisition for the Supplies or Services Required:

Earlier project planning will ensure future procurements allow adequate time for full GC competition and subcontractor system sourcing.

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION SECTION 1: IDENTIFICATION OF THE AGENCY AND THE CONTRACTING ACTIVITY

Department of State Contracting Activity ☐ Office of Acquisitions Management ☐ Foreign Service Institute ☐ Office of Foreign Missions ☐ U.S. Mission to the United Nations ☒ Overseas Post U.S. Embassy Rome, Italy Requiring Activity U.S. Embassy in Rome – GSO

SECTION 2: NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING APPROVED

Approval is requested to solicit and award, on a sole-source basis, an IDIQ contract to Queen Limousine for transportation services with drivers in support of a senior high-level USG VIP visit to Italy, as described in Section 3, on behalf of the Requiring Activity.

The authority to act under this Class Justification and Approval (J&A) expires on February 28, 2026.

This action will result in a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract.

SECTION 3: DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY'S NEEDS

The Embassy requires transportation services with drivers to support a Senior high-level USG VIP visit in connection with the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympic Games.

Services Estimated Quantity Estimated Period of Performance Transportation Services with Drivers 190 Vehicles 20 January – 15 February The estimated value for the entire period of performance is estimated at $7,584,597.43.

Task orders will be issued as required to meet operational needs and security requirements.

The contractor shall provide high-quality vehicles and drivers and operate with established, robust internal processes for financial management, quality assurance, and operational oversight to ensure all aspects of contract execution are properly monitored and controlled.

SECTION 4: IDENTIFICATION OF THE STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION

This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 41 USC 3304, as implemented by FAR 6.3 and substantiated by the following:

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE ☒ FAR 6.103-2 – Unusual and compelling urgency.

SECTION 5: DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED

The contractor’s unique qualifications and expertise are essential due to the scale and complexity of the event, the specific requirements to be met, and the contractor’s demonstrated experience and capacity to manage such services effectively.

This assessment is further supported by the last-minute notification of VIP travel, the stringent security and operational standards to be met, and the overall critical nature of the required services, which creates an unusual and compelling urgency.

These unique senior high-level USG VIP travel requirements result in only a single, or a very limited number of, responsible sources capable of providing the required level of operational support. The proposed contractor can meet these requirements due to a strong record of past performance on similar projects.

SECTION 6. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS WERE SOLICITED FROM AS

MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE, INCLUDING WHETHER A NOTICE WAS OR

WILL BE PUBLICIZED AS REQUIRED BY FAR SUBPART 5.2 AND, IF NOT, WHICH EXCEPTION

UNDER FAR 5.202 APPLIES

A formal synopsis of the proposed procurement was not published on SAM.gov because this contract action is being made under the conditions described in FAR 6.103-2, which allows for exceptions due to unusual and compelling urgency. Market research identified a few other vendors; however, none demonstrated the experience or capacity to manage operational services of this scale.

SECTION 7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST TO THE GOVERNMENT IS FAIR AND REASONABLE

The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to the Government of the services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable based on: o Rates from prior similar events SECTION 8. DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED (SEE PART 10) AND THE

RESULTS OR A STATEMENT OF THE REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED

This event is attended by both official and unofficial representatives from around the world. Most services have already been secured, and costs increase significantly during this period, further limiting the number of vendors capable of meeting the Embassy’s transportation requirements.

The short notice, high demand, and security-sensitive nature of the requirement have limited the ability to conduct full and open market research.

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE SECTION 9. ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN

COMPETITION

The unique requirements associated with senior high-level USG VIP travel, combined with security considerations and the operational environment of the event, limit the Government’s ability to conduct a full and open competition.

The proposed contractor possesses unique qualifications that meet the Government’s security and logistical requirements. Any delay in the award may result in the unavailability of qualified transportation resources.

SECTION 10. LISTING OF THE SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED, IN WRITING, AN INTEREST

IN THE ACQUISITION

MTM Italia Srl expressed interest in providing these services. MTM Italia Srl does not, however, currently possess the experience required to support such a complex, high-profile assignment with stringent security and logistical standards.

Furthermore, due to the urgency of the requirement and the limited time available before the event, there is insufficient time to onboard and prepare a new contractor to meet the complex operational demands. Attempting to do so would pose significant risks to the successful execution of the event and could compromise both security and mission objectives.

SECTION 11. STATEMENT OF THE ACTIONS, IF ANY, THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO REMOVE OR

OVERCOME ANY BARRIERS TO COMPETITION BEFORE ANY SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITION FOR THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED

The Government recognizes the importance of fostering full and open competition for future acquisitions of similar services. The unique operational environment connected with the event, characterized by extreme demand, early block allocation, and security-driven constraints, has significantly limited the Government’ s ability to conduct meaningful competition in the immediate term.
