JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL

For Other Than Full and Open Competition FAR Part 6 Acquisition and Technology Transformation and NBIS Integrated Master Schedule

1. Agency and contracting activity: The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), Procurement Solutions (PRS) Directorate, is the procuring activity for this action. The PRS Directorate proposes to enter into a contract action on an other than full and open competition basis with KPMG, LLC, (CAGE Code 7QEG9) on behalf of DCSA Acquisition and Technology (AT). DCSA has an urgent requirement for contractor support to assist the AT Operating Component in its organizational transformation. This organizational transformation is foundational to establishing the optimized organizational structure, streamlined processes, and agile governance required to successfully execute the National Background Investigation Services (NBIS) critical path. This work is a direct prerequisite for ensuring the people and processes are in place to deliver on the urgent congressional mandate for the NBIS program.

2. Description of action being approved: This justification and approval authorizes and approves the use of other than full and open competition to issue a new, standalone, sole-source letter contract (also known as an undefinitized contract action or UCA) to KPMG. This action is for non-commercial services with an estimated value of. The contract type will be determined during the definitization period. DCSA Working Capital Funds will be used. DCSA has an urgent congressional mandate for the NBIS program. The urgency of initiating this organizational transformation is directly tied to the NBIS program's critical path and immutable deadlines. Delaying the effort to establish an optimized and agile AT operating component will create unacceptable schedule delays and cascade into a high risk of failure for the entire NBIS implementation. The use of a letter contract is essential to allow the contractor to start work immediately upon receipt of the letter contract. A fully functional organizational structure must be put in place without delay to support the complex demands of the NBIS schedule and prevent the kind of systemic programmatic breakdown described in Head of Contracting Authority (HCA) feedback. Waiting for a definitized contract would mean losing critical time and momentum, directly and negatively impacting DCSA's ability to meet its congressional mandate. This is not a divisible requirement that could be partially awarded or delayed without significant programmatic harm.

3. Description of Supplies/Services: DCSA requires immediate, expert services to complete two inextricably linked tasks: (1) the development of the NBIS Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) with a critical path and risk analysis, and (2) a comprehensive assessment of the NBIS parent organization (DCSA AT) to ensure it is optimally structured to manage the NBIS implementation and support the agency’s broader mission. These tasks must be performed concurrently, as the viability of the IMS is directly dependent on the capabilities of the organization executing J&A for AT Transformation it. Therefore, this represents a single, integrated requirement to ensure NBIS program succe ss. The total estimated value of this procurement is $4,000,000. This action is for expert advisory and assistance services to support the DCSA AT Operating Component's organizational transformation. These services are critical for the successful execution of the NBIS program. The work is divided into two primary phases over a seven-month period of performance: x Phase I (Assessment & Planning): The contractor shall assess AT's current processes, technologies, and performance metrics to develop a roadmap for creating a unified and agile organization. Key tasks include: o Lifecycle Optimization: Analyzing and streamlining the "buy, build, run" lifecycle for capability delivery. o Technology Assessment: Evaluating the current technology landscape and developing a 5-year technology plan and roadmap. o Performance Measurement: Establishing a framework to measure transformation success and developing a consolidated NBIS IMS with an identified critical path, to be delivered by no later than April 2, 2026. x Phase II (Implementation Planning Support): The contractor shall provide program management, technical expertise, and change management support to guide the implementation of the recommendations from Phase I. This includes developing project charters, designing new governance processes, and creating a change management and communications plan.

4. Authority cited: The statutory authority permitting Other Than Full & Open Competition for this action is 10 USC 3204(a)(2), as implemented by RFO 6.103-2, “Unusual and compelling urgency.” Specifically, RFO 6.103-2(b) provides that agencies may contract without providing for full and open competition when the agency’s need for the services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured, financially or otherwise, unless the agency is permitted to limit the number of sources from which it solicits bids or proposals. This authority is exercised in accordance with the principles of RFO 1.102(a)(1) to meet the agency’s mission efficiently and effectively first.

5. Reason for Authority Cited: This justification is based on an unusual and compelling urgency that materialized upon the Acting DCSA director’s testimony before the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (HOGR) in February 2026. This testimony established a new, nonnegotiable deadline of April 2026 for the delivery to HOGR of a comprehensive NBIS IMS, complete with a critical path and risk analysis. This timeline was not previously anticipated J&A for AT Transformation and has created a compressed and urgent timeframe for performance that precludes the use of full and open competition. A competitive action, which would require a minimum of 70 days in accordance with DCSA’s procurement administrative lead time, would make it impossible for DCSA to meet the April 2026 deadline to provide information to HOGR. This failure would constitute a significant injury to the Government, resulting in unacceptable programmatic and mission risks: 1) Reputational Damage and Loss of Credibility: Failure to meet this deadline would severely damage the agency’s credibility with Congress and other stakeholders in its management of the critical NBIS program. 2) Programmatic Disruption and High Probability of Failure: The NBIS IMS is the foundational document for the entire system deployment and ensure alignment with TW 2.0 IMS. A delay in its creation would cascade, jeopardizing the implementation timeline and DCSA’s ability to meet both its NBIS delivery timeline and its TW 2.0 delivery timeline. Additionally, the concurrent organizational assessment is necessary to ensure DCSA has the capability to execute the NBIS, IMS, and is not hampered by a potentially flawed and inefficient management structure. This introduces a high probability of compounding delays, significant cost overruns, and potential mission failure. 3) Mission Degradation: NBIS is the future of the Government’s personnel vetting enterprise. Delays in its delivery directly impact the Government’s ability to onboard, investigate, and adjudicate personnel. This creates a potential bottleneck that degrades national security and the readiness of the entire Federal workforce. KPMG is the only source that can perform this integrated requirement. Any other vendor, regardless of general experience with government programs, would need to undertake a significant discovery and data-gathering phase to replicate the knowledge KPMG already possesses. This knowledge is not merely documented; it is largely tacit, comprising the undocumented architectural decisions, stakeholder contexts, and risk trade-offs made during the Trusted Workforce (TW) 2.0 IMS development. This level of experiential knowledge is unobtainable through simple document transfer and would require any other vendor a prohibitive amount of time to reverse-engineer. KPMG's unique capability is twofold: 1) Deep Knowledge of the Required Work: Through their foundational role in authoring the TW 2.0 IMS under the Personnel Vetting (PV) Transformation Other Transaction Authority (OTA) agreement, KPMG possesses an unparalleled, granular understanding of the specific tasks, dependencies, and workflows the NBIS organization will be required to execute. This knowledge is the essential baseline for any credible organizational assessment. 2) Ability to Assess Structure Against Strategy: An organizational assessment is not a generic exercise. It is an analysis of an organization's fitness to execute a specific strategy. KPMG is performing under the PV Transformation OTA, as well as the Financial Management (FM) Transformation requirement. Because KPMG has the deepest understanding of DCSA's intertwined strategic plans (and the Integrated Master J&A for AT Transformation Schedules), they are uniquely positioned to evaluate how the current organizational structure enables or impedes that strategy. A different vendor would lack this critical context and would have to first learn the IMS from scratch before they could even begin to assess the organization, a delay the Government cannot afford. 3) Holistic and Efficient Solution: By utilizing KPMG for both components, DCSA eliminates the significant risk of communication gaps, data silos, and conflicting recommendations that would arise from using two separate vendors. The seamless integration of these two tasks under one provider is the only way to meet the urgent deadline with a coherent and actionable result. The scope of this proposed sole-source action is strictly limited to providing the integrated services necessary to (1) develop the NBIS IMS for the April 2026 deadline and (2) conduct a concurrent organizational assessment of the NBIS parent organization (DCSA AT). The total period of performance will not exceed seven months, sufficient only to address the immediate urgent requirement for the IMS while also completing the necessary, concurrent organizational assessment to ensure long-term program viability.

6. Efforts to Obtain Competition: This action is being conducted under the authority of RFO 6.103-2, "Unusual and compelling urgency," which permits limiting the number of sources solicited. As detailed in Section 5, the Government's urgent need to meet a deadline of early April 2026 for the NBIS IMS makes it impractical to solicit offers from any source other than KPMG, LLP. The extensive lead-time required for any other contractor to replicate KPMG's knowledge would result in unacceptable delays and guarantee failure to meet this critical deadline.

The Government's efforts to obtain competition are focused on the long-term. This solesource action is a tactical, short-term mechanism designed to address the immediate crisis while simultaneously creating the conditions for future competition. The deliverables from this contract, specifically the AT Lifecycle Improvement Plan and Technology Roadmap, are critical drivers for this contract strategy. These documents will codify and define the organizational processes and technical requirements currently understood only by KPMG. By formally documenting these structures, the Government will significantly lower the barrier to entry for potential competitors in future related acquisitions, as the "discovery phase" that only KPMG will have completed will be substantially reduced.

While market research did identify other potential sources capable of providing general management and transformation consulting based on NAICS 541611, these firms do not possess the unique capabilities of KPMG as mentioned in paragraph 5.

As this action is being conducted under the authority of RFO 6.103-2, the requirement for a pre-award synopsis of the proposed contract action at FAR 5.201 is waived in accordance with the exception at FAR 5.202(a)(2). Publicizing a notice of intent and waiting for responses would prevent the agency from meeting its critical mission requirements.

J&A for AT Transformation However, in accordance with FAR 5.301, a notice of the final contract award will be publis hed on the Government Point of Entry (sam.gov), and the approved Justification and Approval document will be posted with the award notice.

7. Market research: Pursuant to FAR Part 10, market research was conducted to identify sources capable of providing the required services on this compressed timeline. The research included the following methods:

1. Review of Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs): A comprehensive search was performed using the GSA eLibrary and GSA Advantage to identify vendors on the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) and the OASIS+ contract vehicle.

2. Industry Analysis: A review of the competitive landscape for federal professional services was conducted to identify leading contractors with demonstrated expertise in large-scale organizational transformation for federal agencies.

3. Review of Agency's Existing Contract Portfolio: An internal review was conducted to understand the current landscape of transformation and advisory service contracts within the agency to identify potential synergies and risks.

B. List of potential capable vendors discovered during market research:

Although there are other vendors who perform work within NAICS code 541611, none of these firms would be able to meet the Government’s schedule except for KPMG, given their unique capabilities mentioned in paragraph 5.

8. Other Facts: a) Procurement History: This requirement is similar to at least two other major, ongoing "transformation" type contracts within DCSA for which KPMG, LLP, is the incumbent prime contractor. This proposed action is a new, standalone contract for Acquisition and Technology to address an urgent and unforeseen requirement that is outside the scope of existing contracts but critically dependent on the knowledge gained from them. b) Subcontracting Competition: As KPMG, LLP, is an Other than Small Business, the Government will request a small business subcontracting plan.

Justification and Approval (J&A) for Other Than Full and Open Competition

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION

(See "Specific Guidance for Completing this Template" after item XII below.) I. Agency and Contracting Activity. Department of the Air Force (DAF) United States Space Force (USSF) Combat Forces Command (CFC) Space Acquisition & Integration Office (SAIO) 135 Dover St. Ste. 2225, Peterson SFB, CO 80914 II. Nature and/or description of the action being approved. U.S. Space Command (USSPACECOM) has an urgent need for a new contract in support of the basing decision and move of HQ USSPACECOM to Redstone Arsenal (RSA). At the direction of the United States Secretary of War (SECWAR), USSPACECOM is ordered to establish 50% of the command on RSA by October 2028, with construction of the permanent Command and Control Facility beginning in 2027. To accomplish this, the newly established USSPACECOM Redstone Transition Team (RTT) requires a dedicated Program Management Office (PMO.)

To meet the SECWAR direction and the USSPACECOM RTT planning objectives, a new contract is needed as soon as possible. The contract will be a Firm-Fixed-Price, commercial services contract under FAR 6.302-2 10 USC 3204(a)(2), Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs. US Space Command (USSPACECOM) RTT Program Management Office (PMO) manages the design, construction, and mission equipment integration for the USSPACECOM Command & Control Facility (C2F), as well as the transition-to-occupancy. The design and construction planning and project execution responsibilities include the integration of all USSPACECOM requirements, which also consists of information technology (IT) and security components. As the USSPACECOM Command & Control Facility (C2F) Requirements Owner, the RTT PMO requires this support to assist in establishing technical and engineering expertise to successfully accomplish assigned tasks.

This is a requirement for performance-based services with a 12-month period with an estimated period of performance of 23 February 2026 through 22 February 2027. It covers various Advisory and Assistance Services (A&AS) within the RTT PMO to support planning, design, construction, and transition to occupancy for the C2F.

This requirement is for A&AS support and falls under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 541330 - Engineering Services.

The anticipated contract line items (CLINs) and the corresponding line item type are as follows: Labor: Firm Fixed Price Travel: Firm Fixed Price Other Direct Costs: Firm Fixed Price Contract Access Fee: Firm Fixed Price Estimated cost for the one year period of performance is. The estimated cost was determined by using a bottom up cost estimating technique and researching labor category fully burdened rates for the Huntsville, AL area.

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION

The Procuring Contracting Officer and USSPACECOM have determined this to be a commercially available service.

The CLIN structure will not include separately-priced CLINs for intellectual property (IP) and IP rights.

IV. Demonstration that the contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited above. In order to successfully meet the urgent need to support the RTT PMO, a direct award to DEFTEC Corporation, a small business, has been determined to be the appropriate course of action. USSPACECOM J4 has a contract of similar scope that was competitively awarded to DEFTEC. This contract is currently in its first option period and performance is determined to be satisfactory or higher in all areas. There is significant risk of mission impact and subsequent military readiness if additional delays are incurred by engaging in further market research or issuing requests for information to broader industry. In this case, since a high performing company is performing like requirements, and was selected through a competitive process, additional market research would not result in substantive differences that outweigh the mission impact.

V. Description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under FAR 5.202 applies. The Government's market research indicates that while there are multiple companies that could perform this work, competition should not be pursued at this time. Competition would introduce unacceptable risk in performance delays due to the need for a transition/phase-in period for the contractor to get acclimated and would not make good business sense for a short-term contract solution. This acquisition will not require a Pre-solicitation Notice IAW FAR 5.1 or a Solicitation Notice IAW FAR 5.2 due to the use of other than full and open competition exception FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency. VI. Determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable. The Procuring Contracting Officer has historical cost and price data for multiple A&AS awards with many of the same or similar labor categories and levels, which will be utilized with proposal analysis techniques under FAR 15.404-1 to determine fair and reasonable pricing. Additionally, analysis of certified cost or pricing data through comparison with historical pricing, evaluation of direct labor rates, and trend analysis will also be conducted to determine the price as realistic and fair and reasonable. The contracting officer will utilize all of the above to analyze the contractor's proposed prices for the 12-month award so that the proposed contract price can be determined to be fair and reasonable. VII. Description of the market research conducted and the results, or a statement of the reasons market research was not conducted. Market research consisted of searches on GSA and in the public marketplace as well as an examination of recent acquisition history for like requirements. Additionally, USSPACECOM J4 has a contract of similar scope that was competitively awarded to DEFTEC. This contract is currently in its first option period and performance is determined to be satisfactory or higher in all areas. VIII. Any other facts supporting the use of Other Than Full and Open Competition. Due to the directives by SECWAR to move as quickly as possible to complete the HQ USSPACECOM transition to RSA, many avenues and novel approaches to completing MILCON are being considered. Depending on the specific approach that is implemented over the next 6-9 months, the end requirements to support the PMO could be drastically different. This would make competitively awarding this contract at this point substantially higher risk of not being able to support the ultimate needs of the PMO.

Given the urgent need to establish the USSPACECOM headquarters at Redstone Arsenal to meet strategic national security objectives, a sole-source award is the only viable option. The DEFTEC's qualifications and experience in the defense ecosystem are essential to support the command's transition team and fulfill the leadership's directive for an expedited and seamless relocation. Any other course of action would result in unacceptable delays, increased costs, and a potential degradation of mission readiness during a critical time for our nation's defense in the space domain. Simplified Procedures for Commercial Products and Services

41 U.S.C. 1901

1. Agency and Contracting Activity. The U.S. Secret Service (USSS), Office of Procurement, proposes to enter into a sole source contract using simplified acquisition procedures (SAP) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 12.201-1 (FAR Class Deviation 2521) and 41 U.S.C. 1901.

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.

(a) Nature of action. The United States Secret Service (USSS) intends to procure on a sole source basis due to an urgent need for engineering support services for its Counter-Unmanned Aerial Systems (C-UAS) program. This contract action will provide immediate, mission-critical support to address rapidly emerging unmanned aerial threats and ensure the continuity of protective operations. The effort will include system integration, technical support, and operational enhancements to the existing C-UAS environment. This procurement based on urgency is necessary to avoid unacceptable delays and mitigate risks to personnel and protectees during this critical period.

12.5.2025 v.1.0 Justification and Approval (J&A) when using Simplified Acquisition Procedures for Commercial Products and Services Procurements exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), but less than $9M pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1901, including Brand Name The USSS is responsible for protecting high-profile government officials and designated protectees against a range of evolving threats. In recent years, the proliferation of unmanned aerial systems (UAS) has introduced new risks to secure environments and protective operations. To counter these threats, USSS has implemented a specialized C-UAS program, which requires ongoing engineering support to maintain, enhance, and rapidly adapt system capabilities. The current requirement arises from rapidly emerging UAS-related threats and the urgent need to ensure the effectiveness and readiness of C-UAS assets in support of critical mission objectives.

3. Description of Supplies/Services.

The requirement is to acquire urgent engineering support services for the USSS’ C-UAS program. The objectives of this contract are to: • Ensure C-UAS systems operate securely, effectively, and reliably across a wide range of complex and dynamic operational environments, addressing emerging threats while maintaining compliance with stringent cybersecurity and National Security System (NSS) standards. • Enhance system integration and validation practices through rigorous testing, evaluation, and continuous improvement methodologies to guarantee seamless interoperability and mission readiness. • Leverage advanced analytics and data-driven insights to continuously assess mission and system performance, identify operational gaps, and inform decision-making processes for capability enhancements. • Maintain transparency, accountability, and strategic alignment through disciplined program management, comprehensive risk oversight, and proactive stakeholder engagement, ensuring contract activities remain mission-focused, cost-effective, and responsive to Government priorities.

4. Identification of the authority.

41 U.S.C. 1901, using SAP up to $9M as authorized and implemented by FAR 12.102(b) (FAR Class Deviation 25-21).

5. Identification of Exception to the Buy American Statute. Not Applicable

6. Demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited.

12.5.2025 v.1.0 Justification and Approval (J&A) when using Simplified Acquisition Procedures for Commercial Products and Services Procurements exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), but less than $9M pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1901, including Brand Name (a) Circumstances for Not Using Full and Open Competition:

Urgency - An urgent and compelling need exists, and following the procedures to compete the requirement would result in unacceptable delays The urgency of this acquisition is driven by a rapidly evolving threat landscape and imminent operational demands. This is not the result of poor planning or oversight; it is a direct response to unpredictable, emergent threats that require immediate mitigation Routine competitive acquisition procedures would introduce significant delays, potentially compromising the effectiveness of protective operations during a period of heightened risk. The mission-critical nature of these services means any delay could result in reduced situational awareness, degraded operational effectiveness, and increased risk to personnel and protectees.

To ensure compliance with acquisition regulations, a competitive contract is already planned and in progress for the larger, ongoing requirement. The effective period of this urgent sole source award will be strictly limited to the minimum time necessary to transition to a competed contract, with clear milestones in place to facilitate timely and fair competition for future support. Awarding this urgent procurement to Assured Momentum will enable a structured and effective transition period, allowing for critical knowledge transfer to the competitively awarded vendor. This approach ensures continuity of operations, minimizes disruptions, and preserves mission effectiveness, supporting a seamless handover of responsibilities in support of USSS protective operations.

(b) Events Leading to the Situation and Segregation for Competition:

(c) Alternatives Considered and Why They Will Not Work:

Alternatives, including competing the requirement among other vendors, were considered and rejected. These options would necessitate extensive onboarding, training, and integration efforts, resulting in unacceptable delays and operational risks. Vendors without prior, direct experience with the USSS C-UAS system lack the system-specific expertise necessary for immediate and effective support during this critical period.

(d) Impact to the Mission if the J&A Is Not Approved:

Failure to approve this J&A and procure the required urgent services from Assured Momentum will result in a significant and immediate degradation of C-UAS operational effectiveness. This would reduce situational awareness, increase risk to personnel and protectees, and potentially result in mission failure ██████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████ ████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████ (e) Nonavailability Exception to the Buy American Statute:

This requirement does not invoke the nonavailability exception to the Buy American statute.

United States Department of the Interior NATIONAL PARK SERVICE DENVER SERVICE CENTER CONTRACTING SERVICES 1 DENVER FEDERAL CENTER, BUILDING 50 P.O. BOX 25287 DENVER, COLORADO 80225-0287 File Code: A16 Sole Source Justification Park/PMIS NAMA 291052 PR Number TBD Date: March 31, 2026 Reference: Construction Services, NAMA 291052 Nano Bubble Subject: Sole Source Justification Other than Full and Open Competition In accordance with FAR 6.103-2, the following information is provided:

1. Identification of the Agency and the Contracting Activity:

Department of the Interior (DOI), National Park Service (NPS), Denver Service Center (DSC), Contracting Services (CS) Division on behalf of DOI NPS DSC, Design and Construction (D&C) Division.

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved: This action covers the procurement and installation of a fully integrated Nano Bubble Filtration System designed to replace the existing, failing filtration infrastructure at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. The system uses nanobubble ozone infusion technology to improve water quality by reducing bacteria, pathogens, algae, and organic contaminants.

The acquisition is required on an urgent basis because the existing system is no longer meeting operational requirements and the Reflecting Pool must be treated and operational prior to major scheduled public events.

3. A Description of the Supplies or Services Required to Meet the Agency’s Needs, Including the Estimated Value: The required system consists of:

• Onsite generation of oxygen and ozone • Patented nanobubble infusion technology • Pumps, valves, piping, fittings, controls, safety sensors • Electrical components (transformers, panels, cabling, conduit) • HVAC units for system housing • Structural frames and insulated connections • Installation, testing, startup, and commissioning The system is engineered to distribute ozone-filled nanobubbles throughout the entire water column with long residence time and high oxidative efficiency, validated by NOAA, Ohio State University, and the University of Florida.

The Independent Government Estimate (IGE) for the Nano Bubble portion is $1,808,352.

4. Identification of the Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition:

FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency. This authority applies when the Government’s need is of such an unusual and compelling nature that delays in award would seriously injure the Government.

FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency, applies because delaying the award long enough to conduct a competitive procurement would prevent the National Park Service from completing the work in time to reopen the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool for the Nation’s 250th anniversary event series. This delay would result in serious injury to the Government, including failure to meet statutory visitor-safety responsibilities and operational commitments for the 250th.

A competitive acquisition would introduce an unavoidable 10–15-week delay for solicitation, proposal development, evaluation, and award. Missing this window would mean the Reflecting Pool could not be refilled and made operational for the 250th anniversary, which constitutes mission failure and exposes the Government to public-safety, resource-protection, and event-support risks.

This acquisition fulfills the immediate need to restore water-quality performance and the extended fabrication and delivery lead times associated with the Nano Bubble Filtration System.

The Reflecting Pool is a central feature of the National Mall’s visitor experience and is an essential component in NPS’s planned programming and crowd-management posture for the 250th. Failure to complete the concrete repairs and coating installation before the required curing window closes would result in the Pool remaining drained or partially inoperable during the event period. This outcome constitutes mission failure, as the NPS has explicit responsibilities for public safety, resource protection, and visitor services tied to the 250th.

5. Minimum Quantity and Why the full scope is Urgent.

The agency evaluated whether the requirement for the Nano Bubble Filtration System could be divided into urgent and non-urgent components or procured in partial phases. This analysis concluded that the entire system constitutes the minimum quantity necessary to meet the urgent water-quality and operational needs of the Reflecting Pool.

The Nano Bubble Ozone Technology (NBOT) relies on a fully integrated, interdependent system that includes oxygen generation, ozone generation, nanobubble infusion equipment, pumps, controls, electrical distribution components, structural mounting, HVAC units, heat tracing, piping, valves, and safety sensors. These elements must operate together as a complete assembly to achieve the required treatment performance. Partial procurement or staged installation would not allow the system to function or produce the expected reductions in bacteria, algae, pathogens, and organic contaminants.

Additionally, the existing filtration system is no longer capable of meeting operational or water-quality performance standards, and the Reflecting Pool requires immediate treatment to ensure acceptable conditions and support upcoming public events. The Nano Bubble Filtration System has significant fabrication and delivery lead times, and any delay in obtaining the full system would jeopardize operational readiness.

Because the system cannot be divided into functional subcomponents, and because full installation is required to restore water-quality performance, the complete Nano Bubble system represents the minimum quantity necessary to meet the agency’s urgent mission requirements.

Based on this evaluation, limiting the award to a minimum subset of work would fail to achieve the Government’s urgent need and would still result in operational failure during the 250th anniversary. Therefore, the full scope constitutes the minimum quantity necessary to meet the urgent mission requirement.

6. A Demonstration that the Proposed Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or the Nature of the Acquisition Requires Use of the Authority Cited.

The NPS intends to award this contract to Greenwater Services.

The Nano Bubble system is a highly specialized and niche technology with limited domestic suppliers. The required configuration involves proprietary manufacturing methods and system-integration expertise unique to this technology. Procuring directly from the system manufacturer reduces lead times, mitigates delays related to subcontractor involvement, and minimizes cost escalation risks.

The Government determined these qualifications are essential, not merely beneficial, because improper installation of any single material system results in delamination, blistering, discoloration, microbial growth, or premature failure — all of which compromise public safety and the operational readiness of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

The requirement meets the standard for “unusual and compelling urgency” for the following reasons:

The existing filtration system is failing and cannot maintain water quality, resulting in elevated levels of bacteria and algae.

The Reflecting Pool is a core operational, visitor-service, and ceremonial feature of the National Mall and must be operational for the Nation’s 250th anniversary events.

Delaying award to conduct a competitive procurement would introduce unavoidable 10–15 week delays for solicitation development, proposal preparation, evaluation, and award.

Such delays would push installation beyond the permissible environmental window and prevent the Pool from being refilled in time, resulting in mission failure.

The Nano Bubble system has long fabrication and delivery lead times, requiring immediate authorization to proceed.

7. A Description of Efforts Made to Ensure that Offers are Solicited from as Many Potential Sources as is Practicable, Including Whether a Notice Was or Will be Publicized as Required by FAR 5.2 and, if Not, Which Exception Under FAR 5.202 Applies:

The required system relies on specialized nanobubble ozone generation technology that is not commercially available from general water-treatment suppliers. Only systems using this specific technology can achieve the identified performance outcomes, including deep-column oxidant penetration, long ozone residency, and the ability to reduce bacteria, algae, and organic contaminants without chemicals. The unique engineering requirements and proprietary design restrict available sources.

Why a Competitive Cycle Cannot Meet the Timeline: 4–6 weeks for solicitation preparation and posting 3–4 weeks for proposal development 2–3 weeks for evaluation and award 1–2 weeks for GC subcontract solicitation, evaluation, and award to the system manufacturer Thus, a competitive procurement is incompatible with the critical path dictated by long-lead system fabrication.

8. A Determination by the Contracting Officer that the Anticipated Cost to the Government Will be Fair and Reasonable:

The Contracting Officer has determined pricing to be fair and reasonable based on historical pricing for comparable systems, proprietary manufacturer pricing, and market research in accordance with FAR 15.401.

Pricing will be evaluated by the Contracting Officer using: • Comparison with prior NPS and DOI awards of similar complexity • Market research of proprietary manufacturer pricing • Comparable water treatment systems • Ozone and oxygen generation technology

9. A Description of the Market Research Conducted and the Results or a Statement of the Reason Market Research Was Not Conducted:

Market research determined that while various water-quality mitigation methods exist—including chemical treatment, aeration, and standard ozone systems—none provide the extended ozone half-life, full-column distribution, or oxidant persistence achieved through nanobubble infusion. Third-party validation by NOAA, The Ohio State University, and the University of Florida confirms the system’s ability to significantly reduce algae, bacteria, pathogens, and organic contaminants without residue or ecological risk.

10. Any Other Facts Supporting the Use of Other than Full and Open Competition:

Future acquisitions will benefit from early planning to allow time for complete competition cycles and expanded market engagement ahead of fixed public-event deadlines.

While multiple firms expressed interest during market research, the NPS determined that pursuing competition under the available timeline would itself prevent the NPS from meeting its mission obligations during the 250th anniversary. GAO case law requires agencies to demonstrate how delay not priority status causes injury. Here, the consequences of delay are concrete, time-bound, and unavoidable.

The Reflecting Pool has persistent water-quality challenges driven by environmental exposure, wildlife activity, and organic loading. The nanobubble system improves clarity, odor, water quality, and dissolved oxygen while reducing ecological impacts. It also supports the operational need for reliable conditions before significant upcoming public events. Long fabrication lead times require procurement ahead of other activities to ensure availability.

Competing the requirement introduces a minimum 10–15 week delay, which would: •	delay the cleaning and replacement of the pool due to the failure of the old system •	prevent the NPS from restoring the Pool to operational status before the 250th activities commence; and •	create public-safety and resource-protection risks associated with an empty or partially repaired Pool during a major national event.

11. A Listing of the Sources, if any, that Expressed in Writing, an Interest in the Acquisition:

Multiple contractors expressed interest in the project, however due to the time constraints listed in above a competitive acquisition is not the best route for the Government.

12. A Statement of the Actions, if any, the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome any Barriers to Competition Before any Subsequent Acquisition for the Supplies or Services Required:

Earlier project planning will ensure future procurements allow adequate time for full GC competition and subcontractor system sourcing.

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL

Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition (FAR 6.3)

1. Contracting Agency and Activity. The Department of the Interior (DOI), United States Geological Survey (USGS), Earth Resources Observation and Science (EROS) Center.

2. Nature of Action Being Approved. This is a 6-month bridge contract to DCT, Incorporated for operations and maintenance services at EROS Center.

3. Description of Supplies or Services. The required service is for operation and maintenance of the physical facilities of the EROS Center in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Services include comprehensive Operation and Maintenance of all aspects of the 318-acre USGS-owned property, including a 300,000 sq. ft. building with three computer rooms, heating and air conditioning, boilers, electrical systems that convert, switch, and distribute the incoming 13kV power to proper and stable power of various levels to operate the multiple systems and IT assets valued at hundreds of millions of dollars. EROS operates and maintains two high performance computing systems (HPCs). The services also include operating and maintenance of a backup generating plant of 4-750KW generators for emergency power to maintain operations in case of commercial power loss, building automation, facility security systems, a wastewater treatment pond system, the phone private branch exchange (PBX), the physical network infrastructure, grounds upkeep and snow removal.

4. Estimated Dollar Value. $1,738,440.00

5. Statutory Authority. The proposed action may be awarded on a limited source basis under the authority of FAR 6.302-2

6. Rationale Supporting Use of Citation in No. 5. The bridge contract is necessary to allow DOI time to complete, advertise, and award the pending 5-year recompete contract for operations and maintenance. Due to the government shutdown and staff shortages caused by voluntary early retirement packages, the bid package was not completed prior to the contract period of performance end date. We have exhausted a 6-month contract extension and a 6-month emergency task order to extend these necessary services. EROS cannot operate without operations and maintenance services, and the complex nature of the work precludes an off-theshelf or in-house solution.

7. Other Information. 2

8. The Efforts to Identify Additional Sources Including the Market Research Conducted. The existing contract is within three (3) months of expiration. Given the extremely limited timeframe, this brief procurement affords the Government sufficient time to award a full and openly competed contract for the required services and allow for a requisite 30-day transition period. Contractors exist in the market that are able to meet the requirement however, the Government would be seriously injured and the mission adversely critically affected if competition is not limited. (IAW FAR 6.302-2).

9. Future Plans to Permit Competition. A competitively bid 5-year contract recompete is in progress. This bridge contract is needed only to ensure services do not lapse for the EROS Center. Due to the highly specialized skills and equipment needed to perform site operations and maintenance there are no federal staff properly trained to keep the Center operating in the event of a contract lapse. Additionally, at the current time, there are no federal staff properly trained to bring a new Contractor up to speed on the needed tasks.

10. Recommendation and Certification from Program Office Based on the above, I recommend this acquisition be conducted on the basis of other than full and open competition. U.S. GENERAL SERVICES ADMINISTRATION

Public Buildings Service Acquisition Project Delivery Contracting Division - East Legal Services for Roosevelt Hotel Project Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition

1. Agency and Contracting Activity (FAR 6.104-1(a)(1) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-202506)): The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service, proposes to enter into a contract for highly specialized, multi-disciplinary legal counsel for the possible renovation, operation, maintenance and redevelopment of the Roosevelt Hotel property in New York City.

2. Nature and Description of Action (FAR 6.104-1(a)(2) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-202506)): GSA must acquire the services of a premier, multi-disciplinary law firm with an elite track record in large-scale New York City real estate transactions, high-value hotel assets, and international sovereign negotiations. GSA has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with the Government of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan for the renovation, operation, maintenance and redevelopment of the Roosevelt Hotel at 45 East 45 Street in New York (the “Project”). The Memorandum is subject to a terminal expiration of 180 calendar days (August 2026), creating a “Time is of the Essence” window that leaves no margin for the administrative delays inherent in standard procurement cycles.

3. Description of Services (FAR 6.104-1(a)(3) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06)): The required services include a complete panoply of legal services for a potentially high-value dollar transaction: ● Transactional Architecture & Equity Transfer: Executing the transfer of necessary equity or leasehold rights and interests from Pakistan to the United States or its designee. ● Forensic Due Diligence: Identifying encumbrances, reviewing title records, and providing formal opinions of title within the Midtown Manhattan market. ● Regulatory & Permit Navigation: Securing all necessary Federal, state, and local permits and approvals ● Compliance: Ensuring all actions accord with applicable laws, regulations, and the interplay between Federal Supremacy and local NYC zoning.

4. Identification of Statutory Authority (FAR 6.104-1(a)(4) (GSA Class Deviation RFO2025-06)): The statutory authority for this justification is 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2), as implemented by FAR 6.103-2 — Unusual and Compelling Urgency (GSA Class Deviation RFO2025-06). 2

5. Demonstration of the Proposed Contractor’s Unique Qualifications and Urgency (FAR 6.104-1 (a)(5) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06)): A. Unique Expertise and Knowledge The Roosevelt Hotel represents a distinct, high-value asset class at the epicenter of Manhattan’s Midtown East Subdistrict. Unlike standard commercial acquisitions, this project is inextricably linked to the Greater East Midtown Rezoning—a complex regulato ry framework involving floor area ratios and air rights transfers unique to the Grand Central Terminal vicinity. The proposed contractor must possess significant local expertise and understanding of the specific nuances of New York City land use controls, preservation rules, practices, and procedures. Furthermore, the Roosevelt Hotel’s current ownership structure and its role in bilateral diplomatic relations require counsel with sophistication to handle sovereign-adjacent negotiations. The project demands more than standard real estate law knowledge and expertise; it requires an interdisciplinary mastery of wide-ranging fields, including: ● Adaptive Reuse of Historic Landmarks: Addressing issues under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act. ● New York City-Specific Tax and Liability: Addressing unique local burdens, including the New York State Real Estate Transfer Tax and potential “mansion tax” implications, as these apply to a Federal acquisition from a foreign entity. ● Labor and Occupancy Nuances: Navigating the complex New York City hotel environment and the current “Special Occupancy” status of the building, which presents immediate operational hurdles that a firm without localized “knowledge capital” would be challenged to mitigate. B. Unusual and Compelling Urgency & Serious Injury Any perceived delay or lack of progress by GSA could impair the Project and negatively impact the United States’ multifaceted relationship with Pakistan. Absent the limitation on competition addressed herein, standard competitive procurement requirements would put the Government’s ability to execute the necessary work within the required timeframe at substantial risk. Failure to meet the 180-day window to cooperatively define the Project’s precise technical, economic, and commercial parameters would undermine U.S. credibility in critical areas. The urgency is therefore a matter of national strategic interest. The serious injury to the Government includes not only a possible degradation of the U.S. Pakistan strategic partnership but also a significant financial opportunity cost. Failure to execute a project within the 180-day window risks the loss of a high dollar asset repositioning in the world’s most competitive real estate market, potentially resulting in the loss of substantial revenue to the Federal Government. 3

6. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by FAR 5 and, if not, which exception under FAR part 5 applies (FAR 6.104-1 (a)(6) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06)). Due to the extreme urgency and the specialized nature of Manhattan real estate and sovereign equity transfers, a full and open solicitation and procurement is not feasible. The GSA Office of the General Counsel conducted targeted market research to identify a number of sources from which it solicited proposals from firms capable of meeting these extraordinary needs within the MOU’s 180-day timespan. Additionally, in order to ensure continuity of the complex services required, as well as alignment with evolving requirements, the resulting contract period of performance will be one year. For the reasons discussed above, entering into a separate contract for the required services using competitive procedures during this period would be infeasible. In accordance with FAR 5.101(b)(2) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06), t he Contracting Officer is not required to post a presolicitation notice to the Governmentwide Point of Entry GPE when using other than full and open competition (see 6.103), except for the authorities at 6.103-1 (only one responsible source) and 6.103-6 (national security). The Request for Quote (RFQ) was sent to three firms.

7. Dete rmination of Fair and Reasonable Cost (FAR 6.104-1 (a)(7) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06)): The Contracting Officer will ensure that costs are fair and reasonable, benchmarked against the elite New York City legal market, the most specialized and expensive in the nation. The Independent Government Cost Estimate is. The contracting officer will take the following steps to ensure that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable:

(1) A detailed cost analysis will be performed comparing the hourly rate quoted with an independent government cost estimate and comparative evaluation of all quotations. (2) Negotiations will be conducted as necessary to ensure that the final total price is fair and reasonable.

The signature of the Contracting Officer provided below represents a determination that the anticipated cost to the Government will be considered fair and reasonable.

4

8. A description of the market research conducted (see FAR Part 10) and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted (FAR 6.104-1 (a)(8) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06)): The GSA Multiple Award Schedule was reviewed under category 541110 for Professional Legal Services. The list of forty-five (45) contractors did not possess the capabilities for the highly specialized, multi-disciplinary legal counsel required for this Project. As outlined in paragraph 5 and 6, GSA conducted market research with a limited number of law firms determined capable of meeting complex services required within the Memorandum’s timespan. The constraint is not the lack of law firms in the market, but the complex and urgency of this Project’s requirements.

9. Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition (FAR 6.104-1 (a)(9) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06)): It is in the Government’s best interest to enter into a Labor-Hour contract as it provides the necessary flexibility to adjust the level of effort and specific task assignments. As the Project progresses and evolves, the task assignments and ancillary services will be more defined. A Labor Hour contract allows the Government to scale the awardee's involvement based on the actual needs of the project at any given time, optimizing resource allocation. As such, awarding the contract to a highly capable and qualified law firm with the required knowledge and expertise is integral to keeping the Project moving forward.

10. A listing of the sources, if any, that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition (FAR 6.104-1(a)(10) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06)).

Not applicable.

11. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services required (FAR 6.104-1(a)(11) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06)).

Applicable FAR regulations would be followed in subsequent acquisitions for similar services. The Government will continue to conduct thorough market research to gauge the marketplace capabilities for future requirements.

12. Contracting officer certification that the justification is accurate and complete to the best of the contracting officer’s knowledge and belief (FAR 6.104-1(a)(12) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-06)).

Con tracting Officer: I certify that the data supporting the recommended use of other than full and open competition is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief. 5 Sotheavy Khon Contracting Officer Branch E - Downstate NY Acquisition Project Delivery Contracting Division - East GSA Public Buildings Service ——— 1

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION

In accordance with FAR 6.302 or FAR 13.501(a), the proposed contractual action is pursuant to the statutory authority identified in paragraph 4. This template is required for actions over the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (unless the procurement is acquired as a limited source IAW FAR 8.405-6 or is an Exception to Fair Opportunity IAW FAR 16.505(b)(2)).

1. Agency and Contracting Activity (FAR 6.303-2(b)(1)). U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Reclamation, Lower Colorado Basin.

2. Nature/Description of Action (FAR 6.303-2(b)(2)). Approval is being requested for other than full and open competition for a firm-fixed price contract for parking and ticketing services at Hoover Dam.

3. Description of Supplies/Services (FAR 6.303-2(b)(3)). This is a service requirement for parking and ticketing services at Hoover Dam which includes all personnel, equipment, materials, supervision, and other items and services necessary to implement, manage, and operate an integrated on-site Ticket Sales and Reservations System for the Visitor Center admission, tour tickets and special events at Hoover Dam, as well as, for the Hoover Dam Parking Garage (HDPG), Fee Collection Point (FCP) and Parking Lot Number 9. The period of performance for this requirement is 6 months with an option in accordance with FAR 52.217-8, using FY 2026 funding. The estimated value of this procurement is

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition (FAR 6.3032(b)(4)). Authorit y FAR Cover age Application ܈41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(2) FAR 6.302-2 U nusual and compelling urgency

5. Demonstration of Contractor’s Unique Qualifications (FA R 6.303-2(b)(5)). This requirement is being solicited on a sole source basis in accordance with FAR 6.3022, Unusual and Compelling Urgency. The current performanc e period for these services will end on December 31, 2025, and the contract has already utilized the maximum sixmonth extension allowed under FAR 52.217-8. The requirement is to provide operations and management services to run the parking lot and tour ticketing at Hoover Dam. This project has been in the planning stages for the past year; however, unforeseen delays have significantly impacted the acquisition timeline. These delays include a late and incomplete requisition package from the customer, a Government shutdown, and staffing losses within both the program and contracting offices. The Delayed Resignation Program (DRP) further exacerbated the situation by causing unexpected staff departures and prohibiting rehiring, leaving both offices short-staffed and unable to maintain the acquisition schedule. Notably, the contracting office lost a Contracting Officer (CO) due to DRP, which increased the workload for the remaining CO and contributed to the delay in completing the competitive acquisition. The solicitation for the new competitive contract has been written and is currently undergoing acquisition review. However, considering the remaining acquisition steps — including required legal and policy reviews, corrections to solicitation documents, System for Award Management (SAM) posting, a site visit, vendor questions, solicitation amendments, source selection, negotiations, and pre-award reviews — it is not reasonable to expect that a new competitive contract will be in place by December 31, 2025. A lapse in service would result in the closure of the Hoover Dam parking garage, parking lots, and Visitor Center, including ceasing all public tours. This disruption would cause a significant financial loss to the Government and negatively impact public access, visitor experience, and operational continuity. Hoover Dam receives approximately 1 million visitors annually, averaging 2,700 to 3,000 visitors per day, depending on the season. Based on the mix of ticket types for the Dam, Powerplant, and Visitor Center tours, the estimated daily revenue from ticket sales is approximately. If services were interrupted during the anticipated six-month period required to complete the competitive acquisition, the estimated revenue loss would total approximately per month. To avoid this insurmountable financial loss and ensure uninterrupted public access and operations, the Government must pursue a short-term sole source bridge contract. Ticket sales at Hoover Dam contribute significantly to covering the operational and maintenance costs of the facility. Any disruption in these services would result in a loss of revenue, which would have a ripple effect on the overall operations and sustainability of Hoover Dam. The inability to collect fees and manage visitor access effectively is unacceptable and would not only negatively impact financial stability but also diminish the visitor experience and public trust. The proposed sole source contractor is Laz Parking LTD, LLC., located at 1 Financial PLZ, Hartford, CT 06103. Laz Parking has been the incumbent contractor for these services at Hoover Dam for five and a half years, with a record of satisfactory performance. During this contract period, Laz Parking has consistently demonstrated the unique capabilities, experience, and expertise required to perform the specialized services at the Hoover Dam Fee Collection Point, Visitor Center, and parking garage. Their familiarity with the operational environment, security protocols, and customer service expectations has ensured uninterrupted and high-quality service delivery. Laz Parking’s personnel are already trained and embedded in the operational structure of Hoover Dam, and their continued presence is critical to maintaining continuity of service. Transitioning to a new contractor at this time would require onboarding and training of new personnel, which would introduce significant risk of service disruption. Given the critical nature of these services and the high volume of public visitation at Hoover Dam, any delay or interruption would result in substantial financial loss and operational impact on the Government. Laz Parking’s proven ability to perform these services without interruption, combined with their institutional knowledge and operational readiness, makes them uniquely qualified to continue providing services under a short-term bridge contract. This bridge contract will allow sufficient time for the Government to complete the solicitation, evaluation, and award of the new five-year competitive contract. It is a temporary, risk-mitigation measure that ensures continuity of services while the Government completes the in-progress, competitive acquisition for a long-term solution.

6. Description of efforts made to maximize competition (FAR 6.303-2(b)(6)). Although this action is being conducted under the authority of FAR 6.302-2 due to unusual and compelling urgency, the Government remains committed to promoting competit ion to the maximum extent practicable. In this case, the urgent need to avoid a lapse in critical services precludes the ability to conduct full and open competition for the bridge contract. However, the Government is actively developing a competitive solicitation for a new five-year contract. Market research is underway to identify qualified sources, and the upcoming solicitation will be posted on SAM.gov to ensure broad visibility and access to all interested vendors. The bridge contract is a temporary measure to maintain continuity of operations while the competitive process is completed. The Government will not extend the bridge contract beyond the minimum time necessary to complete the competitive acquisition to demonstrate its intent to restore full and open competition as soon as practicable.

7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost (FAR 6.303-2(b)(7)). The Contracting Officer anticipates the cost for this sole source bridge contract will be fair and reasonable. This determination will be based on a comparison with historical pricing from the incumbent’s current and previous contracts for the same or similar services at the Hoover Dam Visitor Center. The incumbent, Laz Parking LTD, LLC, has been providing these services for the past five and a half years,. There will be no significant changes in the level of effort, service requirements, or performance locations during the bridge period. Given the short-term nature of the bridge contract and the urgent need to avoid a lapse in critical services, the Government will use FAR 15.404-1(b)(2)(ii) historical pricing as a comparison of the proposed prices in making a price reasonableness determination.

8. Description of Market Research Conducted (FAR 6.303-2(b)(8)). Due to the urgent nature of this requirement and the limited time available before the current contract expires on December 31, 2025, the scope of market research was necessarily constrained. However, the Government leveraged existing knowledge of the market gained through the administration of the current contract and prior procurements for similar services. The incumbent, Laz Parking LTD, LLC, has been performing these services for over five years with satisfactory results. Their continued performance has provided the Government with insight into the technical and operational requirements of the Hoover Dam site, including visitor flow management and revenue collection systems. While no formal Request for Information (RFI) or sources sought notice was issued for this bridge action, the Government is actively conducting market research in preparation for the upcoming full and open competition for the long-term requirement. This includes reviewing vendor capabilities, industry practices, and pricing data through platforms such as SAM.gov, GSA eLibrary, and FPDS. The bridge contract is a one-time, short-term solution to prevent a lapse in critical services. The Government remains committed to maximizing competition for the followon contract and will continue to engage with industry to identify qualified sources.

9. Any Other Supporting Facts (FAR 6.303-2(b)(9)). The Hoover Dam Visitor Center is a high-profile federal facility that serves thousands of visitors each week and generates significant revenue through parking and ticketing operations. The services provided under this contract are essential to maintaining public access, ensuring visitor safety, and supporting the operational integrity of the site. In addition, the statute that established the construction and management of Hoover Dam required allowing visitation after construction.

A lapse in these services would not only result in the closure of the Visitor Center and parking facilities but would also lead to substantial financial losses for the Government and negatively impact the public’s experience at a nationally significant landmark. Additionally, the unique security and logistical requirements of the Hoover Dam site make it impractical to onboard a new contractor under urgent conditions without risking operational disruption. The use of FAR 6.302-2 is appropriate and justified given the compelling urgency and the potential consequences of service interruption.

10. Listing of Interested Sources (FAR 6.303-2(b)(10)). Laz Parking LTD, LLC., located at 1 Financial PLZ, Hartford, CT 06103

11. Actions Taken to Remove Barriers to Competition (FAR 6.303-2(b)(11)). The Government is committed to promoting full and open competition and has taken steps to remove barriers that may have previously limited vendor participation. Although this bridge contract is being awarded under the authority of FAR 6.302-2 due to unusual and compelling urgency, it is a temporary measure to prevent a lapse in critical services. To support future competition, the Government is: x Developing a new competitive solicitation for a five-year contract that will be posted on SAM.gov to ensure broad visibility and access to all interested vendors. x Conducting market research to identify additional qualified sources capable of performing the required services. x Reviewing and updating the performance work statement (PWS) to ensure it is clear, current, and does not contain unnecessarily restrictive requirements. x Engaging with industry through informal outreach and planning for potential presolicitation notices to encourage vendor interest and feedback. These actions are intended to ensure that the follow-on contract is awarded through full and open competition, consistent with the Competition in Contracting Act (CICA) and the Government’s acquisition objectives.

Docusign Envelope ID: C92A1974-9DC1-4DFF-B82A-DCC2BB323D3C General Services Administration Public Buildings Service Acquisition Management Division Services Acquisition Branch (6P1QC) Contract 47PL0224D0002 Operations and Mechanical Maintenance Services Edith Green Wendell Wyatt Federal Building 1220 SW 3rd Avenue, Portland, OR Justification for Other than Full and Open Competition RFO FAR 6.103-2, GSA Agency Deviation RFO-2025-06, Unusual and Compelling Urgency Sole Source Bridge Contract to Maintain Continuity of Services Nature and/or description of the action being approved.

Contract 47PL0218D0011 was awarded to Northern Management Services by GSA PBS Region 10, with an effective date of July 1, 2018. This contract ended December 31, 2023 and, sole source contract 47PL0224D0002 was awarded to Northern Management Services. This sole source contract served as a bridge with a one-year period of performance, four one-month option periods, and a six month extension. The full period of performance for this contract was January 1, 2024 - October 31, 2025.

Late March, 2025, GSA PBS Region 6 took over the contracting functions from Region 10. Unsuccessful offer letters were sent by the new contracting team on March 21, 2025, and de-briefings were held March 31, 2025. TeamGOV, one of the unsuccessful quoters also filed a protest on March 31, 2025.

GSA PBS Region 6 prepared a response to this protest, but ultimately there was insufficient documentation to support the award decision and no remaining personnel to provide statements. In conjunction with the Office of General Council, Region 6 responded to the protest with corrective action and cancelled this award.

The anticipated consolidated contract is not in place and services will currently end altogether at the Edith Green Wendell Wyatt Federal Building on October 31, 2025.

The purpose behind this bridge contract will allow us time to award a consolidated Facilities Engineering contract, which would combine the Edith Green Wendell Wyatt building with other Portland area buildings under a single Facilities Engineering contract.

This justification is for an emergency, sole source bridge contract to provide Operations and Mechanical Maintenance services at the Edith Green Wendell Wyatt Federal Building, 1220 SW 3rd Avenue, Portland OR 97204 for a period of approximately 1-year, starting on November 1, Docusign Envelope ID: C92A1974-9DC1-4DFF-B82A-DCC2BB323D3C 2025, through October 31, 2026. This bridge contract will be a firm fixed-price, commercial item, performance-based contract, and will contain no additional option periods.

Description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency's needs (including the estimated value).

The General Services Administration (GSA) has determined there is a continued need for the provision of operation and mechanical maintenance services at the subject location, starting on November 1, 2025, through October 31, 2026.

The Contractor will continue to provide all administration, management, supervision, labor, materials, supplies, repair parts, tools and equipment; and must plan, schedule, coordinate, inspect and ensure effective and economical completion of all work and services specified for the operation, maintenance and repair of the building(s), equipment and related services, all equipment, electrical and mechanical systems, structures, architectural finishes, and utilities, located on, within, or beneath, this facility's interior and exterior extending to the legal property line at the Edith Green Wendell Wyatt Federal Building.

Period of Performance for Bridge Contract: November 1, 2025 through October 31, 2026 Estimated Value of Bridge Contract: ████████████████████████████████████████████ Statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition.

RFO FAR 6.103-2, GSA Agency Deviation RFO-2025-06, Unusual and Compelling Urgency; 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(2), Use of Noncompetitive Procedures Demonstration the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited.

The Edith Green Wendell Wyatt Federal Building houses numerous government agencies and their employees, and a disruption in these services would directly impact their ability to perform their missions. Potential consequences include: building safety and occupant well-being, mission critical operations, damage to government property, and increased costs.

Due to the GAO protest and corrective action resulting in the termination of BPA 47PL0225A0001, there is not sufficient time to properly conduct a competitive full and open procurement to fulfill the Government’s requirements. The GAO protest created an immediate and significant challenge to the planned procurement process. Per FAR 16.191, a bridge contract may be appropriate when (1) the competitive follow-on contract or solicitation has been protested.

Northern Management Services is best situated to continue fulfilling these services. There would be significant phase-in and phase-out activities associated with the potential transition to another vendor In order to provide a successful transition, a new vendor would need at least 60 days to perform initial inspections, submit necessary documentation (e.g. building operation plan, deficiency report, etc.), and any other work required before the start of the period of Docusign Envelope ID: C92A1974-9DC1-4DFF-B82A-DCC2BB323D3C performance.

Additionally, the risk of bringing in a different contractor to perform these services on short notice and for only a one-year duration with no options would be significant in terms of increased pricing and potential performance failure at the site. The Government has less than 180 days until October 31, 2025, to award a bridge contract to ensure Operations and Mechanical Maintenance services continue at the Edith Green Wendell Wyatt Federal Building. Based on the extremely short time available to make an award, a sole source procurement utilizing RFO FAR 6.103-2, GSA Agency Deviation RFO-2025-06, Unusual and Compelling Urgency is the Government's only viable option to ensure services are maintained.

Efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies.

Due to the circumstances under which this bridge contract is required, it is impracticable for the Government to request offers from as many potential sources as possible (see above). Only the incumbent vendor has the ability to continue services without the need for additional site visits, interstate travel, and phase-in of new employees, equipment, and other items necessary to provide the requested services.

However, during this bridge contract period of performance the Government will work to submit a solicitation to the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) under FAR Part 8.4. This solicitation will be for a negotiated, performance based, requirements contract that will be set-aside for total small businesses in accordance with FAR 6.203 and 19.502-2. The expected beginning of performance for the new solicited award will be November 1, 2026.

No synopsis is required for this contract action in accordance with the exception identified under FAR 5.202(a)(2). This bridge contract must be awarded in less than 60 days, which does not give the Government time to comply with the time periods specified in FAR 5.203. By synopsizing the requirement, the Government would be seriously injured as required services would not be offered at the Edith Green Wendell Wyatt Federal Building for an extended duration.

However, in accordance with 41 U.S.C §3304 and RFO FAR 6.301(b)(1), GSA Agency Deviation RFO-2025-06 the justification for non-competitive procedures will be posted to the Government Point of Entry (GPE) within 30 days of award of the bridge contract.

Determination that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.

The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost of this bridge contract to be fair and reasonable. The determination is based on the following facts: (1) this bridge contract is being issued to a current O&M vendor in Region 10 who is familiar with the building and the scope of work and has a track record of good past performance and reasonable pricing; (2) the Docusign Envelope ID: C92A1974-9DC1-4DFF-B82A-DCC2BB323D3C Government developed an IGE which accounts for the unusual nature of this bridge contract; and (3) the labor rates for productive personnel are set by the Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division and are applicable to all Service Contract Labor Standards Act. These factors allow the Contracting Officer to determine the cost for this bridge contract to be fair and reasonable.

A description of the market research conducted.

No additional market research has been conducted for this bridge contract.

Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition.

In this instance, failure to produce a bridge contract will result in Operations and Mechanical Maintenance services to stop at the Edith Green Wendell Wyatt Federal Building. There will be significant failure in the operation of the building and in the support of the agency tenants if services are not continued. Conducting a full procurement with full and open competition would result in necessary services not being performed to maintain the building at a level required for tenant occupancy. This is in violation of our occupancy agreements with our tenant agencies and may result in preventable damage to the building that could be exceedingly expensive to repair or replace.

A listing of the sources, if any, that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition.

N/A

Statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services required.

The re-procurement of Operations and Mechanical Maintenance services for the Edith Green Wendell Wyatt Federal Building will be procured through eBuy, using full and open competition after exclusion of sources in accordance with FAR 6.203, set-asides for small business concerns. This re-procurement will be conducted during the period of performance of this bridge contract which will provide ample time for small business participation.
