47PD5426C0006.text:
JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 1. Contracting Agency and Activity (FAR 6.103-2) (Deviation RFO-2025-06) The General Service Administration (GSA), Public Building Service (PBS), Office of Acquisition Management, Acquisition Project Delivery Contracting Division West, intends to award a contract using other than full and open competition.

Justification for other than full and open competition in accordance with FAR 6.103-2 (GSA Class Deviation RFO- 2025-06). 2. Nature of Action Being Approved & Description of Supplies or Services (FAR 6.104-1(a)(2)) and (FAR 6.104-1(a)(3)) (Deviation

RFO-2025-06)

This justification authorizes a contract award to ATI Restoration, LLC (ATI Restoration), UEI PF7GKP1KLLJ2, for the Emergency Water Leak Remediation Services project at Chet Holifield Federal Building, 24000 Avila Road, Laguna Niguel,

CA.

This contract is being established for Immediate Water Mitigation & Structural Stabilization. On January 30, 2026, an eight (8)-inch main sprinkler pipe burst on the first floor in Suite 1700, resulting in significant flooding affecting 100,000 square feet of occupied space.

The incident was discovered by the Operations and Maintenance

(O&M) contractor, King & George, at approximately 11:00pm;

GSA facility personnel were immediately notified. Due to the scale of flooding, the presence of asbestos-containing materials within the affected area, and the need for immediate stabilization efforts,

ATI

Restoration was identified to perform emergency mitigation and remediation services. The scope of ATI’s water remediation services includes the following: Phase 1: Initial Emergency Drying and Extraction Phase 2: Ongoing Structural Drying and Monitoring Phase 3: Remaining Clean-Up Efforts (Remediation) 3. Estimated Dollar Value: The Government estimate is $980,000.00 4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition (FAR 6.104-1(a)(4)) (Deviation

RFO-2025-06)

FAR 6.103-2 (Deviation RFO-2025-06), Unusual and Compelling Urgency (41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(2)) This authority permits contracting without full and open competition when the agency's need for supplies or services is of such unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured unless the agency is permitted to limit the number of sources from which it solicits bids or proposals. revised 08/26/2024 Docusign Envelope ID: 6632AB1E-C253-8326-818C-12E0952160CC

5. A statement demonstrating the unique qualifications of the proposed contractor or the nature of the action requiring the use of the authority

(FAR

6.104-1(a)(5)) (Deviation

RFO-2025-06)

ATI Restoration has extensive knowledge of the federal building, ability to quickly mobilize, security clearances, and special capabilities to perform emergency water leak remediation at the Chet Holifield Federal Building.

Having dealt with remediation at the building previously,

ATI

Restoration is familiar with the building where work will be performed. ATI Restoration can provide immediate manpower and has the ability to deploy more than thirty-five (35) + technicians within 48 hours.

ATI

Restoration also has specialized equipment such as industrial-grade dehumidification, moisture mapping infrared tech, and HEPA-filtration systems at scale on hand. The O&M provided the initial emergency response and identified ATI Restoration as the subcontractor to support their response.

Having the demonstrated capabilities, resources and experience in the building,

ATI

Restoration is identified as a capable source to support this requirement.

This project is considered unusual and compelling urgency.

Without professional remediation, the facility faces imminent risk of permanent structural degradation and toxic mold proliferation, which would result in "serious injury" (financial and operational) to the Government. The facilities team noted

ATI

Restoration LLC’s unique ability to manage the "unknown extent" of damage without requiring extensive sub-contracting delays. The primary objective is to stabilize the environment as early as possible to mitigate water damage and mold development.

6. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by

FAR

5.2 and, if not, which exception under

FAR

5.202 applies

(FAR

6.104-1(a)(6)) (Deviation

RFO-2025-06)

The O&M initially subcontracted ATI Restoration to support the initial emergency response due to their capabilities, ability to immediately resource the work, knowledge of the building and demonstrated past success on similar work.

The response is larger than originally anticipated and requires additional support.

Based on the fact that

ATI

Restoration supported the initial response and carries the intricate knowledge of the project history and existing conditions, they were identified as a capable source to support this requirement: the Office of Facilities Management and the Acquisition Project Delivery Contracting Division West did not solicit available capabilities from industry for the emergency water leak remediation under the exception of

FAR

5.202 (a)(2).

Soliciting additional sources would result in unacceptable delays, which would cause permanent structural degradation and toxic mold proliferation. A competitive procurement is not feasible given the timeline constraints of structural degradation and toxic mold buildup if the water leak is not addressed immediately.

Any competitive procurement would require extended solicitation periods for multiple contractors to assess the water leak.

Additionally, most contractors are reluctant to assume the substantial risks associated with a water leak without the immediate equipment readily available, further limiting the pool of willing and capable sources. This could create inconsistent baseline assumptions and complicated evaluation, price negotiations, and post-award execution.

These complications, combined with multiple bidders making different assumptions about existing conditions and execution methods, would significantly extend the procurement timeline beyond the planned award timeline.

The Government has identified

ATI

Restoration as the firm with the capabilities of meeting the immediate requirements without these competitive procurement risks. Other contractors performing in California may possess general capabilities or security clearances individually, but

ATI

Restoration combines immediate availability of cleared personnel, willingness to assume project risks, and proven performance on prior

GSA detention facility projects.

This combination of qualifications makes

ATI

Restoration the identified source capable of meeting the critical timeline. Due to their initial involvement with the emergency response, having ATI Restoration bid the project would reduce assumption discrepancies and scope interpretation risks.

ATI

Restoration's experience with

GSA under prior and active contracts provides familiarity with operational requirements, minimizing execution risks from multiple contractor evaluations and varying project interpretations. revised 08/26/2024 2 Docusign Envelope ID: 6632AB1E-C253-8326-818C-12E0952160CC

7. Determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the government will be fair and reasonable

(FAR

6.104-1(a)(7)) (Deviation

RFO-2025-06)

The Contracting Officer determines that the anticipated price will be fair and reasonable based on a detailed price analysis.

ATI

Restoration’s proposed price will be reviewed by the Contracting Officer and

GSA personnel with technical expertise and compared against the Independent Government

(IGE).

Prior to award of the proposed contract, price information shall be obtained from the contractor, and a price analysis will be conducted and documented to sufficiently determine that the cost to the Government of the proposed acquisition will be fair and reasonable.

8. A description of the market research conducted (see FAR Part 10) and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted

(FAR

6.104-1(a)(8)) (Deviation

RFO-2025-06)

Market research was conducted by the Contracting Officer. Based on the market research conducted, ATI Restoration

LLC was identified to provide the immediate, high-capacity response necessary to prevent further damage based on the follow: The first phase of market research involved immediate internal coordination between the Operations & Maintenance

(O&M) first responders (King & George) and the

GSA

Facilities Management team. ● Capability Gap Analysis: The team discussed the size and scale of the eight-inch main fire sprinkler pipe burst to determine if internal resources or the existing

O&M contract could handle the remediation. ● Determination of Scope: It was determined that the scale of flooding (approximately 100,000 square feet) and the presence of asbestos-containing materials in Suite 1700 required specialized expertise beyond standard maintenance capabilities. Based on the nature of the requirement, the search focused on firms with proven capacity for large-scale mobilization. ● Past Performance Review: The Facilities Management team reviewed historical data and documented success with similar large-scale remediation projects at this specific location. ● Knowledge of Facility: ATI Restoration LLC was identified due to their extensive knowledge of the Chet Holifield Federal Building's unique characteristics and their ability to navigate the complex environment without sub-contracting delays.

Market research indicated that local Small Business (SB) set-asides were not feasible due to: ● Inventory Constraints: The scale of equipment required (including 200+ pieces for drying and testing) exceeded current local

SB inventory. ● Time-to-Mobilization: Risk mitigation for toxic mold proliferation required a provider already vetted and ready for immediate deployment. This acquisition is conducted under the FAR Part 6.103-2 Unusual and compelling urgency, prioritizing the preservation of the facility over traditional protracted competition cycles.

9. Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition (FAR 6.104-1(a)(9)) (Deviation RFO-2025-06) The Chet Holifield Federal Building is scheduled for sale and final conveyance to new ownership by early June 2026.

The Government has a pending

$146.4M+ interest in the sale of this property.

Failure to remediate the water intrusion and maintain the facility's condition immediately would likely be viewed as a material change in the property's status.

This could empower the purchaser to renegotiate for a significantly lower sale price, delay the closing indefinitely, or seek legal remedies for breach of the conveyance terms.

Without immediate professional remediation, the facility faces imminent risk of potential lost in sales. revised 08/26/2024 3 Docusign Envelope ID: 6632AB1E-C253-8326-818C-12E0952160CC Market research and historical data indicate that every 24-hour delay in water mitigation leads to a non-linear increase in remediation costs as moisture penetrates deeper into the building's 1,000,000 square foot envelope.

A stoppage in services now would transition this project from a standard mitigation effort to a much more costly and protracted restoration and hazardous material abatement project, further draining Government resources and jeopardizing the firm June 2026 transfer deadline. The selection of ATI Restoration ensures that remediation remains continuous, leveraging their pre-existing mobilization and building knowledge to avoid the high costs of operational failure and mission displacement.

10. A listing of any sources that expressed a written interest in the acquisition (FAR 6.104-1(a)(10)) (Deviation

RFO-2025-06)

ATI Restoration verbally confirmed its capability and availability to continue the remediation effort within the required timeframe.

11. A statement of any actions the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition, if subsequent acquisitions are anticipated

(FAR

6.104-1(a)(11)) (Deviation

RFO-2025-06)

It is acknowledged that competitive procurement is a priority and that this award is justified only by the unusual and compelling urgency of this specific requirement.

This procurement addresses emergency water leak remediation services with significant timeline constraints.

Given the urgency of accomplishing this requirement, there are no actions that can be taken to remove or overcome the existing barriers to competition for this specific acquisition.

Competition among qualified sources will be utilized for all future requirements unless a valid justification such as this one exists. The Government will continue to conduct thorough market research to gauge the marketplace capabilities for future requirements.

The Government will seek competition for future acquisitions for these products or services.

12. Research to support the facts presented for the justification above Approved acquisition plan and market research. See attached. 13. CERTIFICATIONS (FAR 6.104-1(a)(12)) (Deviation RFO-2025-06) (See, FAR Part 6.104-2 for approval thresholds and

FAR

This statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S. Code 1901 implemented by FAR 12.000; see also FAR 12.102(b).

Authority: 10 United States Code section 3204(a)(2) as implemented in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-2(b), Unusual and compelling urgency.

Amount: The total combined contract capacity is estimated to be $.

2 Justification and Approval for Other than Full and Open Competition

1. Contracting Activity: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Honolulu District

(POH)

2. Description of Action: Award a contract to repair the 40-foot rappel tower at the Army 25 th Infantry Division (25ID) Lightning Academy, Schofield Barracks, Oahu, Hawaii.

3. Description of Supplies/Services: The Contractor shall repair and retrofit the existing 40-foot rappel tower at Lightning Academy, Schofield Barracks, Oahu, Hawaii to make it code compliant. Work for this project includes, but is not limited to: repair damage caused by initial pull tests; remove existing paint to facilitate work and recoat in areas where coating was removed and on new members; repair welding in areas with exposed seams, ensuring there is no trapped moisture which would cause further corrosion; add grip texture to stair nosings; replace short bolts which are depressed within nuts with bolts of proper thread length; repair, relocate, and detail primary anchor points; replacement of hitching; add secondary anchors; add platform edge padding; modify or replace floor grating to allow for proper connection details for anchors and hitching posts; retrofit of brace gusset plates and brace bolts; load testing of hitching posts and anchors.

4. Authority Cited: 10 United States Code section 3204(a)(2) as implemented in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-2(a)(2), When the agency’s need for the supplies or services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured unless the agency is permitted to limit the number of sources from which it solicits bids or proposals, full and open competition need not be provided for.

5. Reason for Authority Cited: a. Background Due to the compelling need of the rappel tower, USACE POH solicited this requirement as an 8(a) sole source to Sharon Zambo-Fan & Associates, Inc. (SZF) on 11 September 2025 with the intention of awarding a contract in fiscal year (FY) 2025. During the site visit, it was discovered that the stakeholder had made modifications to the site, resulting in an increase in the estimated project cost. Consequently, the stakeholder required additional time to secure funding due to the Government shutdown from 1 October to 12 November, leading to the project's postponement to FY 2026, with an award date no later than 3 December 2025, as SZF would graduate from the 8(a) program on that date. On 3 December 2025, the USACE POH was notified by the stakeholder that they had received their allotment of funds and are now authorized to proceed with the project.

CUI CUI

3 b. Justification Per 10 USC 3204(a)(2), a contract can be awarded without full and open competition if the agency’s need for the supplies or services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured unless the agency is permitted to limit the number of sources from which it solicits bids or proposals.

The 25ID requires the use of an operational, on-site rappel tower to provide critical training to all U.S. Forces within the Indo-Pacific by supporting the Programs of Instruction (POI) for the 25ID Lightning Academy's Air Assault, Rappel Master, and Jungle Operations Training Courses (JOTC). The existing 40-foot rappel tower at Schofield Barracks has been unusable for 22 months due to structural deficiencies that require repair. Due to the non-operational status of the rappel tower, training courses have been canceled which led to a complete loss of training opportunities for 140 soldiers, course capacity has been reduced which diminished the output of qualified personnel by approximately 50%, and an unsustainable reliance on a temporary alternate site at Marine Corps Base Hawaii (MCBH) has created significant logistical and operational burdens. This has created a compelling justification under 10 USC 3204(a)(2) for this other than full and open action. If the rappel tower is not repaired, combat effectiveness of 25ID will decrease and lower warfighter capabilities in the Indo-Pacific region.

The following list details the critical impacts of not having an operational, onsite rappel tower at the 25ID Lightning Academy:

1. Direct Degradation of Warfighting Skills. Ai r assault and vertical insertion/extraction are perishable skills that are tied to essential military missions. The inability to consistently train in these tasks leads to skill atrophy, which limits operational reach and tactical flexibility.

2. Erosion of Institutional Expertise. The l ack of training has a cascading adverse effect. Lightning Academy courses are designed to create subject-matter experts who act as force multipliers within their home units. Without these experts, unit commanders do not have access to the specialized expertise required for complex operations.

3. Logistical and Financial Inefficiencies. The c urrent reliance on the 28foot rappel tower at MCBH is not a feasible long-term solution. Training capacity is limited to 50% and units must expend additional time, manhours, fuel, and maintenance to transport personnel and equipment across Oahu. This dependence on an external installation also creates scheduling conflicts and administrative hurdles which makes training unpredictable and inefficient.

CUI CUI

4

4. Potential Risk to Accreditation. The Air Assault Course and Rappel Master Course both require the use of a 40-foot rappel tower. Utilizing the 28-foot rappel tower at MCBH requires a semiannual exception to policy (ETP) with the U.S. Army Maneuver Center of Excellence. The Lightning Academy has obtained temporary ETP approval which allows these courses to utilize the 28-foot rappel tower at MCBH on the condition that the 40-foot rappel tower at Schofield Barracks will be remediated and operational to support future courses. Failure to repair the 40-foot rappel tower at Schofield Barracks immediately may place the accreditation of the Institutional Training Division and Lightning Academy at risk.

The 2025 Government shutdown created an unusual circumstance that prevented the consummation of the 8(a) contract prior to the selected contractor graduating from the 8(a) program. If the Government had not shutdown for 43 days in October 2025 and sufficient funds had been provided to USACE POH by 13 November 2025, a contract would have been awarded to SZF by 3 December

2025. SZF and their subconsultants are already familiar with this requirement as they have had multiple site visits and submitted proposed pricing. Resoliciting the requirement as a sole source to another contractor or as a competitive action will further delay the repair of the rappel tower and would not be in the Government’s best interest.

The critical need of an operational rappel tower and the unusual situation of the Government shutdown have created and met the justification needed per 10 USC 3204(a)(2). c. Alternatives There are no viable alternatives for this acquisition. An operational 40-foot rappel tower is essential for conducting required training in the Indo-Pacific region. At present, there are no other training facilities on the island of Oahu that feature a 40-foot rappel tower capable of accommodating the necessary number of trainees. Resoliciting this requirement as a sole source award to another contractor or as a competitive action will require scheduling another site visit and answering Requests for Information (RFIs). d. Impact If this justification is not approved, the risk of insufficient training would significantly increase, potentially resulting in reduced mission readiness and warfighting capability.

6. Efforts to Obtain Competition:

A notice as required by FAR 5.201 will not be published. Per FAR 5.202(a)(2), a

CUI CUI

5 notice required under FAR 5.201 is not required if the proposed contract action is made under the conditions described in FAR 6.302-2 and the Government would be seriously injured if the agency complies with the time periods specified in 5.203.

7. Actions to Increase Competition:

This justification supports a discrete requirement that will end when the project is complete. Therefore, there are no planned actions to increase competition for the requirement covered by this justification. POH will nevertheless evaluate the reasons and causes for increased requirements for rappel tower repair/retrofit not foreseen.

8. Market Research:

Market Research was conducted and an Independent Government Estimate (IGE) obtained. The full Market Research analysis report and IGE are included in Attachment 1.

9. Interested Sources: Reference Market Research analysis report included in Attachment 1

10. Other Facts: N/A.

Justification and Approval (J&A) For Other Than Full and Open Competition (>SAT) Acquisition Plan Action ID: ████████████████████████████ Project #: 629-26-103 Emergency St. John Roof Replacement and Interior Mitigation

1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office 16 (NCO 16) 400 Veterans Avenue Biloxi, MS 39531-2410 Organizational Activity: St. John VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic

(CBOC)

4004 West Airline Highway Reserve, LA 70084-5712 Southeast Louisiana Veteran Health Care System

(SLVHCS)

2400 Canal Street New Orleans, LA 70119-6535 2237 Number/Funding: ███████████

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved:

This urgent, one-time firm-fixed-price sole source requirement addresses severe deterioration of the facility’s roofing system and interior spaces by replacing the extensively damaged roof with a new commercial-grade Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer (EPDM) system built to withstand Gulf Coast climate conditions, and by repairing interior areas affected by water intrusion through removal and replacement of damaged walls, ceilings, and flooring, mold remediation, and renovation of affected rooms. The construction effort includes demolition of existing roofing layers, inspection and repair of the underlying structural deck, and installation of a complete roofing system with appropriate vapor barriers, insulation, and drainage to ensure long-term durability.

3. Description of Supplies/Services Required to Meet the Agency’s Needs:

To meet the needs of the St. John VA CBOC for the roof system removal and interior repairs, the following supplies and services are required:

██████████████████████████████ ██████████████████████████████ Acquisition ID#: ███████████████████

1. Labor and Supervision: - Skilled labor for all aspects of roofing and interior renovations, including demolition, construction, and installation. - Supervisory personnel to oversee the work and ensure compliance with specifications and safety regulations.

2. Materials: - Roofing Supplies: - EPDM roofing membrane and associated materials. - Insulation (minimum R-30). - Underlayment, flashings, and other roofing accessories. - Interior Renovation Supplies: - Sheetrock (5/8 moisture and mold-resistant), paint, and wall treatments. - Acoustical tiles and ceiling grid systems. - Vinyl composite tile (VCT) flooring. - Cabinetry, fixtures, and hardware to match existing specifications.

Period of Performance (POP) for this project is 45 calendar days from issuance of Emergency Notice to Proceed (NTP).

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition:

() (1) Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements per 41 USC §3304(a)(1) as implemented by

RFO 6.103-1;

(X) (2) Unusual and Compelling Urgency per 41 USC §3304(a)(2) as implemented by RFO 6.103-2; () (3) Industrial Mobilization, Engineering, Developmental or Research Capability or Expert Services per 41 USC §3304(a)(3) as implemented by RFO 6.103-3; () (4) International Agreement per 41 USC §3304(a)(4) as implemented by RFO 6.103-4 () (5) Authorized or Required by Statute per 41 USC §3304(a)(5) as implemented by RFO 6.103-5; () (6) National Security per 41 USC §3304(a)(6) as implemented by RFO 6.103-6; () (7) Public Interest per 41 USC §3304(a)(7) as implemented by RFO 6.103-7;

5. Demonstration that the Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or Nature of the Acquisition Requires the Use of the Authority Cited Above (applicability of authority):

Acquisition ID#:

This requirement is justified for other than full and open competition per RFO FAR 6.103-2 due to the unusual and compelling urgency of replacing the severely deteriorated roofing system and conducting interior remediation at St. John VA

CBOC.

A competitive procurement would add an estimated 60 days, which is not feasible given the ongoing damage and associated risks. Coactint, LLC, a verified SDVOSB with prior experience at SLVHCS, is the most suitable contractor because they possess the specialized expertise needed for EPDM roof replacement, extensive demolition, mold remediation, and strict safety and infection-control protocols, and they can mobilize within two weeks. Their unique qualifications, familiarity with the site, and ability to meet the project’s technical and safety requirements support the use of the cited authority for a sole source emergency award.

Due to the facts outlined above, if this emergency work for water intrusion / roof repair under unusual and compelling urgency is not awarded to Coactint, LLC., it will harm CBOC operations which in turn will affect patient safety.

6. Description of Efforts Made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as possible (including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by RFO Part 5 and, if not, which exception under RFO Part 5 applies):

Market research conducted with Small Business Administration Dynamic Small Business Search (SBA DSBS) demonstrates that 6 SDVOSB/VOSB certified with NAICS 238160 with potential capabilities to perform this work. However, due to the unusual and compelling urgency regarding this requirement, this will be sole sourced to Coactint LLC, as to not affect patient safety.

Per RFO FAR 5.101 (b)(2), the Contracting Officer need not submit the notice required by RFO 5.201 when (FAR 5.101(b)(2), The proposed contract action is made under the conditions described in RFO FAR 6.103, specifically RFO 6.103-2 (b), the Government would be seriously injured. Due to the unusual and compelling urgency of this action, the action will not be synopsized as referenced above

7. Determination by the CO that the Anticipated Cost to the Government will be Fair and Reasonable:

Based on historical data, there is reasonable expectation that a fair and reasonable cost can be negotiated. In addition, the Contracting Officer anticipates cost will be considered fair and reasonable based on comparing finalized cost to the Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE).

8. Description of the Market Research Conducted and the Results, or a Statement of the Reasons Market Research Was Not Conducted:

The recommended sole source award source, Coactint, LLC, an SBA certified SDVOSB, was able to immediately diagnose and provide market research pricing for the work. There are no known Buy American Act exceptions to this requirement.

The contract incorporates FAR 52.225-9 and confirmation of the materials will be made upon submittal review by the Southeast Louisiana VA Engineering group. If there are concerns that materials do not meet the Buy American Act, the appropriate measures will be taken by the Engineers and/or the Contracting Team to mitigate the use of improper materials.

None at this time.

NON COMPETITIVE MEMORANDUM FOR SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION ACTIONS

IAW FAR 13.101-3(b)

1. REQUIRING AGENCY - DOJ/Bureau of Prisons, FCI Cumberland

2. NATURE/DESCRIPTION OF ACTION BEING APPROVED - Sole source acquisition

3. DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY'S NEEDS As part of the mission of the institution, comprehensive medical services are provided to the inmate population. In meeting the healthcare needs of the inmate population, the BOP provides essential medical, dental, and mental health services to Federal inmates. When a medical need arises that cannot be provided by the institution medical staff, referrals are made to community-based medical providers. These services include Inpatient/Outpatient Facility and Physician services, as well as Outpatient Institution Services of Dentist, Dietician, Pharmacist, and Optometrist. The services will be procured by purchase orders. The proposed performance period will be from April 1, 2026, through April 31, 2026. Estimated value of requirement is $250,000.00.

4. IDENTIFICATION OF STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION - 41 U.S.C. 253; 41 U.S.C. 1901(e)

5. DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR'S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE

NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED:

American Correctional Healthcare, Inc (ACH) is the incumbent and has agreed to continue at the previous negotiated contracted rates. FCI Cumberland's comprehensive medical contract has expired, and this ensures continuity of care while a new multi-year agreement is negotiated by the Field Acquisition Office. This interim acquisition is necessary pending competitive award of a CMS contract. The incumbent contractor continues to provide the necessary medical services through their established network of local medical facilities and physicians. The immediate availability of community-based health care services is critical to avoid any disruption in obtaining the necessary medical services and to ensure the orderly operation of the institutions. In an effort to maintain continuity of care, the Government has determined that it is in the best interest to continue to utilize ACH who can provide the required medical services without delay. This has been determined to be fair and reasonable, and in the Government's best interest. Their established medical network ensures the institution's medical needs are fulfilled and their network of medical service providers alleviates delay and disruption of the overall mission of basic and emergency medical care. Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION SECTION 1: IDENTIFICATION OF THE AGENCY AND THE CONTRACTING ACTIVITY

☐ Office of Acquisitions Management ☐ Foreign Service Institute ☐ Office of Foreign Missions ☐ U.S. Mission to the United Nations ☒ Overseas Post U.S. Embassy Rome, Italy Requiring Activity U.S. Embassy in Rome – GSO

Approval is requested to solicit and award, on a sole-source basis, an IDIQ contract to Queen Limousine for transportation services with drivers in support of a senior high-level USG VIP visit to Italy, as described in Section 3, on behalf of the Requiring Activity.

The authority to act under this Class Justification and Approval (J&A) expires on February 28, 2026.

This action will result in a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract.

SECTION 3: DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY’S NEEDS

The Embassy requires transportation services with drivers to support a Senior high-level USG VIP visit in connection with the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympic Games.

Services Estimated Quantity Estimated Period of Performance Transportation Services with Drivers 190 Vehicles 20 January – 15 February The estimated value for the entire period of performance is estimated at $7,584,597.43.

Task orders will be issued as required to meet operational needs and security requirements.

The contractor shall provide high-quality vehicles and drivers and operate with established, robust internal processes for financial management, quality assurance, and operational oversight to ensure all aspects of contract execution are properly monitored and controlled.

SECTION 4: IDENTIFICATION OF THE STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 41 USC 3304, as implemented by FAR 6.3 and substantiated by the following:

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE ☒ FAR 6.103-2 - Unusual and compelling urgency.

SECTION 5: DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED

The contractor’s unique qualifications and expertise are essential due to the scale and complexity of the event, the specific requirements to be met, and the contractor’s demonstrated experience and capacity to manage such services effectively.

This assessment is further supported by the last-minute notification of VIP travel, the stringent security and operational standards to be met, and the overall critical nature of the required services, which creates an unusual and compelling urgency.

These unique senior high-level USG VIP travel requirements result in only a single, or a very limited number of, responsible sources capable of providing the required level of operational support. The proposed contractor can meet these requirements due to a strong record of past performance on similar projects.

SECTION 6. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS WERE SOLICITED FROM AS

MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE, INCLUDING WHETHER A NOTICE WAS OR

WILL BE PUBLICIZED AS REQUIRED BY FAR SUBPART 5.2 AND, IF NOT, WHICH EXCEPTION

UNDER FAR 5.202 APPLIES

A formal synopsis of the proposed procurement was not published on SAM.gov because this contract action is being made under the conditions described in FAR 6.103-2, which allows for exceptions due to unusual and compelling urgency. Market research identified a few other vendors; however, none demonstrated the experience or capacity to manage operational services of this scale.

SECTION 7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST TO THE GOVERNMENT IS FAIR AND REASONABLE

The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to the Government of the services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable based on: o Rates from prior similar events SECTION 8. DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED (SEE PART 10) AND THE

RESULTS OR A STATEMENT OF THE REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED

This event is attended by both official and unofficial representatives from around the world. Most services have already been secured, and costs increase significantly during this period, further limiting the number of vendors capable of meeting the Embassy’s transportation requirements.

The short notice, high demand, and security-sensitive nature of the requirement have limited the ability to conduct full and open market research.

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE SECTION 9. ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION The unique requirements associated with senior high-level USG VIP travel, combined with security considerations and the operational environment of the event, limit the Government's ability to conduct a full and open competition.

The proposed contractor possesses unique qualifications that meet the Government's security and logistical requirements. Any delay in the award may result in the unavailability of qualified transportation resources.

SECTION 10. LISTING OF THE SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED, IN WRITING, AN INTEREST

IN THE ACQUISITION

MTM Italia Srl expressed interest in providing these services. MTM Italia Srl does not, however, currently possess the experience required to support such a complex, high-profile assignment with stringent security and logistical standards.

Furthermore, due to the urgency of the requirement and the limited time available before the event, there is insufficient time to onboard and prepare a new contractor to meet the complex operational demands. Attempting to do so would pose significant risks to the successful execution of the event and could compromise both security and mission objectives.

SECTION 11. STATEMENT OF THE ACTIONS, IF ANY, THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO REMOVE OR

OVERCOME ANY BARRIERS TO COMPETITION BEFORE ANY SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITION FOR THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED

The Government recognizes the importance of fostering full and open competition for future acquisitions of similar services. The unique operational environment connected with the event, characterized by extreme demand, early block allocation, and security-driven constraints, has significantly limited the Government' s ability to conduct meaningful competition in the immediate term.

DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS

Justification and Approval (J&A) For Other Than Full and Open Competition (>SAT) Acquisition Plan Action ID: 36C242-26-AP-1074

1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs, VISN 02, Station 526 James J. Peters VA Medical Center.

• NCO2 Contracting – James J. Peters VA Medical Center • 2237: 526-26-1-636-0079

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Processed:

This is an emergency construction contract for the James J. Peters Veterans Affairs Medical Center, 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, New York 10468 to furnish all supervision, labor, equipment, and material necessary to replace the existing flooring with Stonhard flooring in the OR area. The work under this scope includes the removal of existing floor finishes and installation of new seamless, resinous Stonhard flooring in Operating Rooms (ORs), Control Rooms, and Corridors within the surgical suite area. The new flooring system shall meet all applicable standards for infection control, durability, slip resistance, and chemical resistance suitable for hospital operating environments. All work shall be coordinated to minimize disruption to hospital operations and performed in accordance with ICRA (Infection Control Risk Assessment) and safety requirements. The estimated FFP Construction cost is.

3. Description of Supplies/Services Required to Meet the Agency’s Needs:

The total estimated value of this project is. The estimated period of performance is 180 days. The work is completed during off-hours due to operating room being mainly active during business hours. The OR flooring needs to be replaced due to the cracks and breaches found during the surgical light replacement project. The integrity of OR flooring is critical to maintaining infection control standards and ensuring a sterile surgical environment. Therefore, this project falls under FAR 6.302-2 unusual and compelling urgency due to the imminent threat of having to cancel/delay surgical procedures at the Bronx VAMC operating room.

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition:

() (1) Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements per 41 USC §3304(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1; ( X) (2) Unusual and Compelling Urgency per 41 USC §3304(a)(2) as implemented by FAR 6.302-2; () (3) Industrial Mobilization, Engineering, Developmental or Research Capability Attachment 1: Request for Sole Source Justification Format >SAT Revision: 03 Effective Date: 04/15/24 Acquisition ID#: 36C242-26-AP-1074 or Expert Services per 41 USC §3304(a)(3) as implemented by FAR 6.302-3; () (4) International Agreement per 41 USC §3304(a)(4) as implemented by FAR 6.302-4 () (5) Authorized or Required by Statute per 41 USC §3304(a)(5) as implemented by FAR 6.302-5; () (6) National Security per 41 USC §3304(a)(6) as implemented by FAR 6.302-6; () (7) Public Interest per 41 USC §3304(a)(7) as implemented by FAR 6.302-7;

5. Demonstration that the Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or Nature of the Acquisition Requires the Use of the Authority Cited Above (applicability of authority):

The sole source award will be given to Veterans Contracting Group, Inc., an SBA certified SDVOSB based on the requirement in VAAR 819.7008 and under the authority of FAR 6.302-2 unusual and compelling urgency. Veterans Contracting Group, Inc. is a responsible contractor that has performed multiple projects to completion at the Bronx VAMC. Veterans Contracting Group is currently working in the Operating room performing surgical light replacement. Given that the contractor is already mobilized and working within the restricted OR suite, they possess active infection control barriers (ICRA), negative air containment, and all necessary safety and isolation measures in place. Engaging a new contractor would: • Require demobilization and re-establishment of new ICRA barriers, • Cause project delays and additional cost, • Increase risk of contamination by introducing new personnel and equipment into the sterile zone, and • Disrupt the current sequence of work within active surgical areas.

Cracks and breaches in the seamless flooring system create potential harborage points for bacteria and contaminants, posing a serious risk to patient safety and violating infection control requirements. The integrity of OR flooring is critical to maintaining infection control standards and ensuring a sterile surgical environment. This project is under time constraint because the rooms are scheduled to be turned back over to E.R. in a few weeks. If the cracked floors are not fixed, it will result in OR rooms not being operational and will result in canceled/delayed surgical cases. Therefore, this project falls under FAR 6.302-2 Unusual and compelling urgency as it will have a direct negative impact on patient care at the VA. For reasons of patient safety, infection control compliance, and schedule continuity, it is in the government’s best interest to issue this additional flooring replacement work to Veterans Contracting Group, Inc.

6. Description of Efforts Made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as deemed practicable:

Veterans Contracting Group is currently working in the Operating room performing surgical light replacement. Given that the contractor is already mobilized and working within the restricted OR suite, they possess active infection control barriers (ICRA), negative air containment, and all necessary safety and isolation measures in place. A proposal was immediately requested from Veterans Contracting Group after discovery of cracks and breaches in the OR’s flooring system. Under the authority of FAR 6.302-2 unusual and compelling urgency, a sources sought notice was not sent out as a quick award needed to be made to prevent patient care issues. Attachment 1: Request for Sole Source Justification Format >SAT Revision: 03 Effective Date: 04/15/24 Acquisition ID#: 36C242-26-AP-1074

7. Determination by the CO that the Anticipated Cost to the Government will be Fair and Reasonable:

The price provided for this emergent work to avoid delays that affect patient care was deemed fair & reasonable. The labor costs for the project are high due to the off hour work required while following safety, infection control, and isolation protocols in an active surgical environment. Engineering management also reviewed pricing to ensure it was fair and reasonable and sent their technical acceptance of the proposal.

8. Description of the Market Research Conducted and the Results, or a Statement of the Reasons Market Research Was Not Conducted:

The threat to patient care is evident in this project, and this is considered an FAR 6.302-2 unusual and compelling urgency based on the facts presented. Under the authority of FAR 6.302-2 unusual and compelling urgency, there was limited market research done based on the imminent threat of having to cancel/delay surgical procedures, which would directly and critically affect patient care at the Bronx VAMC. Based on the knowledge that VCG has, they have the ability and expertise to make the repairs/replacement efficiently and expeditiously, so that surgical procedures will not have to be cancelled/delayed. No other contractor can effectively perform the work without the need for additional delays, including possible detrimental effects on patients needing immediate surgical procedures.

9. Any Other Facts Supporting the Use of Other than Full and Open Competition:

Under the authority of FAR 6.302-2 and the requirements in VAAR 819.7008 an SBA certified SDVOSB was selected for this emergency work to prevent patient safety and infection control issues.

10. Listing of Sources that Expressed, in Writing, an Interest in the Acquisition:

Multiple sources were not sought under the authority of FAR 6.302-2 unusual and compelling urgency.

11. A Statement of the Actions, if any, the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome any Barriers to Competition before Making subsequent acquisitions for the supplies or services required:

In the future, if the acquisition is not an emergency, the facility will send out a sources sought notice and ensure proper competition for work being completed. This sole source is being justified under the authority of FAR 6.302-2 unusual and compelling urgency due to the critical need to replace the OR flooring without impacting patient care and safety.

U.S. Department of Justice Federal Bureau of Prisons Field Acquisition Office U.S. Armed Forces Reserve Complex Grand Prairie, Texas 75051 Justification for Other than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC) FCI Terminal Island Pursuant to FAR Subpart Deviation 6.103, the Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) has determined that the procurement for emergency shoring of tunnel at Federal Correctional Institution (FCI) Terminal Island located within the city limits of San Pedro, California, meets the criteria established for other than full and open competition. It is further concluded that this requirement is of an unusual and compelling urgency that delay in award would result in serious injury, financial, or other, to the Government. This limitation on competition is justified as supported by the following information:

1. FAR Deviation 6.104-1(a)(1): Identification of the agency and the contracting activity, and specific identification of the document as a "Justification for other than full and open competition.": Federal Bureau of Prisons Federal Correctional Institution Terminal Island (FCI Terminal Island) 1299 Seaside Avenue San Pedro, CA 90731

2. FAR Deviation 6.104-1(a)(2): Nature and/or description of the action being approved: The action being approved is for a new contract for emergency shoring of tunnel at FCI Terminal Island. The emergency requirement was identified during an engineering assessment of the institution’s underground steam tunnel that prompted immediate and urgent action to provide critical infrastructure support for the underground steam and hot water supply for staff, food service and inmate housing units. The contract type will be firmfixed price and a request for quote will be issued to Seamair Constuction, Inc (Unique Entity

ID: L23LG4M97QK4).

3. FAR Deviation 6.104-1(a)(3): Description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs (including the estimated value): To meet the Bureau of Prisons’ mission-critical requirement of maintaining safe and habitable conditions for staff, contractors and inmate population, all program areas must be kept in compliance with health, safety standards and be of hazardous free conditions. The contractor shall install approximately 250-foot sections of properly sized timber sets, and plywood fastened to timber sets at 6-foot intervals to the length of the tunnel. The shoring will provide support for existing wight loads, prevent soil and infrastructure movements and prevent collapsing of structures. The estimated cost for this project is $380,000.

4. FAR Deviation 6.104-1(a)(4): An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition: The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(2) as implemented by FAR Deviation 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency. FAR Deviation 6.103-2(b) provides for the applicability of this authority in situations "when the agency's need for the supplies or services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured unless the agency is permitted to limit the number of sources from which it solicits bids or proposals for."

5. FAR Deviation 6.104-1(a)(5): A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited: FCI Terminal Island’s underground tunnel holds access to the piping system for steam and hot water that supplies various program areas within the institution such as staff working quarters, food service and inmate housing units. It was identified during an engineering assessment of the institution that a 250-foot section of the tunnel was failing and at the verge of infrastructure collapse resulting in an unusual and compelling urgency for shoring tunnel service. The contractor, Seamair Constuction, Inc located in San Luis Obispo, California demonstrated the ability to mobilize quickly and has specialized knowledge to meet the urgent shoring requirements.

6. FAR Deviation 6.104-1(a)(6): A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as possible, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by part 5 and, if not, which exception under part 5 applies: The proposed contract action is made under the conditions described in FAR Deviation 6.103-2 and therefore the exception as FAR Deviation 5.201(b)(1) is applicable. The Government would be seriously injured if the agency complied with the time periods specified in FAR Deviation 5.201. This is an unusual and compelling urgent acquisition. Any further delay may result in serious injury, financial or other, to the Government.

Therefore, soliciting offers from additional sources would not be practicable. A notice will be publicized as required by part 5.

7. FAR Deviation 6.104-1(a)(7): A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable: The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated cost to the Government is fair and reasonable. This determination is based on the Independent Government Estimate (IGE), which was developed using pricing from similar shoring projects at other FBOP facilities and current market rates for equipment, labor, and materials. The IGE reflects a realistic cost for shoring equipment and material for installing a 250-foot section of timber sets, and plywood with fastened to timber sets at 6-foot intervals to the length of the tunnel.

8. FAR Deviation 6.104-1(a)(8): The market research conducted (see part 10) and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted: Due to the urgent need to stabilize the underground tunnel and support infrastructure from collapsing, it was determined that conducting a full market survey was not feasible. The underground tunnel engineering assessment and site visuals revealed the infrastructure is on the verge of catastrophic collapse of the tunnel system. This has created an immediate risk to safety and habitable conditions for inmates and staff. Given the specialized nature of shoring the tunnel, only a limited number of sources could perform the work without significant delays. As explained in the other sections, the proposed contractor possesses specialized experience and can mobilize quickly to meet the institution’s urgent operational needs.

9. FAR Deviation 6.104-1(a)(9): Any other facts supporting the justification: The urgency of this requirement is further supported by maintaining the health, safety, security, and orderly operation of the institution for staff and inmates. Maintaining the integrity of the institutions infrastructure and underground piping system from collapsing is critical. The underground tunnel systems piping supports climate-controlled temperatures for steam and hot water for food service and inmate housing units. Preventing any delays in the shoring process of tunnel and installing support structure will prevent catastrophic collapse and events. Any failure to promptly move forward could lead to unsafe indoor / outdoor conditions; disruption of essential programs and services; increased tension within the inmate population; and potential security incidents. Additionally, extended delays could result in damage to buildings and infrastructure, deterioration of staff working conditions, and inhumane conditions for both staff and inmates. Immediate action is necessary to mitigate these risks.

10. FAR Deviation 6.104-1(a)(10): A listing of the sources, if any, that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition: No other sources have expressed, in writing, an interest in this acquisition. Based on the urgent operational need and the requirement for immediate mobilization, there are no other sources reasonably available that can provide the required services within the critical time frame necessary to complete shoring of tunnel and install all required supplies to provide infrastructure and soil support.

Seamair Constuction, Inc 205 Suburban Rd, Suite 2 San Luis Obispo, CA 93406

11. FAR 6.104-1(a)(11): A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services required: FCI Terminal Island will continue to monitor industry market trends to identify potential competitive sources capable of meeting the Government’s requirements. For all future, nonurgent acquisitions, the agency will conduct advance planning to allow adequate time for competitive procurement methods. This plan will include regular assessments of the facilities infrastructure, equipment and conditions, to identify aging or failing systems. These actions are intended to mitigate the need for urgent procurements and ensure that maximum competition is sought whenever practicable.

12. FAR 6.104-1(a)(12): Contracting officer’s certification that the justification is accurate and complete to the best of the contracting officer’s knowledge and belief: I hereby certify this Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition is made in good faith. The supporting data and information contained herein are accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief. I further certify that this request is not the result of a lack of advance procurement planning.

The contract requires delivery of specialized in-home hospital beds and accessories to the individual VAMCs, with free on-board (FOB) destination, in accordance with the specific delivery instructions contained within the delivery orders. The contractor shall deliver to any VAMC within the United States and its outlying Territories and areas to include the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Alaska, and Hawaii upon issuance of a delivery order. The contractor must guarantee their ability to provide an uninterrupted source of supply of the awarded devices to satisfy the Government’s requirements for the effective period of the contract. The current contractor has the required supply chain in place to fulfill orders on a nationwide basis. Onboarding a new vendor to fulfill this requirement and deliver the hospital beds and accessories before the expiration of the current contract is not possible and would introduce delays and increased costs that would prevent timely performance and compromise patient care and safety. A new vendor would require at least 45 days to become fully operational. Therefore, Invacare is the only responsible source uniquely positioned to fulfill orders received from VAMCs in a timely manner. Invacare has provided an uninterrupted source of supply and commercial warranty of the hospital beds and accessories since 2020 and has delivered to locations within the United States and US Territories. From July 2023 through March 2025, under the previously awarded 5-year contract 36C10G18D0018, Invacare provided over in-home hospital beds or accessories to Veterans across the nation, demonstrating the capability to fulfill both standard and large-scale orders. Invacare is immediately capable of meeting all requirements of the contract and has the required capabilities to deliver the necessary products without interruption in supply or degradation of quality of care to the Veteran. Cost Savings: Without a bridge contract, VA would lack a National Contract vehicle to provide in-home hospital beds and accessories to Veterans in the community and VAMCs will be required to purchase the items through local Network Contracting Offices (NCO’s), potentially at open market prices, which would result in major financial loss to the Government and significantly delay the time it takes for the Veteran to receive the clinically required items.

ATTACHMENT 2 JUSTIFICATION & APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION for SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITIONS OVER THE MICROPURCHASE THRESHOLD (See FAR Part 2) UP TO SAT (See FAR 13.106-1) Date: _____12/10/2025___________________ PR Number: ____ _____________________

1. Nature and/or description of the item/service being procured and its intended use (include the anticipated cost): At Cuyahoga Valley National Park, the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) conducted a safety inspection of the Cuyahoga Valley Railroad at Bridge 447 and identified multiple critical structural defects. FRA documented wide gauge, defective and deteriorated bridge timbers, loose tie plates, and loose spikes, and issued a 30-day deadline for corrective action under a known defect report. Replacement of the defective bridge timbers cannot be performed using any off-the-shelf product. Each timber on Bridge 447 is a custom structural component, engineered and dapped (cut) to fit a specific location on the bridge. The Park and the Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad (CVSR), the Park’s non-profit operational partner, located the original engineered drawings for Bridge 447 and coordinated their recertification to ensure they remained valid for fabrication of new timbers. This certification process required additional time. Simultaneously, the National Park Service worked to secure project funding through the Federal Highway Administration. The estimated project cost is. Engineering review, funding approval, and manufacturer feedback confirmed that fabrication of new bridge timbers would require approximately 90 days, due to the specialized cutting, dapping, and structural design requirements. To stabilize the track condition while funding and drawings were being finalized, the Park implemented temporary control measures. A contractor installed approximately 25 gauge rods and re-spiked the tie plates to help hold the track gauge. However, FRA formally stated that these actions do not constitute corrective measures. FRA specifically noted: “As a reminder, gage rods are not considered a remedial action by FRA. The wide gage defects on the open deck bridge can only be corrected by re-gaging the rail, and the tie defects can only be corrected by replacing a sufficient number of bridge ties within the FRA allotted 30-days.” In addition to railroad safety compliance, public safety hazards were identified. Bridge 447 spans the Cuyahoga River, which supports heavy recreational use, including kayaking and canoeing on the park’s designated river trail. Loose spikes, tie plates, or deteriorated timber fragments could fall from the structure onto visitors, posing risks of serious injury or death. The National Park Service owns the rail line, while CVSR operates excursion services for park visitors, including the popular Bike Aboard program used by cyclists, paddlers, and hikers along the Towpath Trail and Cuyahoga River. CVSR’s operating season runs from February through December, leaving January as the only feasible window for full bridge timber replacement without shutting down service. If the project extends into summer months, CVSR would incur significant revenue loss, impair operational sustainability, and disrupt visitor services throughout the park.

Last updated 6/2/2016 The scope of the required work now includes not only fabrication and installation of new bridge timbers but also installation of new 132-lb railroad rail across the bridge deck to ensure structural integrity, address the wide-gauge condition, and maintain compliance with FRA requirements.

2. Sole Source Justification rationale (Check one and explain below):

______ Only one responsible source. __X___ Urgent and compelling circumstances exist. Include critical delivery or performance dates, and when you became aware of the requirement. Provide a specific statement of the impact on Government operations, financial or otherwise, if the required delivery or performance dates are not met. ______ Other _____________________________________________________ Explain: Given the FRA’s mandated timeline, the 90-day fabrication period, the threat to public and operational safety, and the restricted construction window, conducting full and open competition would cause unacceptable delays, expose the Government to enforcement action, and result in serious injury to the Government’s interests.

3. Market Research. Please explain the results or why one was not performed. State whether any other offers were received or anyone expressed interest:

Market research for this requirement was necessarily limited due to the FRA-mandated 30-day corrective action deadline, the structural safety concerns, and the 90-day fabrication period required for custom-engineered bridge timbers. However, the National Park Service performed targeted market research to determine the availability of qualified firms capable of fabricating and installing the required materials within the allowable timeframe.

1. Custom Timber Fabrication Bridge 447 uses engineered, location-specific bridge timbers that must be:  cut to exact dimensional tolerances,  dapped for placement on the bridge structure, and  produced using certified engineering drawings unique to this bridge. Through industry review and discussions with CVSR engineering staff, NPS confirmed that only a limited number of firms in the region fabricate custom railroad bridge timbers. Of these, most indicated fabrication lead times of 12–16 weeks, which would exceed the FRA compliance period and push construction into the rail operating season—an unacceptable delay that would result in operational shutdown and potential safety enforcement actions.

2. Railroad Bridge Specialists NPS reviewed previous contractors used by CVSR and other rail industry partners who perform:  bridge timber replacement,  custom milling/dapping,  rail re-gauging, and  installation of 132-lb rail sections. Many contractors with railroad experience do not fabricate timber in-house and rely on subcontracted specialty mills, which extend lead times beyond feasible limits. Only one known source verified the Last updated 6/2/2016 capability to fabricate custom timbers within the required 90-day timeframe and mobilize for installation during the January non-operational window.

3. Rail Material Availability Replacement rail (132-lb) is not a common off-the-shelf item in the region. Market checks determined that few suppliers maintain sufficient stock on hand, and many vendors require bulk orders or extended delivery schedules. The sole identified source was able to provide rail and associated hardware in the required quantity and within the repair schedule.

4. Safety and Work Window Constraints Competitive procurement for this type of work typically requires:  several weeks to develop specifications,  solicitation advertisement,  response periods,  evaluations, and  award processing. Even with accelerated procedures, the time required for full and open competition exceeds the FRA’s mandated timeline and would delay work beyond the January work window, resulting in:  loss of railroad service for CVSR,  inability to operate visitor programs (e.g., Bike Aboard),  financial impacts to the park partner, and  continued risk of structural failure or falling debris onto river users.

5. Summary of Market Research Findings Market research concluded:  Only one contractor identified could meet all the following simultaneously: o Fabricate custom bridge timbers within the 90-day period o Install new bridge timbers and 132-lb rail within the January shutdown window o Meet FRA safety and compliance requirements o Mobilize quickly under emergency conditions  Attempting full competition would cause procurement delays of 2–4 months, which would: o Violate FRA corrective action deadlines o Extend repairs into the active operating season o Create ongoing public and operational safety hazards Therefore, the results of the market research support limiting the procurement to the only known capable and timely source under FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

Sign Language interpretation is a highly specialized field. When used as a reasonable accommodation, successful interpretation relies upon technical acumen, familiarity with the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (D/HOH) person, as well as the nature of their communication with non-D/HOH individuals. Sign Language Interpreters need to be constantly aware of situational circumstances (tone, side-by-side conversations, and communication goals) while bridging a twoway language barrier (hearing to sign language and vice versa) in a timely and accurate matter. The proposed Contractor possesses demonstrated capability and experience to provide such services to the NRC. This experience includes sustained interaction with NRC D/HOH employees, understanding of agency operations, and familiarity with the technical subject matter commonly discussed in NRC settings. Further, their existent experience with the NRC and its employees allows for seamless continuity of service, without any typical learning curve requirements associated with onboarding a new provider, thereby reducing the risk of service delays or impairing the services being provided.

The NRC had a current contract for these specialized services; however, the contract ceiling and funding were exhausted. In February 2026, the NRC attempted to negotiate with SBA to increase the ceiling of the existing contract but was unsuccessful. The NRC also attempted to negotiate a 4-month bridge contract under the 8(a) program; however, the selected vendor withdrew its proposal due to an inability to certify compliance with the limitations on subcontracting thresholds.

Despite the NRC’s best efforts to ensure these statutorily required services could be supported through other means, competitive action is no longer feasible to ensure continuity of service and avoid putting the NRC at financial risk. Moreover, failure to provide support for reasonable accommodations to employees with disabilities covered by these NRC JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL Version Control Date: June 10, 2024 Federal statutes places the NRC at risk of violating the applicable laws. Violations may carry fines up to $300,000 per violation, as well as other monetary compensation. As such, the NRC has determined that the current circumstances for this requirement are of unusual and compelling urgency such that they warrant awarding a sole-source bridge contract to the incumbent contractor for four months and two one-month option periods. This approach ensures continuity of the required services and maintains compliance with the Rehab Act, ADA, and ADAAA while a follow-on procurement can be competitively awarded.

• Performing a wide range of diagnostic tests and support duties such as the collection of blood samples for analysis for research, coagulation studies and blood gas determination. • Operating radiologic fluoroscopy equipment to allow the medical team to appropriately visualize images during the procedure. • Assisting or performs testing such as electrocardiograms (ECG), intravascular ultrasound, intracoronary pressure wire, drug exercise challenges, and the administration of dynamic electrocardiographic monitoring (Holter) analysis. • Monitoring cardiac rhythms and able to recognize abnormal and life-threatening rhythms. • Performing other monitoring procedures such as oximetry, blood pressure, arterial monitoring, intracardiac monitoring and able to recognize abnormal readings. • Performing patient care procedures such as applying dressings, and collection of specimens or blood samples for analysis, and removal of access sheaths.

The Period of Performance (PoP) for this requirement is 10/20/2025 – 04/30/2026. The total contract value is $687,431.90.

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Restricted Competition: FAR 13.5 Simplified Procedures for Certain Commercial Items. The statutory authority for applying the Simplified Procedures for Commercial Items of FAR 13.5 is 41 U.S.C. § 1901 and is implemented by FAR 13.106-1(b)(2) for restricting competition on this procurement. Competition is restricted on this procurement for the reason below:

Acquisition ID#: 36C262-26-AP-0932 () Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements (X) Unusual and Compelling Urgency () Industrial Mobilization, Engineering, Developmental or Research Capability or Expert Services () International Agreement () Authorized or Required by Statute () National Security () Public Interest

5. Demonstration that the Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or Nature of the Acquisition Requires the Use of the Authority Cited Above (applicability of authority):

An incident occurred with the current contract (36C26221D0014 with an expiration date of 01/31/2026) that negatively impacted patient care. During a surgical procedure, a contracted Cardiovascular Technologist left the procedure because their shift was over. The individual did not provide for back-up coverage, leaving the surgical team without complete staffing. This incident most likely occurred because the current contractor was having financial issues that caused them to miss paying their employees for the prior pay period. This situation was part of an overall pattern of contract issues that are now resulting in failure to perform and the potential for performance issues in the future. Due to the direct impact on veteran care, it is critical that a new contract be immediately awarded to continue these services. Hence, this acquisition strategy is considered an emergency. Posting a solicitation would delay an already urgent request. A-Team Solutions, LLC is currently performing Cardiovascular Technologist Staffing Services with the VA San Diego Healthcare System (VASDHS) and is positioned to perform the same at the VAGLAHS.

6. Description of Efforts Made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as deemed practicable:

Market research for Cardiovascular Technologist Staffing Services for a new contract with an anticipated start date of 02/01/2026 was conducted for the VAGLAHS and is current as of 10/07/2025. Sources Sought 36C26226Q0016 seeking capability to provide Cardiovascular Technologist Staffing Services at the VAGLAHS was posted on Contract Opportunities on 08/28/2025. Market research recommended a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. A-Team Solutions responded to the Sources Sought and was deemed capable of performing. The upcoming new requirement will be re-competed as an SDVOSB set-aside.

This pricing accounts for 95 percent of the total quoted price of $687,431.90 and is reasonable considering the impact of inflation over the year. The quoted price for the Overtime Rate, at $125.82, is 48 percent higher. Although this is a significant increase over the current contract, it accounts for only one percent of the total quoted price. The On Call Rate, at $10.00, is 67 percent higher. The Embassy requires transportation services with drivers to support a Senior high-level USG VIP visit in connection with the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympic Games.

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE ☒ FAR 6.103-2 – Unusual and compelling urgency.

The contractor's unique qualifications and expertise are essential due to the scale and complexity of the event, the specific requirements to be met, and the contractor's demonstrated experience and capacity to manage such services effectively.

This assessment is further supported by the last-minute notification of VIP travel, the stringent security and operational standards to be met, and the overall critical nature of the required services, which creates an unusual and compelling urgency.

These unique senior high-level USG VIP travel requirements result in only a single, or a very limited number of, responsible sources capable of providing the required level of operational support. UNDER FAR 5.202 APPLIES

SECTION 7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST TO THE GOVERNMENT IS FAIR AND REASONABLE

U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE

UNICOR, Federal Prison Industries, Inc.

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION:

Authority Cited: 6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements; 10 U.S.C 3304 (c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(1) 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency; 10 U.S.C. 2304 (c)(2) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a) (2).

1. Identification of the agency and the contracting agency.

Bureau of Prisons - UNICOR - Federal Prison Industries – Allenwood, PA

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.

The UNICOR Factory at LSCI Allenwood manufactures office furniture, specifically seating. This factory needs specific parts to manufacture their product. The needed items for their product were on contract with Nightingale, however, that contract has since expired. Procurement is currently in the process of soliciting and awarding a new contract. Although the contract has expired, the Allenwood factory needs the supplies to keep the factory operating. Since these parts for seating are unique to Nightingale, I would like to request a justification for other than full and open competition to purchase from Nightingale to meet the current needs of the factory. The total cost of this bridge contract will be under $10,000,000.00.

Due to the unusual and compelling nature of this procurement, UNICOR wishes to waive other than full and open competition and negotiate with the potential vendor.

3. A description of the supplies or services required that meet the agency’s needs (including the estimated dollar amount).

DESCRIPTION: Raw materials to build the seating lines here at LSCI Allenwood. Examples are: VXO, IC2, WXO, MXO, LXO, SXO, CXO, etc. Estimated value of raw materials is $5,838,639.66, see attached excel spreadsheet for detailed information

4. Identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition.

6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements; 10 U.S.C 3304 (c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(1) 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency; 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(2) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(2). LSCI Allenwood is a high producing Office Furniture(seating) factory and we are in the middle of our busy season. We are in the process of putting out a new solicitation but due a new procurement review board process, it is taking more time than anticipated. FPI UNICOR Allenwood has a large volume of orders it must fulfill. In order to meet the mission of the factory, it has to utilize specific parts from Nightingale. Nightingale can supply the unique parts that is needed to fulfill its orders. We would like to implement a bridge contract as an avenue to continue ordering parts from Nightingale so the factory can continue to operate and fulfill orders as scheduled at a fair and reasonable price.

5. A description of effects made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practical including whether a CBD notice was, or will be, publicized as required by Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies.

FAR 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Due to the unusual and compelling nature of this procurement, competition will be waived, Only Nightingale can provide this unique and specific parts and material for this line of seating.

6. A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.

LSCI Allenwood previously had a contract with Nightingale for the needed seating parts, Nightingale has agreed to keep the prices constant from the last contract. Nightingale can provide the unique parts at a fair and reasonable price. This is considered a fair and reasonable price due to past pricing.

7. A description of the market survey conducted and the results or a statement of the reasons a market survey was not conducted.

These chairs are specific to Nightingale and the only company that we can get these parts from..

8. Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition.

This bridge contract is being set up as a 6 month base with 3 each two month options. In anticipation of the solicitation being posted to award a new base with 4 option years, indefinite delivery indefinite quantity for OFG seating line.

9. A listing of sources, if any, that expressed in writing, an interest in the acquisition Nightingale Corporation, 2301 Dixie Road, Mississauga, ON L4Y 1Z9
