This proven infrastructure supports uninterrupted supply continuity and minimizes risk of delay, factors critical to meeting the Veterans’ needs. The contract requires delivery of specialized in-home hospital beds and accessories to the individual VAMCs, with free on-board (FOB) destination, in accordance with the specific delivery instructions contained within the delivery orders. The contractor shall deliver to any VAMC within the United States and its outlying Territories and areas to include the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Alaska, and Hawaii upon issuance of a delivery order. The contractor shall also provide a commercial warranty in accordance with industry standards. The contractor must guarantee their ability to provide an uninterrupted source of supply of the awarded devices to satisfy the Government’s requirements for the effective period of the contract. The current contractor has the required supply chain in place to fulfill orders on a nationwide basis. Onboarding a new vendor to fulfill this requirement and deliver the hospital beds and accessories before the expiration of the current contract is not possible and would introduce delays and increased costs that would prevent timely performance and compromise patient care and safety. A new vendor would require at least 45 days to become fully operational. Therefore, Invacare is the only responsible source uniquely positioned to fulfill orders received from VAMCs in a timely manner. Invacare has provided an uninterrupted source of supply and commercial warranty of the hospital beds and accessories since 2020 and has delivered to locations within the United States and US Territories. From July 2023 through March 2025, under the previously awarded 5-year contract 36C10G18D0018, Invacare provided over in-home hospital beds or accessories to Veterans across the nation, demonstrating the capability to fulfill both standard and large-scale orders. Invacare is immediately capable of meeting all requirements of the contract and has the required capabilities to deliver the necessary products without interruption in supply or degradation of quality of care to the Veteran. Cost Savings: Without a bridge contract, VA would lack a National Contract vehicle to provide in-home hospital beds and accessories to Veterans in the community and VAMCs will be required to purchase the items through local Network Contracting Offices (NCO’s), potentially at open market prices, which would result in major financial loss to the Government and significantly delay the time it takes for the Veteran to receive the clinically required items.

U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE

UNICOR, Federal Prison Industries, Inc.

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION:

Authority Cited: 6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements; 10 U.S.C 3304 (c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(1) 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency; 10 U.S.C. 2304 (c)(2) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a) (2).

1. Identification of the agency and the contracting agency.

Bureau of Prisons - UNICOR - Federal Prison Industries – Allenwood, PA

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.

The UNICOR Factory at LSCI Allenwood manufactures office furniture, specifically seating. This factory needs specific parts to manufacture their product. The needed items for their product were on contract with Nightingale, however, that contract has since expired. Procurement is currently in the process of soliciting and awarding a new contract. Although the contract has expired, the Allenwood factory needs the supplies to keep the factory operating. Since these parts for seating are unique to Nightingale, I would like to request a justification for other than full and open competition to purchase from Nightingale to meet the current needs of the factory. The total cost of this bridge contract will be under $10,000,000.00.

Due to the unusual and compelling nature of this procurement, UNICOR wishes to waive other than full and open competition and negotiate with the potential vendor.

3. A description of the supplies or services required that meet the agency’s needs (including the estimated dollar amount).

DESCRIPTION: Raw materials to build the seating lines here at LSCI Allenwood. Examples are: VXO, IC2, WXO, MXO, LXO, SXO, CXO, etc. Estimated value of raw materials is $5,838,639.66, see attached excel spreadsheet for detailed information

4. Identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition.

6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements; 10 U.S.C 3304 (c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(1) 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency; 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(2) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(2). LSCI Allenwood is a high producing Office Furniture(seating) factory and we are in the middle of our busy season. We are in the process of putting out a new solicitation but due a new procurement review board process, it is taking more time than anticipated. FPI UNICOR Allenwood has a large volume of orders it must fulfill. In order to meet the mission of the factory, it has to utilize specific parts from Nightingale. Nightingale can supply the unique parts that is needed to fulfill its orders. We would like to implement a bridge contract as an avenue to continue ordering parts from Nightingale so the factory can continue to operate and fulfill orders as scheduled at a fair and reasonable price.

5. A description of effects made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practical including whether a CBD notice was, or will be, publicized as required by Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies.

FAR 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Due to the unusual and compelling nature of this procurement, competition will be waived, Only Nightingale can provide this unique and specific parts and material for this line of seating.

6. A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.

LSCI Allenwood previously had a contract with Nightingale for the needed seating parts, Nightingale has agreed to keep the prices constant from the last contract. Nightingale can provide the unique parts at a fair and reasonable price. This is considered a fair and reasonable price due to past pricing.

7. A description of the market survey conducted and the results or a statement of the reasons a market survey was not conducted.

These chairs are specific to Nightingale and the only company that we can get these parts from..

8. Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition.

This bridge contract is being set up as a 6 month base with 3 each two month options. In anticipation of the solicitation being posted to award a new base with 4 option years, indefinite delivery indefinite quantity for OFG seating line.

U.S. General Services Administration Justification for other than full and open competition (1) Identification of the agency and the contracting activity: General Services Administration (GSA) Public Buildings Service (PBS) Acquisition Project Delivery Contracting Division - West (2) Nature and/or description of the action being approved: Furnish and installation of protest security barriers to provide forced entry protection of building occupants during protest events. (3) A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs (including the estimated value): The services required include comprehensive site preparation and installation of temporary security barriers along the ██████████████████████████████████████ of the Eugene Federal Building. The contractor shall first complete site preparation work at 211 E 7th Ave, Eugene, OR, including removal of one (1) designated tree (approximately 25 feet tall with 30-inch diameter trunk), complete stump grinding to ground level, grading and leveling of a 5-foot by 60-foot sloped turf area, and application of 2-3 inches of medium fir bark. Following site preparation, the contractor shall supply and install an integrated barrier system (barriers must be gravity-based, not permanently affixed to the sidewalk) and relocate approximately ███ of fencing, concrete block style barriers and Jersey style barriers from a warehouse in ████. All work must comply with OSHA, National Electrical Code, and applicable safety standards, with proper handling of any hazardous materials per AHERA/OSHA/EPA requirements. The contractor must comply with GSA Building Security requirements, coordinate with city for right-of-way permits for sidewalk closures, maintain unobstructed emergency access, and ensure all personnel are properly escorted. The contractor shall provide detailed cost breakdowns by discrete work features, weekly progress updates, and a complete closeout package. The government estimated cost for this procurement is ███████ (4) An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition: Unusual and compelling urgency - 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(2): Agencies may contract without providing for full and open competition when the agency’s need for the supplies or services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured, financially or otherwise, unless the agency is permitted to limit the number of sources from which it solicits bids or proposals. (5) A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited: This contractor has furnished and installed this specific type of anti-scaling protest barrier on federal courthouses throughout the country. Furthermore, they have direct experience installing the fencing on the ████ in recent years during major protest events. This is not standard fencing, it takes special hardware at the connections that also requires additional hardware to further secure the connections. Once those connections are complete, concrete barriers weighing several thousand lbs each are placed adjacent to the fencing to prevent the barrier from being toppled over during protest events. All of these construction activities need to be performed 100% complete during a very limited window of opportunity between protest events, something of which this contractor has very specific experience executing.

(6) A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by part 5 and, if not, which exception under part 5 applies: N/A, Using other than full and open competition (see 6.302-2) Unusual and compelling urgency. (7) A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable: GSA will establish that it is a fair and reasonable price by Comparison of the proposed prices to historical prices paid and Comparison of proposed prices with independent Government cost estimates. Historical pricing for similar work was recently executed at the █████████ ████████ (8) A description of the market research conducted (see part 10) and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted: See market research report in file tab 6. (9) Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition, such as: (i) When 6.302 (Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements) is cited for follow-on acquisitions as described in 6.302-1(2)(ii), an estimate of the cost to the Government that would be duplicated and how the estimate was derived. (ii) When 6.302-2(2)(unusual and compelling urgency) is cited, data, estimated cost, or other rationale as to the extent and nature of the harm to the Government. Due to ongoing protests, the Government faces an immediate emergency requiring urgent execution of these services. Without immediate action, there is an imminent and substantial risk of destruction to critical Government property, resulting in significant operational disruption and potential safety hazards. Any unnecessary delay caused by standard competitive procedures would unnecessarily risk severe harm to the Government's mission-critical operations and financial interests. The time-sensitive nature of this emergency necessitates limiting the number of sources to ensure rapid mobilization to prevent unnecessary risk to government property. (10) A listing of the sources, if any, that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition: N/A (Sole Source) (11) A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services required: The Government will perform a technical analysis of the proposal, comparing proposed costs to historical pricing received for similar services and comparing to the Independent government estimate.

(12) Contracting officer certification that the justification is accurate and complete to the best of the contracting officer’s knowledge and belief:

Technical Personnel Justin Schoenberg Henry Huynh

General Services Administration Public Buildings Service Acquisition Management Division Services Acquisition Branch (6P1QC) Emergency Bridge Contract Janitorial and Related Services Sioux City Federal Building and US Courthouse 320 6th Street Sioux City, IA 51101 Justification for Other than Full and Open Competition RFO 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency Nature and/or description of the action being approved. This justification is for an emergency, sole source bridge contract to provide janitorial and related services at the aforementioned location for a period of approximately 1-year, with services April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2027.

This bridge contract will be a firm fixed-price, commercial item, performance-based contract, and will contain no additional option periods. Description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency's needs (including the estimated value). The General Services Administration (GSA) has determined there is a continued need for the provision of janitorial and related services at the subject location. The Contractor shall provide all management, supervision, labor, materials, supplies and equipment necessary to provide custodial and related services as described herein.

The Contractor shall plan, schedule, coordinate, and assure effective performance of all services.

The contractor will provide janitorial and related services in accordance with the requirements of the solicitation. Period of Performance for Bridge Contract: April 1, 2026 - March 31, 2027 Estimated Value of Bridge Contract: *$254,400.36 ($21,200.03/month) *This value was calculated by adding 10% to the current six month extension monthly price ($19,272.75). GSA believes 10% is a fair estimate considering that the Consumer Price Index increased 25% over the last 5 years according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Therefore, it is reasonable to assume the CPI will increase 5% over the next year plus the added risk of 5% due to the urgency of the emergency sole source procurement. Statutory authorit y permitting other than full and open competition. RFO 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency 41 U.S.C. 3304, Use of Noncompetitive Procedures Demonstration the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited. The current contract (47PG0120D0003) for janitorial and related services with Kleane Kare Team LLC (KKT) expires on October 1, 2025.

The procurement team intends to issue a six month extension per

FAR

52.217-8 to ensure continuity of services and allow enough lead time for a new procurement.

Procurement planning for the new contract was underway but is now on hold due to ongoing revisions to PBS's national scope of work.

Until a definitive scope of work is finalized, the procurement team is unable to proceed with soliciting bids or issuing an award. It is anticipated that the new national scope of work will be issued before the start date of the bridge contract, but too late to practically issue a solicitation, evaluate offers, determine fair and reasonableness, issue award, and begin transition services. The procurement team would need six months at minimum to issue an award from the time of receiving the new scope of work.

Once the scope of work is received, the team will resume procurement activities with an anticipated award date of February 1, 2027 for services to start April 1,

2027. This unavoidable delay necessitates the swift issuance of a bridge contract to the incumbent contractor to ensure uninterrupted janitorial and related services at the Sioux City Federal Building and

US

Courthouse.

Given the uncertain timeline for receiving the new scope of work, a sole-source procurement, under the authority of

RFO

6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency, represents the only viable course of action to maintain critical services without interruption. Efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable,_ including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies.

Only the incumbent vendor has the ability to continue services without the need for additional site visits, interstate travel, and phase-in of new employees, equipment, and other items necessary to provide the requested services. AS3-22-221 CLASS JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION PURSUANT TO FAR 6.302-2

1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Procurement, Acquisition and Logistics Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC) 5202 Presidents Court, Suite 103 Frederick, MD 21703

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.: The purpose of this document is to obtain Senior Procurement Executive (SPE) approval for the use of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Urgency, for twelve months, for the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Procurement & Logistics’ Medical Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) – GenZ Transition contractors. Use of this authority will allow the SAC to meet the medical and surgical supply needs of the Department from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023, and provide the time necessary to solicit and award competitive long term contracts in support of the MSPV program. This MSPV-GenZ Transition 2 period of performance (PoP) includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods.

Currently, the VHA manages multiple decentralized firm-fixed-priced (FFP) indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) distribution contracts with Medline Industries, Inc., Concordance Healthcare Solutions, LLC, and Cardinal Health 200, LLC. These MSPV-GenZ Transition contractors provide mission critical medical/surgical supply distribution services in support of VA’s MSPV program for designated Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISN) and VA facilities throughout the United States and Puerto Rico. Additionally, the VA Consolidated Mail Outpatient Pharmacy (CMOP) and Other Government Agencies (OGAs) utilize the VA MSPV program. Current OGAs leveraging this program through established Inter-Agency Agreements (IAAs) are: Indian Health Services, Federal Bureau of Prisons, Department of Health and Human Services, and Department of State.

The estimated value of the proposed transition contract (MSPV-GenZ Transition 2) will be consistent with the prime vendor’s general regional area of responsibility and current VISN support. The estimated not to exceed maximum total value for the current planned prime vendor transition contract is listed below.

Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 3

AS3-22-221 over 800 active ordering officers for MSPV would need to independently procure requirements for their facilities. Additionally, with the loss of allocations and the MSPV Product List, the ordering officers for each VAMC would be in direct competition with one another on the open market to procure requirements, including PPE. Moreover, the management of the Product List, and associated Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs), Basic Ordering Agreements, and Distribution And Pricing Agreements, through the MSPV program addresses critical supply issues, including medical item recalls, filtering out non-Food and Drug Administration (FDA) non-compliant or greymarket items and non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items. Consequently, at this time, there are no other viable, competitively awarded contract(s) established for VA to utilize subsequent to the November 30, 2022 expiration date to ensure the continuity of the MSPV program. As such, implementation of the transition effort is considered urgent due to the magnitude of impact, and being pursued under FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

This class justification and approval (CJ&A) will authorize the awards for this transition effort, enabling the current contractors to continue to meet the needs of the agency from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023. This performance period includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods during which the SAC will go through the process of soliciting and awarding new, competitive contracts in support of VA’s MSPV program. Based upon the most recent integrated master schedule/plan of action and milestones for the competitive action (dtd September 13, 2022), award is expected May 17, 2023, with the first availability to order post the 120-day implementation period of September 27,

2023. The inclusion of option periods allows for flexibility in the event the competitive procurement timeline is able to be streamlined and awarded sooner.

MSPV Gen-Z Transition 2 contracts will maintain SAC capability to satisfy the mission-critical medical and surgical supply needs of the entire VA Healthcare System. The contracts will continue to meet the four following needs: (1) to increase the number of healthcare supplies available to VHA facilities nationwide; (2) to stem the use of non-preferred sources and contracting methods (example: Government Purchase Card (GPC) over micro-purchase threshold, local/regional contracts, etc.); (3) to increase cost savings and best pricing obtained by leveraging volume; and (4) to generate increased Veteran-owned business opportunities.

3. Description of Supplies or Services: VA, through the VHA and SAC, administers the MSPV Program, MSPV Supply BPAs and MSPV Gen-Z Transition distribution contracts for the supply and distribution of medical and surgical supplies across VHA facilities for the care of veterans. The MSPV program is based on standard commercial practices and enables facilities to reduce inventory holding cost and streamline delivery and distribution tasks within the facility. The national program is mandatory for all VAMCs in accordance with VHA Directive 1761, dated December 30, 2020 (valid through recertification date of December 31, 2025) and was developed as the key element in VA’s integrated healthcare supply chain improvement initiative, and was designed to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and patient safety, because VA lacked sufficient internal capability to warehouse, coordinate deliveries, and consolidate supply stores. The MSPV Gen-Z Transition contracts afford VA critical benefits not available through other contract methodologies, including traditional single source supply contracts, and establishes a national strategic sourcing solution that combines a Government provided capability for ordering a wide range of medical, surgical, dental, laboratory, and environmental medical supplies via a product list with electronic cataloging and ordering capability. The MSPV Product List consists of approxima ely 70,000 supply items, 65 percent of which are supplied by Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 4

AS3-22-221

Services Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses while overall a total of 72 percent are provided by Small Businesses.

4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition: The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2) as implemented by FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

5. A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited: a. Without the award of the MSPV Gen-Z Transition 2 contracts prior to November 30, 2022, VA would lack the ability to obtain critical medical and surgical materials and equipment to support in-patient care and basic operating room procedures for all healthcare facilities. b. The work performed is integral to VA’s mission of delivering healthcare services to the approximately nine (9) million Veterans currently receiving care through our nation’s VA healthcare system. VHA requires a comprehensive contract vehicle for obtaining critical medical supplies for patient care, managing utilization and maintaining spend under management. c. VA will suffer direct financial and operational injury and mission-loss across the MSPV program. VA’s efficient, cost-effective, just-in- time ordering and distribution processes will be severely hindered as facilities will revert to non-preferred contract methods as occurred before the introduction of the national MSPV program in 2005. A program lapse would require approximately 2,000 contracting staff to attempt to process nearly 600,000 formal contracting actions (in addition to their existing workload) annually, via inefficient, ineffective, and frequently duplicative contracting actions and GPC purchases, which entail more than five times the workload burden of the MSPV ordering method. VA will also lose essential allocations of PPE necessary to support VAMCs due to supply chain disruptions created by the COVID-19 pandemic. If these allocations cannot be transferred to another Prime Vendor capable of warehousing and distributing them effectively, VAMCs will not be able to safely deliver patient care. d. No other contractors currently have the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption of or degradation to quality of care upon MSPV Gen-Z Transition contract expiration. Under the proposed contract action, VA’s healthcare facilities will be able to immediately procure their required supplies using the Government-sourced MSPV Product List. e. Failure to properly account for or make correct decisions regarding continued distribution of necessary supplies while simultaneously monitoring the full supply chain spectrum for any critical issues (i.e. medical item recalls, filtering - out non-FDA non-compliant or grey-market items or non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items) would rapidly undermine the safety and efficiency of VHA patient care.

Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 5

AS3-22-221 f. VA’s promise to Veterans, implemented through the Maintaining Internal Systems and Strengthening Integrated Outside Networks Act (MISSION Act) of 2018, may be compromised as VA’s ability to provide Veterans with an excellent healthcare experience and delivery of the right care, at the right time, at the right place, may be impacted. Ensuring that covered veterans do not experience a lapse in care resulting from errors or delays by the Department, its contractors, or an unusual or excessive burden in accessing hospital care, medical services, or extended care services, is a priority. g. Even if VA could perform and sustain the above referenced actions, VA does not have sufficient infrastructure to stock and distribute the required quantity of medical supplies in all locations.

6. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by FAR Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies: VA met its original intent to fully compete and award a competitive action prior to the expiration of MSPV-NG Bridge contracts in the award of MSPV 2.0. Due to extenuating circumstances, and the COFC decision/injunction, competitive award of any temporary solution comparable to MSPV 2.0 is not feasible before the expiration of the MSPV Gen-Z Transition contracts on November 30, 2022. The current long-term competitive MSPV-GenZ procurement action is in the pre-solicitation phase with award not projected until mid- calendar year 2023, as discussed in Section 2 above. The need for mandatory MSPV distribution services is immediate and a lack of comparable services would cause irreparable harm to VA’s mission to provide Veteran care.

VA has also fully considered FAR 6.302-2(c)(2), which requires VA to “…request offers from as many potential sources as is practicable under the circumstances.” As stated above, VA is not aware of any other contractor(s) who currently have the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or EDI in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption or degradation to quality of care upon current MSPV contract expiration. Obtaining competition for this requirement is not feasible given the time required to complete a competitive action of this scope.

7. A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable: In efforts to increase competition in procurement of the 70,000+ unique supplies for distribution to all VHA facilities located in the United States (US) and all US Territories, VHA issued twentythree RFQs for the acquisition of the consumable commodities in support of the MSPV Program catalog on a tiered evaluation basis. These RFQs were set-aside based on an order of priority to maximize SDVOSB and VOSB participation. Likewise, the SAC issued RFP 36C10G19R0022, for the MSPV 2.0 Prime Vendor distribution requirement as a partial setaside, to maximize the participation of SDVOSB, VOSB, and other small business concerns. Prior to the close of RFP 36C10G19R0050, a bid protest was filed challenging the unrestricted basis, for full and open competition, of the acquisition. This protest was sustained, and in performing corrective action, the SAC amended RFP 36C10G19R0050 to incorporate small business set-asides for line items associated with multiple VISNs for small business concerns using a tiered evaluation approach. Considering this procurement history, the SAC is currently conducting market research through vendor engagement and RFI postings, to produce a comprehensive, competitively awarded long-term solution.

In meeting the healthcare needs of the inmate population, the BOP provides essential medical, dental, and mental health services to Federal inmates. When a medical need arises that cannot be provided by the institution medical staff, referrals are made to community-based medical providers. These services include Inpatient/Outpatient Facility and Physician services, as well as Outpatient Institution Services of Dentist, Dietician, Pharmacist, and Optometrist. The services will be procured by purchase orders. The proposed performance period will be from March 1, 2026, through March 31, 2026. Estimated value of requirement is $250,000.00.

FCI Cumberland's comprehensive medical contract has expired, and this ensures continuity of care while a new multi-year agreement is negotiated by the Field Acquisition Office. This interim acquisition is necessary pending competitive award of a CMS contract. The incumbent contractor continues to provide the necessary medical services through their established network of local medical facilities and physicians. The immediate availability of community-based health care services is critical to avoid any disruption in obtaining the necessary medical services and to ensure the orderly operation of the institutions. In an effort to maintain continuity of care, the Government has determined that it is in the best interest to continue to utilize ACH who can provide the required medical services without delay. EVT, Inc. is the only provider capable of performing without onboarding delays, training requirements, or credentialing gaps, and can immediately fulfill the full scope of perfusionist services. The estimated value for the six-month base period is $177,430.00.

EVT, Inc. is already performing at the facility, is fully trained in the ALMVAMC clinical environment, and meets all competency standards required by the VA, CDC, Department of Health, and The Joint Commission. EVT’s personnel can continue services without delay, making them the only practical and responsible source capable of meeting the urgent requirement.

NON COMPETITIVE MEMORANDUM FOR SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION ACTIONS

IAW FAR 13.101-3(b)

1. REQUIRING AGENCY - DOJ/Bureau of Prisons, FCI Cumberland

2. NATURE/DESCRIPTION OF ACTION BEING APPROVED - Sole source acquisition

3. DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY'S NEEDS As part of the mission of the institution, comprehensive medical services are provided to the inmate population. In meeting the healthcare needs of the inmate population, the BOP provides essential medical, dental, and mental health services to Federal inmates. When a medical need arises that cannot be provided by the institution medical staff, referrals are made to community-based medical providers. These services include Inpatient/Outpatient Facility and Physician services, as well as Outpatient Institution Services of Dentist, Dietician, Pharmacist, and Optometrist. The services will be procured by purchase orders. The proposed performance period will be from June 1, 2026, through June 30, 2026. Estimated value of requirement is $160,000.00.

4. IDENTIFICATION OF STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION - 41 U.S.C. 253; 41 U.S.C. 1901(e)

5. DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR'S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE

NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED:

American Correctional Healthcare, Inc (ACH) is the incumbent and has agreed to continue at the previous negotiated contracted rates. FCI Cumberland's comprehensive medical contract has expired, and this ensures continuity of care while a new multi-year agreement is negotiated by the Field Acquisition Office. This interim acquisition is necessary pending competitive award of a CMS contract. The incumbent contractor continues to provide the necessary medical services through their established network of local medical facilities and physicians. The immediate availability of community-based health care services is critical to avoid any disruption in obtaining the necessary medical services and to ensure the orderly operation of the institutions. In an effort to maintain continuity of care, the Government has determined that it is in the best interest to continue to utilize ACH who can provide the required medical services without delay. This has been determined to be fair and reasonable, and in the Government's best interest. Their established medical network ensures the institution's medical needs are fulfilled and their network of medical service providers alleviates delay and disruption of the overall mission of basic and emergency medical care. Any delay could lead to serious injury to the Government, as it would greatly impact our medical mission, patient care, and could cause operational disruptions to the inmates. While market research has indicated that comprehensive medical services are commonly available in the commercial marketplace and has identified several vendors capable of meeting the Government's needs, ACH, as the incumbent, is the only provider able to ensure seamless service delivery without any lapse in performance. No other sources with the ability to provide services immediately, with no lapse in service, have expressed written interest in this acquisition.

I hereby certify that the supporting data provided by the technical and requirements personnel that form the basis for this justification are certified as complete and accurate to the best of my knowledge and belief.

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION SECTION 1: IDENTIFICATION OF THE AGENCY AND THE CONTRACTING ACTIVITY

Department of State Contracting Activity ☐ Office of Acquisitions Management ☐ Foreign Service Institute ☐ Office of Foreign Missions ☐ U.S. Mission to the United Nations ☒ Overseas Post U.S. Embassy Rome, Italy Requiring Activity U.S. Embassy in Rome - GSO

SECTION 2: NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING APPROVED

Approval is requested to solicit and award, on a sole-source basis, an IDIQ contract to Queen Limousine for transportation services with drivers in support of a senior high-level USG VIP visit to Italy, as described in Section 3, on behalf of the Requiring Activity.

The authority to act under this Class Justification and Approval (J&A) expires on February 28, 2026.

This action will result in a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract.

SECTION 3: DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY'S NEEDS

The Embassy requires transportation services with drivers to support a Senior high-level USG VIP visit in connection with the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympic Games.

Services Estimated Quantity Estimated Period of Performance Transportation Services with Drivers 190 Vehicles 20 January - 15 February The estimated value for the entire period of performance is estimated at $7,584,597.43.

Task orders will be issued as required to meet operational needs and security requirements.

The contractor shall provide high-quality vehicles and drivers and operate with established, robust internal processes for financial management, quality assurance, and operational oversight to ensure all aspects of contract execution are properly monitored and controlled.

SECTION 4: IDENTIFICATION OF THE STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 41 USC 3304, as implemented by FAR 6.3 and substantiated by the following:

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE ☒ FAR 6.103-2 – Unusual and compelling urgency.

SECTION 5: DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED

The contractor’s unique qualifications and expertise are essential due to the scale and complexity of the event, the specific requirements to be met, and the contractor’s demonstrated experience and capacity to manage such services effectively.

This assessment is further supported by the last-minute notification of VIP travel, the stringent security and operational standards to be met, and the overall critical nature of the required services, which creates an unusual and compelling urgency.

These unique senior high-level USG VIP travel requirements result in only a single, or a very limited number of, responsible sources capable of providing the required level of operational support. The proposed contractor can meet these requirements due to a strong record of past performance on similar projects.

SECTION 6. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS WERE SOLICITED FROM AS MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE, INCLUDING WHETHER A NOTICE WAS OR WILL BE PUBLICIZED AS REQUIRED BY FAR SUBPART 5.2 AND, IF NOT, WHICH EXCEPTION UNDER FAR 5.202 APPLIES A formal synopsis of the proposed procurement was not published on SAM.gov because this contract action is being made under the conditions described in FAR 6.103-2, which allows for exceptions due to unusual and compelling urgency. Market research identified a few other vendors; however, none demonstrated the experience or capacity to manage operational services of this scale.

SECTION 7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST TO THE GOVERNMENT IS FAIR AND REASONABLE The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to the Government of the services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable based on: o Rates from prior similar events SECTION 8. DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED (SEE PART 10) AND THE RESULTS OR A STATEMENT OF THE REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED This event is attended by both official and unofficial representatives from around the world. Most services have already been secured, and costs increase significantly during this period, further limiting the number of vendors capable of meeting the Embassy’s transportation requirements.

The short notice, high demand, and security-sensitive nature of the requirement have limited the ability to conduct full and open market research.

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE SECTION 9. ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN

COMPETITION

The unique requirements associated with senior high-level USG VIP travel, combined with security considerations and the operational environment of the event, limit the Government’s ability to conduct a full and open competition.

The proposed contractor possesses unique qualifications that meet the Government’s security and logistical requirements. Any delay in the award may result in the unavailability of qualified transportation resources.

SECTION 10. LISTING OF THE SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED, IN WRITING, AN INTEREST

IN THE ACQUISITION

MTM Italia Srl expressed interest in providing these services. MTM Italia Srl does not, however, currently possess the experience required to support such a complex, high-profile assignment with stringent security and logistical standards.

Furthermore, due to the urgency of the requirement and the limited time available before the event, there is insufficient time to onboard and prepare a new contractor to meet the complex operational demands. Attempting to do so would pose significant risks to the successful execution of the event and could compromise both security and mission objectives.

SECTION 11. STATEMENT OF THE ACTIONS, IF ANY, THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO REMOVE OR

OVERCOME ANY BARRIERS TO COMPETITION BEFORE ANY SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITION FOR THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED

The Government recognizes the importance of fostering full and open competition for future acquisitions of similar services. The unique operational environment connected with the event, characterized by extreme demand, early block allocation, and security-driven constraints, has significantly limited the Government’ s ability to conduct meaningful competition in the immediate term.

AS3-22-221 CLASS JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION PURSUANT TO FAR 6.302-2

1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Procurement, Acquisition and Logistics Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC) 5202 Presidents Court, Suite 103 Frederick, MD 21703

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.: The purpose of this document is to obtain Senior Procurement Executive (SPE) approval for the use of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Urgency, for twelve months, for the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Procurement & Logistics’ Medical Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) – GenZ Transition contractors. Use of this authority will allow the SAC to meet the medical and surgical supply needs of the Department from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023, and provide the time necessary to solicit and award competitive long term contracts in support of the MSPV program. This MSPV-GenZ Transition 2 period of performance (PoP) includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods.

Currently, the VHA manages multiple decentralized firm-fixed-priced (FFP) indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) distribution contracts with Medline Industries, Inc., Concordance Healthcare Solutions, LLC, and Cardinal Health 200, LLC. These MSPV-GenZ Transition contractors provide mission critical medical/surgical supply distribution services in support of VA’s MSPV program for designated Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISN) and VA facilities throughout the United States and Puerto Rico. Additionally, the VA Consolidated Mail Outpatient Pharmacy (CMOP) and Other Government Agencies (OGAs) utilize the VA MSPV program. Current OGAs leveraging this program through established Inter-Agency Agreements (IAAs) are: Indian Health Services, Federal Bureau of Prisons, Department of Health and Human Services, and Department of State.

The estimated value of the proposed transition contract (MSPV-GenZ Transition 2) will be consistent with the prime vendor’s general regional area of responsibility and current VISN support. The estimated not to exceed maximum total value for the current planned prime vendor transition contract is listed below.

Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 3

AS3-22-221 over 800 active ordering officers for MSPV would need to independently procure requirements for their facilities. Additionally, with the loss of allocations and the MSPV Product List, the ordering officers for each VAMC would be in direct competition with one another on the open market to procure requirements, including PPE. Moreover, the management of the Product List, and associated Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs), Basic Ordering Agreements, and Distribution And Pricing Agreements, through the MSPV program addresses critical supply issues, including medical item recalls, filtering out non-Food and Drug Administration (FDA) non-compliant or greymarket items and non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items. Consequently, at this time, there are no other viable, competitively awarded contract(s) established for VA to utilize subsequent to the November 30, 2022 expiration date to ensure the continuity of the MSPV program. As such, implementation of the transition effort is considered urgent due to the magnitude of impact, and being pursued under FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

This class justification and approval (CJ&A) will authorize the awards for this transition effort, enabling the current contractors to continue to meet the needs of the agency from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023. This performance period includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods during which the SAC will go through the process of soliciting and awarding new, competitive contracts in support of VA’s MSPV program. Based upon the most recent integrated master schedule/plan of action and milestones for the competitive action (dtd September 13, 2022), award is expected May 17, 2023, with the first availability to order post the 120-day implementation period of September 27,

2023. The inclusion of option periods allows for flexibility in the event the competitive procurement timeline is able to be streamlined and awarded sooner.

MSPV Gen-Z Transition 2 contracts will maintain SAC capability to satisfy the mission-critical medical and surgical supply needs of the entire VA Healthcare System. The contracts will continue to meet the four following needs: (1) to increase the number of healthcare supplies available to VHA facilities nationwide; (2) to stem the use of non-preferred sources and contracting methods (example: Government Purchase Card (GPC) over micro-purchase threshold, local/regional contracts, etc.); (3) to increase cost savings and best pricing obtained by leveraging volume; and (4) to generate increased Veteran-owned business opportunities.

3. Description of Supplies or Services: VA, through the VHA and SAC, administers the MSPV Program, MSPV Supply BPAs and MSPV Gen-Z Transition distribution contracts for the supply and distribution of medical and surgical supplies across VHA facilities for the care of veterans. The MSPV program is based on standard commercial practices and enables facilities to reduce inventory holding cost and streamline delivery and distribution tasks within the facility. The national program is mandatory for all VAMCs in accordance with VHA Directive 1761, dated December 30, 2020 (valid through recertification date of December 31, 2025) and was developed as the key element in VA’s integrated healthcare supply chain improvement initiative, and was designed to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and patient safety, because VA lacked sufficient internal capability to warehouse, coordinate deliveries, and consolidate supply stores. The MSPV Gen-Z Transition contracts afford VA critical benefits not available through other contract methodologies, including traditional single source supply contracts, and establishes a national strategic sourcing solution that combines a Government provided capability for ordering a wide range of medical, surgical, dental, laboratory, and environmental medical supplies via a product list with electronic cataloging and ordering capability. The MSPV Product List consists of approxima ely 70,000 supply items, 65 percent of which are supplied by Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 4

AS3-22-221

Services Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses while overall a total of 72 percent are provided by Small Businesses.

4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition: The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2) as implemented by FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

5. A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited: a. Without the award of the MSPV Gen-Z Transition 2 contracts prior to November 30, 2022, VA would lack the ability to obtain critical medical and surgical materials and equipment to support in-patient care and basic operating room procedures for all healthcare facilities. b. The work performed is integral to VA’s mission of delivering healthcare services to the approximately nine (9) million Veterans currently receiving care through our nation’s VA healthcare system. VHA requires a comprehensive contract vehicle for obtaining critical medical supplies for patient care, managing utilization and maintaining spend under management. c. VA will suffer direct financial and operational injury and mission-loss across the MSPV program. VA’s efficient, cost-effective, just-in- time ordering and distribution processes will be severely hindered as facilities will revert to non-preferred contract methods as occurred before the introduction of the national MSPV program in 2005. A program lapse would require approximately 2,000 contracting staff to attempt to process nearly 600,000 formal contracting actions (in addition to their existing workload) annually, via inefficient, ineffective, and frequently duplicative contracting actions and GPC purchases, which entail more than five times the workload burden of the MSPV ordering method. VA will also lose essential allocations of PPE necessary to support VAMCs due to supply chain disruptions created by the COVID-19 pandemic. If these allocations cannot be transferred to another Prime Vendor capable of warehousing and distributing them effectively, VAMCs will not be able to safely deliver patient care. d. No other contractors currently have the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption of or degradation to quality of care upon MSPV Gen-Z Transition contract expiration. Under the proposed contract action, VA’s healthcare facilities will be able to immediately procure their required supplies using the Government-sourced MSPV Product List. e. Failure to properly account for or make correct decisions regarding continued distribution of necessary supplies while simultaneously monitoring the full supply chain spectrum for any critical issues (i.e. medical item recalls, filtering - out non-FDA non-compliant or grey-market items or non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items) would rapidly undermine the safety and efficiency of VHA patient care.

Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 5

AS3-22-221 f. Ensuring that covered veterans do not experience a lapse in care resulting from errors or delays by the Department, its contractors, or an unusual or excessive burden in accessing hospital care, medical services, or extended care services, is a priority. g. Even if VA could perform and sustain the above referenced actions, VA does not have sufficient infrastructure to stock and distribute the required quantity of medical supplies in all locations.

6. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by FAR Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies: VA met its original intent to fully compete and award a competitive action prior to the expiration of MSPV-NG Bridge contracts in the award of MSPV 2.0. Due to extenuating circumstances, and the COFC decision/injunction, competitive award of any temporary solution comparable to MSPV 2.0 is not feasible before the expiration of the MSPV Gen-Z Transition contracts on November 30, 2022. The current long-term competitive MSPV-GenZ procurement action is in the pre-solicitation phase with award not projected until mid- calendar year 2023, as discussed in Section 2 above. The need for mandatory MSPV distribution services is immediate and a lack of comparable services would cause irreparable harm to VA’s mission to provide Veteran care.

VA has also fully considered FAR 6.302-2(c)(2), which requires VA to “…request offers from as many potential sources as is practicable under the circumstances.” As stated above, VA is not aware of any other contractor(s) who currently have the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or EDI in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption or degradation to quality of care upon current MSPV contract expiration. Obtaining competition for this requirement is not feasible given the time required to complete a competitive action of this scope.

7. A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable: In efforts to increase competition in procurement of the 70,000+ unique supplies for distribution to all VHA facilities located in the United States (US) and all US Territories, VHA issued twentythree RFQs for the acquisition of the consumable commodities in support of the MSPV Program catalog on a tiered evaluation basis. These RFQs were set-aside based on an order of priority to maximize SDVOSB and VOSB participation. Likewise, the SAC issued RFP 36C10G19R0022, for the MSPV 2.0 Prime Vendor distribution requirement as a partial setaside, to maximize the participation of SDVOSB, VOSB, and other small business concerns. Prior to the close of RFP 36C10G19R0050, a bid protest was filed challenging the unrestricted basis, for full and open competition, of the acquisition. This protest was sustained, and in performing corrective action, the SAC amended RFP 36C10G19R0050 to incorporate small business set-asides for line items associated with multiple VISNs for small business concerns using a tiered evaluation approach. Considering this procurement history, the SAC is currently conducting market research through vendor engagement and RFI postings, to produce a comprehensive, competitively awarded long-term solution.

IAW FAR 13.101-3(b)

3. DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY’S NEEDS As part of the mission of the institution, comprehensive medical services are provided to the inmate population. In meeting the healthcare needs of the inmate population, the BOP provides essential medical, dental, and mental health services to Federal inmates. When a medical need arises that cannot be provided by the institution medical staff, referrals are made to community-based medical providers. These services include Inpatient/Outpatient Facility and Physician services, as well as Outpatient Institution Services of Dentist, Dietician, Pharmacist, and Optometrist. The services will be procured by purchase orders. The proposed performance period will be from May 1, 2026, through May 30, 2026. Estimated value of requirement is $250,000.00.

NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED:

American Correctional Healthcare, Inc (ACH) is the incumbent and has agreed to continue at the previous negotiated contracted rates. FCI Cumberland’s comprehensive medical contract has expired, and this ensures continuity of care while a new multi-year agreement is negotiated by the Field Acquisition Office. This interim acquisition is necessary pending competitive award of a CMS contract. The incumbent contractor continues to provide the necessary medical services through their established network of local medical facilities and physicians. The immediate availability of community-based health care services is critical to avoid any disruption in obtaining the necessary medical services and to ensure the orderly operation of the institutions. In an effort to maintain continuity of care, the Government has determined that it is in the best interest to continue to utilize ACH who can provide the required medical services without delay. U.S. Department of Justice Federal Bureau of Prisons Administration Division Field Acquisition Office Grand Prairie, Texas 75051 January 13, 2026

MEMORANDUM FOR CONTRACT FILE

FROM: Luke Bonner, Contracting Officer SUBJECT: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition – Emergency Asbestos Demolition This acquisition is for emergency asbestos demolition and debris removal services for seven staff housing structures destroyed during a tornado event at the Federal Correctional Institution in Marion, IL. The requirement includes wet demolition of remaining structural elements, removal of asbestos-containing debris, cleanup of scattered ACM-contaminated materials, mastic removal, asbestos air monitoring, and EPA-required demolition notifications. These services are necessary to restore the site to a safe condition and prevent further environmental and occupational exposure. This procurement is conducted under FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency, as delay in award would result in serious injury to the Government. Environmental inspection confirmed widespread asbestos-containing materials dispersed across the site, exposed to weather, and posing an immediate health hazard. ACM debris cannot be maintained in adequately wet condition if left in place, increasing airborne fiber risk and potential regulatory noncompliance. Delays would also impede access to the area, increase environmental liability, and allow weather to further spread contaminated debris. Full and open competition would introduce delays incompatible with the urgent need to mitigate hazardous material exposure. Because the total value of this acquisition is below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold, FAR 12.102(a) applies. In accordance with FAR Part 12, the Contracting Officer has determined that only one source is available to meet the Government’s urgent need. Limited-scope market research was conducted to identify firms capable of immediate mobilization. Summit Environmental Services, Inc. was the only contractor able to provide licensed asbestos abatement personnel, mobilize immediately, perform wet demolition and ACM debris removal in compliance with EPA NESHAP requirements, conduct asbestos air monitoring, and provide required EPA notifications. Other vendors contacted were unable to meet the immediate response timeframe. Competition was therefore restricted only to the extent necessary to address the unusual and compelling urgency. The Contracting Officer will determine the price fair and reasonable through comparison to historical pricing, independent estimates, and evaluation of labor, equipment, and disposal costs typical for emergency ACM abatement. This emergency action is limited strictly to immediate hazard mitigation; future reconstruction or follow-on environmental work will be competed to the maximum extent practicable.

AS3-22-221 CLASS JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION PURSUANT TO FAR 6.302-2

1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Procurement, Acquisition and Logistics Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC) 5202 Presidents Court, Suite 103 Frederick, MD 21703

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.: The purpose of this document is to obtain Senior Procurement Executive (SPE) approval for the use of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Urgency, for twelve months, for the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Procurement & Logistics’ Medical Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) – GenZ Transition contractors. Use of this authority will allow the SAC to meet the medical and surgical supply needs of the Department from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023, and provide the time necessary to solicit and award competitive long term contracts in support of the MSPV program. This MSPV-GenZ Transition 2 period of performance (PoP) includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods.

Currently, the VHA manages multiple decentralized firm-fixed-priced (FFP) indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) distribution contracts with Medline Industries, Inc., Concordance Healthcare Solutions, LLC, and Cardinal Health 200, LLC. These MSPV-GenZ Transition contractors provide mission critical medical/surgical supply distribution services in support of VA’s MSPV program for designated Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISN) and VA facilities throughout the United States and Puerto Rico. Additionally, the VA Consolidated Mail Outpatient Pharmacy (CMOP) and Other Government Agencies (OGAs) utilize the VA MSPV program. Current OGAs leveraging this program through established Inter-Agency Agreements (IAAs) are: Indian Health Services, Federal Bureau of Prisons, Department of Health and Human Services, and Department of State.

The estimated value of the proposed transition contract (MSPV-GenZ Transition 2) will be consistent with the prime vendor’s general regional area of responsibility and current VISN support. The estimated not to exceed maximum total value for the current planned prime vendor transition contract is listed below.

Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 3

AS3-22-221 over 800 active ordering officers for MSPV would need to independently procure requirements for their facilities. Additionally, with the loss of allocations and the MSPV Product List, the ordering officers for each VAMC would be in direct competition with one another on the open market to procure requirements, including PPE. Moreover, the management of the Product List, and associated Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs), Basic Ordering Agreements, and Distribution And Pricing Agreements, through the MSPV program addresses critical supply issues, including medical item recalls, filtering out non-Food and Drug Administration (FDA) non-compliant or greymarket items and non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items. Consequently, at this time, there are no other viable, competitively awarded contract(s) established for VA to utilize subsequent to the November 30, 2022 expiration date to ensure the continuity of the MSPV program. As such, implementation of the transition effort is considered urgent due to the magnitude of impact, and being pursued under FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

This class justification and approval (CJ&A) will authorize the awards for this transition effort, enabling the current contractors to continue to meet the needs of the agency from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023. This performance period includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods during which the SAC will go through the process of soliciting and awarding new, competitive contracts in support of VA’s MSPV program. Based upon the most recent integrated master schedule/plan of action and milestones for the competitive action (dtd September 13, 2022), award is expected May 17, 2023, with the first availability to order post the 120-day implementation period of September 27,

2023. The inclusion of option periods allows for flexibility in the event the competitive procurement timeline is able to be streamlined and awarded sooner.

MSPV Gen-Z Transition 2 contracts will maintain SAC capability to satisfy the mission-critical medical and surgical supply needs of the entire VA Healthcare System. The contracts will continue to meet the four following needs: (1) to increase the number of healthcare supplies available to VHA facilities nationwide; (2) to stem the use of non-preferred sources and contracting methods (example: Government Purchase Card (GPC) over micro-purchase threshold, local/regional contracts, etc.); (3) to increase cost savings and best pricing obtained by leveraging volume; and (4) to generate increased Veteran-owned business opportunities.

3. Description of Supplies or Services: VA, through the VHA and SAC, administers the MSPV Program, MSPV Supply BPAs and MSPV Gen-Z Transition distribution contracts for the supply and distribution of medical and surgical supplies across VHA facilities for the care of veterans. The MSPV program is based on standard commercial practices and enables facilities to reduce inventory holding cost and streamline delivery and distribution tasks within the facility. The national program is mandatory for all VAMCs in accordance with VHA Directive 1761, dated December 30, 2020 (valid through recertification date of December 31, 2025) and was developed as the key element in VA’s integrated healthcare supply chain improvement initiative, and was designed to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and patient safety, because VA lacked sufficient internal capability to warehouse, coordinate deliveries, and consolidate supply stores. The MSPV Gen-Z Transition contracts afford VA critical benefits not available through other contract methodologies, including traditional single source supply contracts, and establishes a national strategic sourcing solution that combines a Government provided capability for ordering a wide range of medical, surgical, dental, laboratory, and environmental medical supplies via a product list with electronic cataloging and ordering capability. The MSPV Product List consists of approxima ely 70,000 supply items, 65 percent of which are supplied by Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 4

AS3-22-221

Services Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses while overall a total of 72 percent are provided by Small Businesses.

4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition: The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2) as implemented by FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

5. A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited: a. Without the award of the MSPV Gen-Z Transition 2 contracts prior to November 30, 2022, VA would lack the ability to obtain critical medical and surgical materials and equipment to support in-patient care and basic operating room procedures for all healthcare facilities. b. The work performed is integral to VA’s mission of delivering healthcare services to the approximately nine (9) million Veterans currently receiving care through our nation’s VA healthcare system. VHA requires a comprehensive contract vehicle for obtaining critical medical supplies for patient care, managing utilization and maintaining spend under management. c. VA will suffer direct financial and operational injury and mission-loss across the MSPV program. VA’s efficient, cost-effective, just-in- time ordering and distribution processes will be severely hindered as facilities will revert to non-preferred contract methods as occurred before the introduction of the national MSPV program in 2005. A program lapse would require approximately 2,000 contracting staff to attempt to process nearly 600,000 formal contracting actions (in addition to their existing workload) annually, via inefficient, ineffective, and frequently duplicative contracting actions and GPC purchases, which entail more than five times the workload burden of the MSPV ordering method. VA will also lose essential allocations of PPE necessary to support VAMCs due to supply chain disruptions created by the COVID-19 pandemic. If these allocations cannot be transferred to another Prime Vendor capable of warehousing and distributing them effectively, VAMCs will not be able to safely deliver patient care. d. No other contractors currently have the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption of or degradation to quality of care upon MSPV Gen-Z Transition contract expiration. Under the proposed contract action, VA’s healthcare facilities will be able to immediately procure their required supplies using the Government-sourced MSPV Product List. e. Failure to properly account for or make correct decisions regarding continued distribution of necessary supplies while simultaneously monitoring the full supply chain spectrum for any critical issues (i.e. medical item recalls, filtering - out non-FDA non-compliant or grey-market items or non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items) would rapidly undermine the safety and efficiency of VHA patient care.

Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 5

AS3-22-221 f. VA’s promise to Veterans, implemented through the Maintaining Internal Systems and Strengthening Integrated Outside Networks Act (MISSION Act) of 2018, may be compromised as VA’s ability to provide Veterans with an excellent healthcare experience and delivery of the right care, at the right time, at the right place, may be impacted. Ensuring that covered veterans do not experience a lapse in care resulting from errors or delays by the Department, its contractors, or an unusual or excessive burden in accessing hospital care, medical services, or extended care services, is a priority. g. Even if VA could perform and sustain the above referenced actions, VA does not have sufficient infrastructure to stock and distribute the required quantity of medical supplies in all locations.

6. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by FAR Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies: VA met its original intent to fully compete and award a competitive action prior to the expiration of MSPV-NG Bridge contracts in the award of MSPV 2.0. Due to extenuating circumstances, and the COFC decision/injunction, competitive award of any temporary solution comparable to MSPV 2.0 is not feasible before the expiration of the MSPV Gen-Z Transition contracts on November 30, 2022. The current long-term competitive MSPV-GenZ procurement action is in the pre-solicitation phase with award not projected until mid- calendar year 2023, as discussed in Section 2 above. The need for mandatory MSPV distribution services is immediate and a lack of comparable services would cause irreparable harm to VA’s mission to provide Veteran care.

VA has also fully considered FAR 6.302-2(c)(2), which requires VA to “…request offers from as many potential sources as is practicable under the circumstances.” As stated above, VA is not aware of any other contractor(s) who currently have the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or EDI in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption or degradation to quality of care upon current MSPV contract expiration. Obtaining competition for this requirement is not feasible given the time required to complete a competitive action of this scope.

7. A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable: In efforts to increase competition in procurement of the 70,000+ unique supplies for distribution to all VHA facilities located in the United States (US) and all US Territories, VHA issued twentythree RFQs for the acquisition of the consumable commodities in support of the MSPV Program catalog on a tiered evaluation basis. These RFQs were set-aside based on an order of priority to maximize SDVOSB and VOSB participation. Likewise, the SAC issued RFP 36C10G19R0022, for the MSPV 2.0 Prime Vendor distribution requirement as a partial setaside, to maximize the participation of SDVOSB, VOSB, and other small business concerns. Prior to the close of RFP 36C10G19R0050, a bid protest was filed challenging the unrestricted basis, for full and open competition, of the acquisition. This protest was sustained, and in performing corrective action, the SAC amended RFP 36C10G19R0050 to incorporate small business set-asides for line items associated with multiple VISNs for small business concerns using a tiered evaluation approach. Considering this procurement history, the SAC is currently conducting market research through vendor engagement and RFI postings, to produce a comprehensive, competitively awarded long-term solution.

Single Source Justification for MPT up to SAT Revision: 02 Acquisition ID# 36C244-26-AP-2263 The RO system is approximately 25 years old and is currently in the planning phase for full replacement. However, until the replacement system is installed and fully operational, the existing system must be maintained in working condition without interruption.

Due to the highly specialized nature of the system, repair services require proprietary parts and technical expertise. Engaging a source other than the OEM would result in unacceptable delays due to the time required to identify, source, and validate compatible parts, as well as ensure adequate technical capability. Such delays would significantly increase the risk of system downtime.

As a result, the Government intends to award a contract to as the only responsible source capable of meeting the urgent requirement within the necessary timeframe.

4. Description of market research conducted and results or statement why it was not conducted: Market research was conducted to identify potential sources capable of providing maintenance and repair services for the RO system at the Pittsburgh VA Medical Center. Multiple large businesses with experience supporting RO systems at other VA Medical Centers were identified and contacted by the requiring activity.

However, due to the age of the system, vendors advised that the system has exceeded its expected service life and recommended complete replacement rather than repair.

The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM),, was also consulted and similarly recommended system replacement. However, unlike other vendors, the OEM confirmed it retains the proprietary knowledge, parts, and technical capability necessary to perform interim repairs and maintenance to sustain system functionality.

Failure to maintain the RO system would result in the inability to operate the Dialysis Department, requiring the Pittsburgh VA Medical Center to suspend dialysis services. This would have a significant adverse impact on patient care, as dialysis is a life-sustaining treatment that must be provided without interruption. Additionally, the Government would incur substantially increased costs associated with outsourcing dialysis services to non-VA facilities.
