7. Actions to Increase Competition:

The MSPV Program Office has implemented its Clinician Driven Strategic Sourcing (CDSS) plan to streamline the procurement and delivery of high-use medical, surgical, dental, select prosthetic, laboratory and facility management supplies throughout VA.

The Program Executive Office (PEO) established its CDSS as a central component of MSPV formulary/catalog development and collaboration across VA, facilitating ongoing improvement of VA’s sourcing of key, high-use medical and surgical supply items. CDSS has increased participation, collaboration, and accountability amongst clinicians 9 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 and clinical specialists who are the stakeholders and possess the knowledge and education of items needed for the highest quality of care for Veterans. To ensure the MSPV program is fully based on a foundation that is rooted in CDSS principles, a plan of action was put in place with collaboration of Executive Leadership from the MSPV PEO, the Medical Supplies Program Office, VHA, VHA Procurement and Logistics Office, VA Office of Acquisition and Logistics, National CPOs, Chief Medical Offices, National Center for Patient Safety, and other key offices as required.

MSPV PEO continues to nationally coordinate with healthcare product supply chain stakeholders, clinicians, clinical specialists and leadership to get buy in and engagement on its comprehensive CDSS strategy. The CDSS process currently collects, monitors and evaluates market research, and conducts its product evaluation and value analysis for best quality products, cost reduction, and streamlined strategic acquisitions.

In efforts to increase competition, for the 49,000 types of supplies for distribution to all VHA facilities located in the United States (US) and all US Territories, VHA issued twenty-three (23) RFQs for the acquisition of the consumable commodities in support of the MSPV Program catalog on a tiered evaluation basis. These RFQs were set-aside based on an order of priority to maximize SDVOSB and VOSB participation. Likewise, the SAC issued RFP 36C10G19R0022, for the MSPV 2.0 Prime Vendor distribution requirement as a partial set-aside, to encourage and maximize the involvement of SDVOSB, VOSB, and other small business concerns. With the cancellation of the initial MSPV 2.0 RFP, the SAC issued RFP 36C10G19R0050, unrestricted, for full and open competition, in accordance with market analysis, in the effort to foster and expand vendor competition. Prior to the close of RFP 36C10G19R0050, a bid protest was filed challenging the unrestricted basis, for full and open competition, of the acquisition. This protest was sustained, requiring corrective action on the part of VA to reexamine its small business set-aside strategy (and adding to the time required to put in place a fully competitive contract solution). In performing corrective action, the SAC amended RFP 36C10G19R0050 to incorporate small business set-asides for CLINs associated with VISNs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 17, and 22 for Small Business concerns using a Tiered Evaluation approach.

8. Market Research:

The market research recently conducted for MSPV 2.0 was utilized for this J&A as it was recently amended and completed in September 2019 and is the most up to date market survey available. In preparation for the continuation of the MSPV program, in 2018 SAC assumed responsibility of awarding the MSPV 2.0 distribution contracts and VHA assumed responsibility of awarding the MSPV 2.0 supply contracts. Two RFIs and a Vendor Industry Engagement Day were conducted in support of MPSV 2.0 distribution market research. The RFls played an essential role in determining the market's ability to meet our basic requirements, while offering insight into vendor availability and capability. 10 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 Market research was conducted to determine the suitability of commercial items, the geographic regions to be competed, and the potential use of SDVOSB or other small business set-asides. This market research establishes that— - The Government’s need may be met by a type of item or service customarily available in the commercial marketplace that would meet the definition of a commercial item in accordance with FAR 10.002.

- Competition for geographic regions should be conducted at the VISN level, with the exception of Puerto Rico (PR), Guam, American Samoa, Virgin Islands, and the Philippines. It was contemplated that Oklahoma (OK) should be competed as a single region with VISN 17 Texas (TX), not as part of VISN 19, since the discontinuity between OK and the rest of the VISN. However, the Integrated Product Team (IPT) made the determination to leave OK within VISN 19 in an effort to maintain VISN continuity of management.

Given that the above market research conducted for MSPV 2.0 has shown that there is a limited number of capable vendors that could fulfill the MSPV 2.0 requirement for VA, none would be able to do so without the sizeable startup period built into MSPV 2.0. Considering this, none of the vendors, outside of incumbents that submitted proposals in response to the MSPV 2.0 RFP, would be able to immediately provide the required distribution services of MSPV.

9. Other Facts:

This unusual and compelling urgency precludes full and open competition and it is of certain that any delay in award of this contract action will result in serious patient safety considerations across the entire VA network to include detrimental financial costs to the Government as a result. Prior to the MSPV-NG contract modification, VA had been unsuccessful in populating the Government master list with a large number of medical/surgical items. After the modification, the additional sourcing flexibility to obtain critical healthcare supplies more closely approximates VHA’s existing best in class pharmaceutical PV program that relies heavily on commercial buying practices and has facilitated the inclusion of more than 15,000 additional items. Given the need for facilities to be able to continue to access the broad listing of medical and surgical supplies realized under the MSPV-NG modification, and given that fair and reasonable prices have been confirmed using commercial cost indices, it is in the best interest of VA to ensure the immediate continued distribution through current MSPV distribution channels (Medical-Surgical PVs) while the SAC and VHA offices continue with the implementation of the MSPV 2.0 distribution and supply acquisitions.

The primary mission of VA is to fulfill President Lincoln's promise “To care for him who shall have borne the battle, and for his widow, and his orphan” by serving and honoring the men and women who are America’s Veterans. We seek to accomplish this mission through our 5 core values of Integrity, Commitment, Advocacy, Respect, and 11 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 Excellence. These “I CARE” values are incorporated in the SAC partnership with the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), to deliver timely medical and surgical products to our Nation’s Veterans through the MSPV-NG Program.

Currently, the MSPV PVs are the only sources serving in the critical role of comprehensive emergency supply response in support of local, regional, or national emergencies or disasters. Additionally, VA supports the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and US Department of Health & Human Services with the delivery of medical supplies and coordination of support missions for response to and recovery from nationally-declared emergencies and disasters. VA accomplishes this requirement through the current regional PVs, who are contractually required to perform a full range of support to healthcare facilities to ensure resiliency, continuity and rapid recovery of healthcare services during disasters and other potential disruptions to healthcare service delivery. Given that VAMCs, and other select federal facilities, are designated FEMA facilities with significant contingency and emergency response roles, a supply chain interruption would not only negatively impact healthcare delivery to our nation’s Veterans and their dependents, but also potentially have a direct, negative impact on the greater public.

Approval of this contract action would directly abate significant negative impact to the Government in terms of monetary cost. However, the far greater negative impact not realized would be the undeniable risk to the overall health, welfare and safety of millions of Veterans. Although every effort was made to compare costs, benefits and all other options to this contract action, no reasonable, timely alternative has been identified.

For the reasons described above, the proposed contract action is urgently needed to ensure the continuity of services of the MSPV program, and the availability of safe clinician required commodities on the catalog for the treatment of our Veterans until MSPV 2.0 is awarded.

1. I recommend that Embassy Kuala Lumpur use other than full and open competition for the acquisition of hotel services for a VVIP Visit held in Kuala Lumpur October 2025 The estimated cost is USD $1,604,275 The minimum guarantee for these services is 826 single hotel room nights.

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.

This is a new contract for services not related to any other current or previous purchase.

3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs.

Hotel services for up to 800 travelers, office space, internet lines, and parking for Senior High Level USG Principal traveling with a delegation inclusive of support elements in: Security, Communications, Logistics and Operations.

4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition.

[ X ] 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2; Unusual and Compelling Urgency; (Based on the available time and urgency of the requirement as detailed below) The VIP visit will be held during October 2025. The visit was only confirmed in mid September

2025. The first travelers will arrive within two weeks of visit notification. The lack of time before US government travelers arrive does not allow enough time for full and open competition.

Security concerns prohibit sufficient advanced notification of VIP travel to allow for sufficient time to conduct full and open competition. The Department of State can only communicate with the staff at Posts abroad when authorization is given due to security concerns. They have an extremely short turnaround time when authorization has been granted for negotiations to commence and site selections to be finalized with both the local vendors and Posts before the actual Senior High Level USG VIP visit occurs. Security and logistical teams make determinations during the site survey as to which hotels are most suitable for the Senior High Level USG VIP and his traveling staff to remain overnight. Unique requirements for communications support are under severe time limitations and always a determining factor in the selection process as its capacity to be augmented to the unique requirements necessary to support certain Senior High Level USG Principals.

Many of the arrangements for hotel and transportation are often not confirmed until just before the actual visit. In addition to supporting a large delegation within a short time frame, last minute and frequent changes of itineraries for supporting personnel often result in significant changes in how Posts work with the vendors. With the exception of a few trips, contracts are not permitted to be signed until the Department of State (Post) has written confirmation from all supporting agencies, which enable collection of funds from said agencies in the event of cancellation. This results in an unusual and compelling urgency in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2.

1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Procurement, Acquisition and Logistics Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC) 5202 Presidents Court, Suite 103 Frederick, MD 21703

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.: The purpose of this document is to obtain Senior Procurement Executive (SPE) approval for the use of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Urgency, for twelve months, for the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Procurement & Logistics’ Medical Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) – GenZ Transition contractors. Use of this authority will allow the SAC to meet the medical and surgical supply needs of the Department from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023, and provide the time necessary to solicit and award competitive long term contracts in support of the MSPV program. This MSPV-GenZ Transition 2 period of performance (PoP) includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods.

Currently, the VHA manages multiple decentralized firm-fixed-priced (FFP) indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) distribution contracts with Medline Industries, Inc., Concordance Healthcare Solutions, LLC, and Cardinal Health 200, LLC. These MSPV-GenZ Transition contractors provide mission critical medical/surgical supply distribution services in support of VA’s MSPV program for designated Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISN) and VA facilities throughout the United States and Puerto Rico. Additionally, the VA Consolidated Mail Outpatient Pharmacy (CMOP) and Other Government Agencies (OGAs) utilize the VA MSPV program. Current OGAs leveraging this program through established Inter-Agency Agreements (IAAs) are: Indian Health Services, Federal Bureau of Prisons, Department of Health and Human Services, and Department of State.

The estimated value of the proposed transition contract (MSPV-GenZ Transition 2) will be consistent with the prime vendor’s general regional area of responsibility and current VISN support. The estimated not to exceed maximum total value for the current planned prime vendor transition contract is listed below.

Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 3

AS3-22-221 over 800 active ordering officers for MSPV would need to independently procure requirements for their facilities. Additionally, with the loss of allocations and the MSPV Product List, the ordering officers for each VAMC would be in direct competition with one another on the open market to procure requirements, including PPE. Moreover, the management of the Product List, and associated Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs), Basic Ordering Agreements, and Distribution And Pricing Agreements, through the MSPV program addresses critical supply issues, including medical item recalls, filtering out non-Food and Drug Administration (FDA) non-compliant or greymarket items and non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items. Consequently, at this time, there are no other viable, competitively awarded contract(s) established for VA to utilize subsequent to the November 30, 2022 expiration date to ensure the continuity of the MSPV program. As such, implementation of the transition effort is considered urgent due to the magnitude of impact, and being pursued under FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

This class justification and approval (CJ&A) will authorize the awards for this transition effort, enabling the current contractors to continue to meet the needs of the agency from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023. This performance period includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods during which the SAC will go through the process of soliciting and awarding new, competitive contracts in support of VA’s MSPV program. Based upon the most recent integrated master schedule/plan of action and milestones for the competitive action (dtd September 13, 2022), award is expected May 17, 2023, with the first availability to order post the 120-day implementation period of September 27,

2023. The inclusion of option periods allows for flexibility in the event the competitive procurement timeline is able to be streamlined and awarded sooner.

MSPV Gen-Z Transition 2 contracts will maintain SAC capability to satisfy the mission-critical medical and surgical supply needs of the entire VA Healthcare System. The contracts will continue to meet the four following needs: (1) to increase the number of healthcare supplies available to VHA facilities nationwide; (2) to stem the use of non-preferred sources and contracting methods (example: Government Purchase Card (GPC) over micro-purchase threshold, local/regional contracts, etc.); (3) to increase cost savings and best pricing obtained by leveraging volume; and (4) to generate increased Veteran-owned business opportunities.

3. Description of Supplies or Services: VA, through the VHA and SAC, administers the MSPV Program, MSPV Supply BPAs and MSPV Gen-Z Transition distribution contracts for the supply and distribution of medical and surgical supplies across VHA facilities for the care of veterans. The MSPV program is based on standard commercial practices and enables facilities to reduce inventory holding cost and streamline delivery and distribution tasks within the facility. The national program is mandatory for all VAMCs in accordance with VHA Directive 1761, dated December 30, 2020 (valid through recertification date of December 31, 2025) and was developed as the key element in VA’s integrated healthcare supply chain improvement initiative, and was designed to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and patient safety, because VA lacked sufficient internal capability to warehouse, coordinate deliveries, and consolidate supply stores. The MSPV Gen-Z Transition contracts afford VA critical benefits not available through other contract methodologies, including traditional single source supply contracts, and establishes a national strategic sourcing solution that combines a Government provided capability for ordering a wide range of medical, surgical, dental, laboratory, and environmental medical supplies via a product list with electronic cataloging and ordering capability. The MSPV Product List consists of approxima ely 70,000 supply items, 65 percent of which are supplied by Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 4

AS3-22-221

Services Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses while overall a total of 72 percent are provided by Small Businesses.

4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition: The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2) as implemented by FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

5. A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited: a. Without the award of the MSPV Gen-Z Transition 2 contracts prior to November 30, 2022, VA would lack the ability to obtain critical medical and surgical materials and equipment to support in-patient care and basic operating room procedures for all healthcare facilities. b. The work performed is integral to VA’s mission of delivering healthcare services to the approximately nine (9) million Veterans currently receiving care through our nation’s VA healthcare system. VHA requires a comprehensive contract vehicle for obtaining critical medical supplies for patient care, managing utilization and maintaining spend under management. c. VA will suffer direct financial and operational injury and mission-loss across the MSPV program. VA’s efficient, cost-effective, just-in- time ordering and distribution processes will be severely hindered as facilities will revert to non-preferred contract methods as occurred before the introduction of the national MSPV program in 2005. A program lapse would require approximately 2,000 contracting staff to attempt to process nearly 600,000 formal contracting actions (in addition to their existing workload) annually, via inefficient, ineffective, and frequently duplicative contracting actions and GPC purchases, which entail more than five times the workload burden of the MSPV ordering method. VA will also lose essential allocations of PPE necessary to support VAMCs due to supply chain disruptions created by the COVID-19 pandemic. If these allocations cannot be transferred to another Prime Vendor capable of warehousing and distributing them effectively, VAMCs will not be able to safely deliver patient care. d. No other contractors currently have the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption of or degradation to quality of care upon MSPV Gen-Z Transition contract expiration. Under the proposed contract action, VA’s healthcare facilities will be able to immediately procure their required supplies using the Government-sourced MSPV Product List. e. Failure to properly account for or make correct decisions regarding continued distribution of necessary supplies while simultaneously monitoring the full supply chain spectrum for any critical issues (i.e. medical item recalls, filtering - out non-FDA non-compliant or grey-market items or non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items) would rapidly undermine the safety and efficiency of VHA patient care.

Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 5

AS3-22-221 f. VA’s promise to Veterans, implemented through the Maintaining Internal Systems and Strengthening Integrated Outside Networks Act (MISSION Act) of 2018, may be compromised as VA’s ability to provide Veterans with an excellent healthcare experience and delivery of the right care, at the right time, at the right place, may be impacted. Ensuring that covered veterans do not experience a lapse in care resulting from errors or delays by the Department, its contractors, or an unusual or excessive burden in accessing hospital care, medical services, or extended care services, is a priority. g. Even if VA could perform and sustain the above referenced actions, VA does not have sufficient infrastructure to stock and distribute the required quantity of medical supplies in all locations.

6. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by FAR Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies: VA met its original intent to fully compete and award a competitive action prior to the expiration of MSPV-NG Bridge contracts in the award of MSPV 2.0. Due to extenuating circumstances, and the COFC decision/injunction, competitive award of any temporary solution comparable to MSPV 2.0 is not feasible before the expiration of the MSPV Gen-Z Transition contracts on November 30, 2022. The current long-term competitive MSPV-GenZ procurement action is in the pre-solicitation phase with award not projected until mid- calendar year 2023, as discussed in Section 2 above. The need for mandatory MSPV distribution services is immediate and a lack of comparable services would cause irreparable harm to VA’s mission to provide Veteran care.

VA has also fully considered FAR 6.302-2(c)(2), which requires VA to “…request offers from as many potential sources as is practicable under the circumstances.” As stated above, VA is not aware of any other contractor(s) who currently have the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or EDI in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption or degradation to quality of care upon current MSPV contract expiration. Obtaining competition for this requirement is not feasible given the time required to complete a competitive action of this scope.

7. A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable: In efforts to increase competition in procurement of the 70,000+ unique supplies for distribution to all VHA facilities located in the United States (US) and all US Territories, VHA issued twentythree RFQs for the acquisition of the consumable commodities in support of the MSPV Program catalog on a tiered evaluation basis. These RFQs were set-aside based on an order of priority to maximize SDVOSB and VOSB participation. Likewise, the SAC issued RFP 36C10G19R0022, for the MSPV 2.0 Prime Vendor distribution requirement as a partial setaside, to maximize the participation of SDVOSB, VOSB, and other small business concerns. Prior to the close of RFP 36C10G19R0050, a bid protest was filed challenging the unrestricted basis, for full and open competition, of the acquisition. This protest was sustained, and in performing corrective action, the SAC amended RFP 36C10G19R0050 to incorporate small business set-asides for line items associated with multiple VISNs for small business concerns using a tiered evaluation approach. Considering this procurement history, the SAC is currently conducting market research through vendor engagement and RFI postings, to produce a comprehensive, competitively awarded long-term solution.

U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE

UNICOR, Federal Prison Industries, Inc.

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION:

Authority Cited: 6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements; 10 U.S.C 3304 (c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(1) 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency; 10 U.S.C. 2304 (c)(2) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a) (2).

1. Identification of the agency and the contracting agency.

Bureau of Prisons - UNICOR - Federal Prison Industries – Allenwood, PA

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.

The UNICOR Factory at LSCI Allenwood manufactures office furniture, specifically seating. This factory needs specific parts to manufacture their product. The needed items for their product were on contract with Nightingale, however, that contract has since expired. Procurement is currently in the process of soliciting and awarding a new contract. Although the contract has expired, the Allenwood factory needs the supplies to keep the factory operating. Since these parts for seating are unique to Nightingale, I would like to request a justification for other than full and open competition to purchase from Nightingale to meet the current needs of the factory. The total cost of this bridge contract will be under $10,000,000.00.

Due to the unusual and compelling nature of this procurement, UNICOR wishes to waive other than full and open competition and negotiate with the potential vendor.

3. A description of the supplies or services required that meet the agency’s needs (including the estimated dollar amount).

DESCRIPTION: Raw materials to build the seating lines here at LSCI Allenwood. Examples are: VXO, IC2, WXO, MXO, LXO, SXO, CXO, etc. Estimated value of raw materials is $5,838,639.66, see attached excel spreadsheet for detailed information

6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements; 10 U.S.C 3304 (c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(1) 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency; 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(2) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(2). LSCI Allenwood is a high producing Office Furniture(seating) factory and we are in the middle of our busy season. We are in the process of putting out a new solicitation but due a new procurement review board process, it is taking more time than anticipated. FPI UNICOR Allenwood has a large volume of orders it must fulfill. In order to meet the mission of the factory, it has to utilize specific parts from Nightingale. Nightingale can supply the unique parts that is needed to fulfill its orders. We would like to implement a bridge contract as an avenue to continue ordering parts from Nightingale so the factory can continue to operate and fulfill orders as scheduled at a fair and reasonable price.

5. A description of effects made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practical including whether a CBD notice was, or will be, publicized as required by Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies.

FAR 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Due to the unusual and compelling nature of this procurement, competition will be waived, Only Nightingale can provide this unique and specific parts and material for this line of seating.

6. A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.

LSCI Allenwood previously had a contract with Nightingale for the needed seating parts, Nightingale has agreed to keep the prices constant from the last contract. Nightingale can provide the unique parts at a fair and reasonable price. This is considered a fair and reasonable price due to past pricing.

7. A description of the market survey conducted and the results or a statement of the reasons a market survey was not conducted.

These chairs are specific to Nightingale and the only company that we can get these parts from..

8. Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition.

This bridge contract is being set up as a 6 month base with 3 each two month options. In anticipation of the solicitation being posted to award a new base with 4 option years, indefinite delivery indefinite quantity for OFG seating line.

9. A listing of sources, if any, that expressed in writing, an interest in the acquisition Nightingale Corporation, 2301 Dixie Road, Mississauga, ON L4Y 1Z9

10. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisitions for the supplies or services are required. Once a contract is awarded, LSCI Allenwood will order the needed seating parts and material from the contract.

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION (OVERSEAS CONTRACTING ACTIVITIES)

1. I recommend that Embassy Kuala Lumpur use other than full and open competition for the acquisition of hotel services for a VVIP Visit held in Kuala Lumpur October 2025 The estimated cost is USD $1,604,275 The minimum guarantee for these services is 826 single hotel room nights.

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.

This is a new contract for services not related to any other current or previous purchase.

3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs.

Hotel services for up to 800 travelers, office space, internet lines, and parking for Senior High Level USG Principal traveling with a delegation inclusive of support elements in: Security, Communications, Logistics and Operations.

4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition.

[ X ] 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2; Unusual and Compelling Urgency; (Based on the available time and urgency of the requirement as detailed below) The VIP visit will be held during October 2025. The visit was only confirmed in mid September

2025. The first travelers will arrive within two weeks of visit notification. The lack of time before US government travelers arrive does not allow enough time for full and open competition.

Security concerns prohibit sufficient advanced notification of VIP travel to allow for sufficient time to conduct full and open competition. The Department of State can only communicate with the staff at Posts abroad when authorization is given due to security concerns. They have an extremely short turnaround time when authorization has been granted for negotiations to commence and site selections to be finalized with both the local vendors and Posts before the actual Senior High Level USG VIP visit occurs. Security and logistical teams make determinations during the site survey as to which hotels are most suitable for the Senior High Level USG VIP and his traveling staff to remain overnight. Consideration of the Senior High Level USG Principal and the location are taken into consideration as a determining factor.

Unique requirements for communications support are under severe time limitations and always a determining factor in the selection process as its capacity to be augmented to the unique requirements necessary to support certain Senior High Level USG Principals.

Many of the arrangements for hotel and transportation are often not confirmed until just before the actual visit. In addition to supporting a large delegation within a short time frame, last minute and frequent changes of itineraries for supporting personnel often result in significant changes in how Posts work with the vendors. With the exception of a few trips, contracts are not permitted to be signed until the Department of State (Post) has written confirmation from all supporting agencies, which enables collection of funds from said agencies in the event of cancellation. This results in an unusual and compelling urgency in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2.

1 Justification for Other than Free and Open Competition Embassy Kuala Lumpur

5. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable. The description should include whether a SAM.gov notice was or will be publicized, as required by FAR 5.2, and if not, which exception under FAR 5.202 applies.

GSO requested quotes from multiple hotels in Kuala Lumpur and will use multiple hotels to accommodate visitors. Priority in booking will go to rooms within per diem rates.

6. A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.

Anticipated costs to the Government are fair and reasonable based on market analysis and quotes from hotels.

7. A description of the market survey conducted and the results or a statement of the reasons a market survey was not conducted.

GSO requested quotes from over ten hotels.

8. Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition.

N/A

9. A listing of sources, if any that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition.

N/A

10. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services required.

N/A

The requirements of this visit are unique; therefore, free and open competition will be used for future requests not of this unique nature.

AS3-22-221 CLASS JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION PURSUANT TO FAR 6.302-2

1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Procurement, Acquisition and Logistics Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC) 5202 Presidents Court, Suite 103 Frederick, MD 21703

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.: The purpose of this document is to obtain Senior Procurement Executive (SPE) approval for the use of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Urgency, for twelve months, for the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Procurement & Logistics’ Medical Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) – GenZ Transition contractors. Use of this authority will allow the SAC to meet the medical and surgical supply needs of the Department from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023, and provide the time necessary to solicit and award competitive long term contracts in support of the MSPV program. This MSPV-GenZ Transition 2 period of performance (PoP) includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods.

Currently, the VHA manages multiple decentralized firm-fixed-priced (FFP) indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) distribution contracts with Medline Industries, Inc., Concordance Healthcare Solutions, LLC, and Cardinal Health 200, LLC. These MSPV-GenZ Transition contractors provide mission critical medical/surgical supply distribution services in support of VA’s MSPV program for designated Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISN) and VA facilities throughout the United States and Puerto Rico. Additionally, the VA Consolidated Mail Outpatient Pharmacy (CMOP) and Other Government Agencies (OGAs) utilize the VA MSPV program. Current OGAs leveraging this program through established Inter-Agency Agreements (IAAs) are: Indian Health Services, Federal Bureau of Prisons, Department of Health and Human Services, and Department of State.

The estimated value of the proposed transition contract (MSPV-GenZ Transition 2) will be consistent with the prime vendor’s general regional area of responsibility and current VISN support. The estimated not to exceed maximum total value for the current planned prime vendor transition contract is listed below.

6. The current long-term competitive MSPV-GenZ procurement action is in the pre-solicitation phase with award not projected until mid- calendar year 2023, as discussed in Section 2 above. Obtaining competition for this requirement is not feasible given the time required to complete a competitive action of this scope.

7. A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable: In efforts to increase competition in procurement of the 70,000+ unique supplies for distribution to all VHA facilities located in the United States (US) and all US Territories, VHA issued twentythree RFQs for the acquisition of the consumable commodities in support of the MSPV Program catalog on a tiered evaluation basis. These RFQs were set-aside based on an order of priority to maximize SDVOSB and VOSB participation. Likewise, the SAC issued RFP 36C10G19R0022, for the MSPV 2.0 Prime Vendor distribution requirement as a partial setaside, to maximize the participation of SDVOSB, VOSB, and other small business concerns. Prior to the close of RFP 36C10G19R0050, a bid protest was filed challenging the unrestricted basis, for full and open competition, of the acquisition. This protest was sustained, and in performing corrective action, the SAC amended RFP 36C10G19R0050 to incorporate small business set-asides for line items associated with multiple VISNs for small business concerns using a tiered evaluation approach. Considering this procurement history, the SAC is currently conducting market research through vendor engagement and RFI postings, to produce a comprehensive, competitively awarded long-term solution.

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION (OVERSEAS CONTRACTING ACTIVITIES)

1. I recommend that Embassy Kuala Lumpur use other than full and open competition for the acquisition of hotel services for a VVIP Visit held in Kuala Lumpur October 2025 The estimated cost is USD $1,604,275 The minimum guarantee for these services is 826 single hotel room nights.

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.

This is a new contract for services not related to any other current or previous purchase.

3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs.

Hotel services for up to 800 travelers, office space, internet lines, and parking for Senior High Level USG Principal traveling with a delegation inclusive of support elements in: Security, Communications, Logistics and Operations.

4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition.

[ X ] 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2; Unusual and Compelling Urgency; (Based on the available time and urgency of the requirement as detailed below) The VIP visit will be held during October 2025. The visit was only confirmed in mid September

2025. The first travelers will arrive within two weeks of visit notification. The lack of time before US government travelers arrive does not allow enough time for full and open competition.

Security concerns prohibit sufficient advanced notification of VIP travel to allow for sufficient time to conduct full and open competition. The Department of State can only communicate with the staff at Posts abroad when authorization is given due to security concerns. They have an extremely short turnaround time when authorization has been granted for negotiations to commence and site selections to be finalized with both the local vendors and Posts before the actual Senior High Level USG VIP visit occurs. Security and logistical teams make determinations during the site survey as to which hotels are most suitable for the Senior High Level USG VIP and his traveling staff to remain overnight. Consideration of the Senior High Level USG Principal and the location are taken into consideration as a determining factor.

Unique requirements for communications support are under severe time limitations and always a determining factor in the selection process as its capacity to be augmented to the unique requirements necessary to support certain Senior High Level USG Principals.

Many of the arrangements for hotel and transportation are often not confirmed until just before the actual visit. In addition to supporting a large delegation within a short time frame, last minute and frequent changes of itineraries for supporting personnel often result in significant changes in how Posts work with the vendors. With the exception of a few trips, contracts are not permitted to be signed until the Department of State (Post) has written confirmation from all supporting agencies, which enables collection of funds from said agencies in the event of cancellation. This results in an unusual and compelling urgency in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2.

GSO requested quotes from multiple hotels in Kuala Lumpur and will use multiple hotels to accommodate visitors. Priority in booking will go to rooms within per diem rates.

6.	A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.

Anticipated costs to the Government are fair and reasonable based on market analysis and quotes from hotels.

7.	A description of the market survey conducted and the results or a statement of the reasons a market survey was not conducted.

GSO requested quotes from over ten hotels.

N/A

N/A

N/A

The requirements of this visit are unique; therefore, free and open competition will be used for future requests not of this unique nature.

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL

Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition (FAR 6.3)

1. Contracting Agency and Activity. The Department of the Interior (DOI), United States Geological Survey (USGS), Earth Resources Observation and Science (EROS) Center.

2. Nature of Action Being Approved. This is a 6-month bridge contract to DCT, Incorporated for operations and maintenance services at EROS Center.

3. Description of Supplies or Services. The required service is for operation and maintenance of the physical facilities of the EROS Center in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Services include comprehensive Operation and Maintenance of all aspects of the 318-acre USGS-owned property, including a 300,000 sq. ft. building with three computer rooms, heating and air conditioning, boilers, electrical systems that convert, switch, and distribute the incoming 13kV power to proper and stable power of various levels to operate the multiple systems and IT assets valued at hundreds of millions of dollars. EROS operates and maintains two high performance computing systems (HPCs). The services also include operating and maintenance of a backup generating plant of 4-750KW generators for emergency power to maintain operations in case of commercial power loss, building automation, facility security systems, a wastewater treatment pond system, the phone private branch exchange (PBX), the physical network infrastructure, grounds upkeep and snow removal.

4. Estimated Dollar Value. $1,738,440.00

5. Statutory Authority. The proposed action may be awarded on a limited source basis under the authority of FAR 6.302-2

6. Rationale Supporting Use of Citation in No. 5. The bridge contract is necessary to allow DOI time to complete, advertise, and award the pending 5-year recompete contract for operations and maintenance. Due to the government shutdown and staff shortages caused by voluntary early retirement packages, the bid package was not completed prior to the contract period of performance end date. We have exhausted a 6-month contract extension and a 6-month emergency task order to extend these necessary services. EROS cannot operate without operations and maintenance services, and the complex nature of the work precludes an off-theshelf or in-house solution.

7. Other Information. 2

8. The Efforts to Identify Additional Sources Including the Market Research Conducted. The existing contract is within three (3) months of expiration. Given the extremely limited timeframe, this brief procurement affords the Government sufficient time to award a full and openly competed contract for the required services and allow for a requisite 30-day transition period. Contractors exist in the market that are able to meet the requirement however, the Government would be seriously injured and the mission adversely critically affected if competition is not limited. (IAW FAR 6.302-2).

9. Future Plans to Permit Competition. A competitively bid 5-year contract recompete is in progress. This bridge contract is needed only to ensure services do not lapse for the EROS Center. Due to the highly specialized skills and equipment needed to perform site operations and maintenance there are no federal staff properly trained to keep the Center operating in the event of a contract lapse. Additionally, at the current time, there are no federal staff properly trained to bring a new Contractor up to speed on the needed tasks.

10. Recommendation and Certification from Program Office Based on the above, I recommend this acquisition be conducted on the basis of other than full and open competition. I certify that technical data which form a basis for this justification that are the responsibility of technical or requirements personnel are complete and accurate. ____________________________ ___________________________ __________ Tracy Michel Signature Date Acting Facilities Manager

This justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.

Control Number: 36C10G20D0029-001 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 Justification and Approval July 29, 2020

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION

1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Acquisition Operations Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC) 10300 Spotsylvania Avenue, Suite 400 Fredericksburg, VA 22408

2. Description of the Action:

The proposed action is to modify the Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) distribution contract for Medline Industries, Inc., 36C10G20D0029, to add Medical Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) services for Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISNs) 6 and 8, on the basis of other than full and open competition. Medline Industries, Inc. is one of the MSPV Bridge contractors that is currently providing supply and distribution services of medical and surgical supplies for VA in support of VA’s MSPV program for other designated geographic areas.

MSPV is a national program, for which participation is mandatory by policy, Veterans Health Administration (VHA) MSPV Mandatory Policy Memorandum (June 22, 2015), for VA Medical Centers (VAMCs), facilities and VA personnel, that provides a customized distribution system to meet facility requirements by providing an efficient, cost-effective, just-in-time distribution catalog ordering process. The MSPV program is based on standard commercial practices and enables facilities to reduce inventory holding costs and streamline delivery and distribution tasks within the facility. The Prime Vendor (PV) model is required because VA lacks sufficient internal capability to warehouse, coordinate deliveries, and consolidate supply stores.

The current MSPV-Next Generation (NG) Bridge contracts were awarded on March 13, 2020 for the period April 1, 2020 to March 31, 2021. The Period of Performance (PoP), for these contracts, is apportioned as a six (6) month base and two (2) – three-month options periods of contract terms concluding on March 31, 2021. Bridge contracts were awarded to the four (4) incumbent MSPV-NG contractors, one of which was American Medical Depot (AMD). During the first four (4) months of performance under their Bridge contract, AMD’s performance deteriorated to a level requiring the Government to terminate for cause under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12. The Contacting Officer notified AMD of the termination for cause on July 29, 2020. PV services in AMD’s supported regions are still vital to patient safety and must continue, especially considering the current COVID-19 pandemic.

Competitively acquired long-term MSPV contracts will not be immediately awarded, as they have been delayed due to statutorily mandated stays of award, on account of bid 2 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 protests. Additionally, any newly awarded PV, other than one of the incumbents from one of the other regions, would require an initial implementation period, of up to four months, to install required information technology (IT)/software, establish necessary distribution agreements with suppliers, and begin identifying and stocking needed supplies for each facility. During this implementation period, there would be a disruption of MSPV supply deliveries, which would result in interruptions in patient care on a massive scale. Given the current healthcare crises VA is facing and could potentially face (i.e. long wait times, epidemics, pandemics, etc.), any disruption to VA supply chain would be unacceptable and injurious. This justification and approval (J&A) will authorize and allow a non-competitively awarded contract, via contract modification, to one of the other incumbent MSPV Bridge contractors, to meet the needs of the agency and its approximate nine (9) million Veteran medical patients’ needs for the duration of this gap. The incumbent vendor has demonstrated requisite expertise, knowledge of management, responsiveness, experienced personnel, without which seamless, uninterrupted service of current delivery of medical and surgical equipment would be impossible. MSPV product usage and the ability to obtain volume based committed use pricing until such time as the follow-on competitive MSPV 2.0 contract action is currently in progress and will be awarded with all expediency. VA’s need for distribution services, is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the primary mission of VA will be in jeopardy of failing, unless permitted to limit the number of sources from which Government solicits bids or proposals. Use of non-competitive contracts, via contract modification, awarded for the span of 8 months to one of the other incumbent Bridge contractors, poses the least risk to the provision of medical care within VA’s facilities.

When VA awards its new, competitively awarded contract(s) they will meet the four following needs: (1) to increase the number of healthcare supplies available to VHA facilities nationwide, (2) to stem the use of non-preferred Sources and contracting methods (example: Government Purchase Card (GPC), local/regional contracts, etc.), (3) to increase cost savings and best pricing obtained by leveraging volume, and (4) to generate increased Veteran-owned business opportunities.

However, the time loss due to protests coupled with the implementation period (needed for IT/software installation from the new vendor so that orders can be met) has caused a gap in which no new vendor would be able to step into the systems to meet the distribution needs at this time. While VA now has a process to provide the source of supply, the loss of distribution at the same time is insurmountable.

The PoP for this contract would be (August 1, 2020 to March 31, 2021). The PoP, for this contract, is apportioned as a two (2) month base and two (2) – three-month options periods, to align PoP with existing bridge contracts. A lapse of service needs to be prevented for the following contract:

VA Contract Number Prime Vendor Contractor 36C10GD0027 American Medical Depot 3 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 This will be executed by modifying the MSPV Bridge contract for the following Prime Vendor to add VISNs 6 and 8 as service areas:

VA Contract Number Prime Vendor Contractor 36C10GD0029 Medline Industries, Inc.

VA’s future MSPV 2.0 competitive contracts (still to be awarded but currently delayed) must provide an implementation period in order to function as planned and to avoid failure to perform. This is not poor advanced acquisition planning to meet the Government’s requirements, but the realities of medical operations and the loss of time due to protests which have necessitated this bridge.

3. Description of Supplies or Services:

VA, through the VHA and SAC, administers the MSPV program and MSPV bridge contracts for the supply and distribution of medical and surgical supplies for the care of Veterans. The MSPV program is based on standard commercial practices and enables facilities to reduce inventory holding cost and streamline delivery and distribution tasks within the facility. The nationally mandated program was developed as the key element in VA’s integrated healthcare supply chain improvement initiative, and was designed to significantly improve efficiency, accuracy, and patient safety, because VA lacked sufficient internal capability to warehouse, coordinate deliveries, and consolidate supply stores. The MSPV-NG contracts afford VA critical benefits not available through other contract methodologies, including traditional single source supply contracts, and establishes a national strategic sourcing solution that combines a Government provided capability for ordering a wide range of medical, surgical, dental, laboratory, and environmental medical supplies via a master listing with electronic cataloging and ordering capability.

The solution offered by this contract will allow all VA healthcare facilities, 1,255 healthcare facilities including, 170 medical centers, and 1,074 outpatient sites, within all 18 VISNs to immediately continue placing orders and avoid an interruption in the healthcare supply chain that would prove injurious to patient health and safety. Under the contract, the PV will provide only distribution services for the medical/surgical (med/surg) items that are added to the Government master listing via VA national and local contracts, VA Distribution and Pricing Agreements (DAPAs), and Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs). Distribution services include, but are not limited to, services such as next-scheduled business day delivery, generating inventory status and other performance reports as identified in the Performance Requirements Summary (PRS), providing emergency deliveries, and providing unit of use or low unit of measure shipments for single and multiple end-user delivery points to the facilities designated delivery point(s). As currently required, distribution services would continue for all, medical, surgical, dental, cleaning, rescue and safety, laboratory, prosthetic supplies, other medical/surgical cleaning, rescue and safety supplies, and non-expendable 4 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 equipment as used by VAMCs. The estimated value of the contract will be consistent with the PV’s regional area of responsibility. The estimated not to exceed maximum total value for the current planned PV contract modification is listed below.

Performance Period Medline Industries, Inc. Base Option 1 Option 2 Total

4. Statutory Authority:

The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C.3304(a)(2) as implemented by the FAR Subpart 6.302-2 entitled, “Unusual and Compelling Urgency.”

5. Rationale Supporting Use of Authority Cited Above:

Due to the statutorily imposed stay because of multiple pre-award protests (B#’s B417745.1, B-417745.2, B-417745.3, B-418223.1, B-418223.2, and B-418223.3) VA’s awards for the competitive follow-on, MSPV 2.0 contract, was delayed by 9 months.

When AMD’s MSPV Bridge contract was terminated for cause on July 29,2020, VA lacks contracts to obtain medical and surgical equipment for such needs as even basic operating room procedures for the specific regions formally supported by AMD.

VA’s rationale is that an unusual and compelling urgency exists, precluding full and open competition for any comparable type of requirement, due to the termination of AMD’s contract. Similarly, any effort to award a fully competitive action or divert an already over-stretched VA workforce to address the PV-supported requirements of MSPV, would not only result in a long break in service and serious jeopardy to patient health and safety but also mission loss for the MSPV program as well as other areas of VA during the COVID-19 pandemic.

A constant and continuous effort is being implemented by VA to make a timely award of the follow-on MSPV 2.0 acquisition; however, due to circumstances beyond our control, an award without a break in service is not possible. Likewise, full and open competition for any temporary solution, of a comparable type of requirement, can’t be accomplished without incurring a significant break in service because of the immediate nature of the AMD termination. With the contract termination of AMD on July 29, 2020, it is imperative that distribution services continue and remain uninterrupted until such time that MSPV 2.0 can be awarded. Under this proposed J&A, the Government will continue responsibility for adding/maintaining items on the master list, and the PVs will act solely in a distribution capacity. 5 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 The VA’s current need for distribution support on the MSPV program is both unusual and compelling. The need is urgent/unusual and compelling for the following reasons:

1. The work performed is essential to accomplishing VA mission of delivering healthcare services and supplies to our nation’s, approximate, nine (9) million Veterans currently receiving care through VA’s healthcare system. A disruption of VA’s healthcare supply chain would immediately hinder the delivery of essential medical, surgical, dental, and laboratory supplies and other contracted healthcare such as cleaning, rescue and safety supplies and services used in the direct delivery of patient care. This impairment would cause unacceptable delays in fulfilling VA’s requirements and would directly impact the health, safety, quality and timeliness of care delivered to Veterans during the COVID-19 pandemic.

2. AMD’s MSPV Bridge contract was terminated for cause on July 29, 2020. Without a replacement, VA will suffer direct financial and operational injury and mission loss across the MSPV program. VA’s efficient, cost-effective, just-in-time ordering, and distribution process will be severely hindered as facilities will revert to non-preferred contract methods as occurred before the introduction of the national MSPV program in 2005. Approximately 2,000 contracting staff would have to attempt processing nearly 600,000 formal contracting actions (in addition to their existing work-load) annually, via inefficient, ineffective and frequently duplicative contracting actions and GPC purchases, which have shown to be more than five times the workload burden of using the MSPV ordering method. VA will also lose essential allocation of personal protective equipment (PPE) necessary to support VAMCs during the current pandemic if these allocations cannot be transferred to another PV capable of warehousing and disturbing the effectively.

3. The three (3) current MSPV Bridge PVs are the only source that is immediately capable of meeting the contractual duties through use of Government sources of supply and not require a 75 to 120-day implementation period. No other contractor currently has the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption or degradation to quality of care upon MSPV-NG expiration. Under the proposed contract action, VA’s healthcare facilities will be able to immediately procure their required supplies using the Government populated master list.

4. VA personnel are not available or able to perform the tasks performed by the PVs. As current regional distributors for the MSPV program, the existing PV’s have the prevailing infrastructure, ordering capability, and required resident knowledge which make them uniquely qualified, and currently the only sources capable of providing enhanced distribution of required medical commodities throughout the entire VA healthcare network. For example, VA would have to 6 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 incur the extensive cost of hiring and training additional Government and/or contractor personnel and leasing and/or constructing central warehouses and distribution centers in the effort to fulfill med/surg shipments to VAMCs.

5. Failure to either properly account for or make correct decisions with regard to continued distribution of necessary supplies while simultaneously monitoring the full supply chain spectrum for any critical issues (i.e. medical item recalls, filtering out non-Food and Drug Administration (FDA) compliant or grey-market items or non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items) would rapidly result in diminished levels of safety and efficiency to patient care.

6. In the event MSPV’s Ordering Officers are unable to place orders via the MSPV catalogs in EDI and those orders are added to the workload of an already overburdened contracting staff, the result would be catastrophic. Lead times to procure these items through contracting for other than emergency orders are 45 days; however, emergency orders require action within three days. Practically all new orders would become immediate emergencies in order to ensure timely delivery of safe, reliable healthcare to Veterans.

7. VA’s promise to Veterans, via the Maintaining Internal Systems and Strengthening Integrated Outside Networks Act (MISSION Act) of 2018, may be compromised as VA’s ability to continue to provide Veterans with an excellent healthcare experience and delivery of the right care, at the right time, at the right place may be impacted. Ensuring that covered veterans do not experience a lapse in care resulting from errors or delays by the Department or its contractors or an unusual or excessive burden in accessing hospital care, medical services, or extended care services is a priority.

Approval of the previously described non-competitive contract action will enable VA to avoid disruption of VA’s healthcare supply chain and catastrophic negative impact to the Department’s ability to provide world-class patient care to our nation’s Veterans during the COVID-19 pandemic. Once more, other negative ramifications that would be averted include: the loss of potential savings as facilities source distribution of supplies through other means, increased workload, man-hours, and cost of operations will increase, as already depleting resources are focused on monitoring the full supply chain spectrum for any critical issues. Authorization of the J&A would keep VA from having to revert to the substantially inefficient and ineffective means of distributing sourced medical supplies.

Therefore, award of the non-competitive contract action for VISNs 6 and 8, via contract modification, to the current MSPV Bridge PV, Medline Industries, Inc., is necessary in order to avoid grave physical and medical risk to Veteran patients as well as direct financial and operational injury to the Government. There are no other vendors, other than current PVs, that the Government could negotiate with, in quick order, to award contracts for distribution services. Each current MSPV Bridge PV will be awarded two 7 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 (2) of AMD’s previously serviced geographic areas. Any effort to award a fully competitive action or divert an already over-stretched VA workforce to address the PVsupported requirements of MSPV, would only result in mission loss for the MSPV program as well as other areas of VA.

6. Efforts to Obtain Competition:

The original intent was to fully compete and award a competitive action prior to the expiration of MSPV-NG, vis-à-vis MSPV 2.0. Due to the extenuating circumstances as outlined above, exercising the remaining option year two on MSPV-NG nor award of the follow-on competitive contract action MSPV 2.0 was a viable option before expiration of the MSPV-NG contracts. The need for MSPV distribution services is immediate and a lack of correlating services would cause irreparable harm to our mission. Obtaining competition for this requirement could not be accomplished due to the time required to complete a competitive action. Previous and current ongoing efforts are being made to maximize and obtain competition for the required supplies under MSPV 2.0. The following timeline and description of past efforts to obtain competition, since the J&A and modification are provided:

- The RFI closed on February 1, 2019. Thirteen (13) interested sources responded to the RFI.

- On January 10, 2019, a Vendor Engagement Day was conducted. Four (4) 1hour sessions were held and limited to two (2) representatives per company. Each session discussed the questionnaire that was included in the RFI.

8 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 - Request for Proposal (RFP) 36C10G19R0022 was posted on June 3, 2019, to FBO, as a partial set-aside, by order of tiered priority, with a response due date of July 8, 2019. - Because FBO migrated to a new system, Amendment A0002 was released on beta.SAM.gov on 11 February 2020 to set-aside CLINs associated with Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISNs) 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 17, and 22 for Small Business concerns using a Tiered Evaluation approach. A0002.

- Request for Quotes (RFQs) for twenty-three (23) various supply categories, were posted to FBO from June 17, 2019 to October 18, 2019, with closing dates from October 17, 2019 to December 18, 2019. 7. Actions to Increase Competition:

The MSPV Program Office has implemented its Clinician Driven Strategic Sourcing (CDSS) plan to streamline the procurement and delivery of high-use medical, surgical, dental, select prosthetic, laboratory and facility management supplies throughout VA.

The Program Executive Office (PEO) established its CDSS as a central component of MSPV formulary/catalog development and collaboration across VA, facilitating ongoing improvement of VA’s sourcing of key, high-use medical and surgical supply items. CDSS has increased participation, collaboration, and accountability amongst clinicians 9 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 and clinical specialists who are the stakeholders and possess the knowledge and education of items needed for the highest quality of care for Veterans. To ensure the MSPV program is fully based on a foundation that is rooted in CDSS principles, a plan of action was put in place with collaboration of Executive Leadership from the MSPV PEO, the Medical Supplies Program Office, VHA, VHA Procurement and Logistics Office, VA Office of Acquisition and Logistics, National CPOs, Chief Medical Offices, National Center for Patient Safety, and other key offices as required.

MSPV PEO continues to nationally coordinate with healthcare product supply chain stakeholders, clinicians, clinical specialists and leadership to get buy in and engagement on its comprehensive CDSS strategy. The CDSS process currently collects, monitors and evaluates market research, and conducts its product evaluation and value analysis for best quality products, cost reduction, and streamlined strategic acquisitions.

In efforts to increase competition, for the 49,000 types of supplies for distribution to all VHA facilities located in the United States (US) and all US Territories, VHA issued twenty-three (23) RFQs for the acquisition of the consumable commodities in support of the MSPV Program catalog on a tiered evaluation basis. These RFQs were set-aside based on an order of priority to maximize SDVOSB and VOSB participation. Likewise, the SAC issued RFP 36C10G19R0022, for the MSPV 2.0 Prime Vendor distribution requirement as a partial set-aside, to encourage and maximize the involvement of SDVOSB, VOSB, and other small business concerns. With the cancellation of the initial MSPV 2.0 RFP, the SAC issued RFP 36C10G19R0050, unrestricted, for full and open competition, in accordance with market analysis, in the effort to foster and expand vendor competition. Prior to the close of RFP 36C10G19R0050, a bid protest was filed challenging the unrestricted basis, for full and open competition, of the acquisition. This protest was sustained, requiring corrective action on the part of VA to reexamine its small business set-aside strategy (and adding to the time required to put in place a fully competitive contract solution). In performing corrective action, the SAC amended RFP 36C10G19R0050 to incorporate small business set-asides for CLINs associated with VISNs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 17, and 22 for Small Business concerns using a Tiered Evaluation approach.

8. Market Research:

The market research recently conducted for MSPV 2.0 was utilized for this J&A as it was recently amended and completed in September 2019 and is the most up to date market survey available. In preparation for the continuation of the MSPV program, in 2018 SAC assumed responsibility of awarding the MSPV 2.0 distribution contracts and VHA assumed responsibility of awarding the MSPV 2.0 supply contracts. Two RFIs and a Vendor Industry Engagement Day were conducted in support of MPSV 2.0 distribution market research. The RFls played an essential role in determining the market's ability to meet our basic requirements, while offering insight into vendor availability and capability. 10 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 Market research was conducted to determine the suitability of commercial items, the geographic regions to be competed, and the potential use of SDVOSB or other small business set-asides. This market research establishes that— - The Government’s need may be met by a type of item or service customarily available in the commercial marketplace that would meet the definition of a commercial item in accordance with FAR 10.002.

- Competition for geographic regions should be conducted at the VISN level, with the exception of Puerto Rico (PR), Guam, American Samoa, Virgin Islands, and the Philippines. It was contemplated that Oklahoma (OK) should be competed as a single region with VISN 17 Texas (TX), not as part of VISN 19, since the discontinuity between OK and the rest of the VISN. However, the Integrated Product Team (IPT) made the determination to leave OK within VISN 19 in an effort to maintain VISN continuity of management.

Given that the above market research conducted for MSPV 2.0 has shown that there is a limited number of capable vendors that could fulfill the MSPV 2.0 requirement for VA, none would be able to do so without the sizeable startup period built into MSPV 2.0. Considering this, none of the vendors, outside of incumbents that submitted proposals in response to the MSPV 2.0 RFP, would be able to immediately provide the required distribution services of MSPV.

9. Other Facts:

This unusual and compelling urgency precludes full and open competition and it is of certain that any delay in award of this contract action will result in serious patient safety considerations across the entire VA network to include detrimental financial costs to the Government as a result. Prior to the MSPV-NG contract modification, VA had been unsuccessful in populating the Government master list with a large number of medical/surgical items. After the modification, the additional sourcing flexibility to obtain critical healthcare supplies more closely approximates VHA’s existing best in class pharmaceutical PV program that relies heavily on commercial buying practices and has facilitated the inclusion of more than 15,000 additional items. Given the need for facilities to be able to continue to access the broad listing of medical and surgical supplies realized under the MSPV-NG modification, and given that fair and reasonable prices have been confirmed using commercial cost indices, it is in the best interest of VA to ensure the immediate continued distribution through current MSPV distribution channels (Medical-Surgical PVs) while the SAC and VHA offices continue with the implementation of the MSPV 2.0 distribution and supply acquisitions.

The primary mission of VA is to fulfill President Lincoln's promise “To care for him who shall have borne the battle, and for his widow, and his orphan” by serving and honoring the men and women who are America’s Veterans. We seek to accomplish this mission through our 5 core values of Integrity, Commitment, Advocacy, Respect, and 11 Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 Excellence. These “I CARE” values are incorporated in the SAC partnership with the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), to deliver timely medical and surgical products to our Nation’s Veterans through the MSPV-NG Program.

Currently, the MSPV PVs are the only sources serving in the critical role of comprehensive emergency supply response in support of local, regional, or national emergencies or disasters. Additionally, VA supports the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and US Department of Health & Human Services with the delivery of medical supplies and coordination of support missions for response to and recovery from nationally-declared emergencies and disasters. VA accomplishes this requirement through the current regional PVs, who are contractually required to perform a full range of support to healthcare facilities to ensure resiliency, continuity and rapid recovery of healthcare services during disasters and other potential disruptions to healthcare service delivery. Given that VAMCs, and other select federal facilities, are designated FEMA facilities with significant contingency and emergency response roles, a supply chain interruption would not only negatively impact healthcare delivery to our nation’s Veterans and their dependents, but also potentially have a direct, negative impact on the greater public.

Approval of this contract action would directly abate significant negative impact to the Government in terms of monetary cost. However, the far greater negative impact not realized would be the undeniable risk to the overall health, welfare and safety of millions of Veterans. Although every effort was made to compare costs, benefits and all other options to this contract action, no reasonable, timely alternative has been identified.

For the reasons described above, the proposed contract action is urgently needed to ensure the continuity of services of the MSPV program, and the availability of safe clinician required commodities on the catalog for the treatment of our Veterans until MSPV 2.0 is awarded.
