GSO requested quotes from rental companies that have the capacity to support this visit. Notice need not be submitted as the compelling urgency precludes competition to the maximum extent practicable.

6. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.: The purpose of this document is to obtain Senior Procurement Executive (SPE) approval for the use of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Urgency, for twelve months, for the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Procurement & Logistics’ Medical Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) – GenZ Transition contractors. Use of this authority will allow the SAC to meet the medical and surgical supply needs of the Department from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023, and provide the time necessary to solicit and award competitive long term contracts in support of the MSPV program. This MSPV-GenZ Transition 2 period of performance (PoP) includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods.

Currently, the VHA manages multiple decentralized firm-fixed-priced (FFP) indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) distribution contracts with Medline Industries, Inc., Concordance Healthcare Solutions, LLC, and Cardinal Health 200, LLC. These MSPV-GenZ Transition contractors provide mission critical medical/surgical supply distribution services in support of VA’s MSPV program for designated Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISN) and VA facilities throughout the United States and Puerto Rico. Additionally, the VA Consolidated Mail Outpatient Pharmacy (CMOP) and Other Government Agencies (OGAs) utilize the VA MSPV program. Current OGAs leveraging this program through established Inter-Agency Agreements (IAAs) are: Indian Health Services, Federal Bureau of Prisons, Department of Health and Human Services, and Department of State.

The estimated value of the proposed transition contract (MSPV-GenZ Transition 2) will be consistent with the prime vendor’s general regional area of responsibility and current VISN support. The estimated not to exceed maximum total value for the current planned prime vendor transition contract is listed below.

Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 3

AS3-22-221 over 800 active ordering officers for MSPV would need to independently procure requirements for their facilities. Additionally, with the loss of allocations and the MSPV Product List, the ordering officers for each VAMC would be in direct competition with one another on the open market to procure requirements, including PPE. Moreover, the management of the Product List, and associated Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs), Basic Ordering Agreements, and Distribution And Pricing Agreements, through the MSPV program addresses critical supply issues, including medical item recalls, filtering out non-Food and Drug Administration (FDA) non-compliant or greymarket items and non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items. Consequently, at this time, there are no other viable, competitively awarded contract(s) established for VA to utilize subsequent to the November 30, 2022 expiration date to ensure the continuity of the MSPV program. As such, implementation of the transition effort is considered urgent due to the magnitude of impact, and being pursued under FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

This class justification and approval (CJ&A) will authorize the awards for this transition effort, enabling the current contractors to continue to meet the needs of the agency from December 1, 2022 until November 30, 2023. This performance period includes a six (6) month base period of December 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and two three-month option periods during which the SAC will go through the process of soliciting and awarding new, competitive contracts in support of VA’s MSPV program. Based upon the most recent integrated master schedule/plan of action and milestones for the competitive action (dtd September 13, 2022), award is expected May 17, 2023, with the first availability to order post the 120-day implementation period of September 27,

2023. The inclusion of option periods allows for flexibility in the event the competitive procurement timeline is able to be streamlined and awarded sooner.

MSPV Gen-Z Transition 2 contracts will maintain SAC capability to satisfy the mission-critical medical and surgical supply needs of the entire VA Healthcare System. The contracts will continue to meet the four following needs: (1) to increase the number of healthcare supplies available to VHA facilities nationwide; (2) to stem the use of non-preferred sources and contracting methods (example: Government Purchase Card (GPC) over micro-purchase threshold, local/regional contracts, etc.); (3) to increase cost savings and best pricing obtained by leveraging volume; and (4) to generate increased Veteran-owned business opportunities.

3. Description of Supplies or Services: VA, through the VHA and SAC, administers the MSPV Program, MSPV Supply BPAs and MSPV Gen-Z Transition distribution contracts for the supply and distribution of medical and surgical supplies across VHA facilities for the care of veterans. The MSPV program is based on standard commercial practices and enables facilities to reduce inventory holding cost and streamline delivery and distribution tasks within the facility. The national program is mandatory for all VAMCs in accordance with VHA Directive 1761, dated December 30, 2020 (valid through recertification date of December 31, 2025) and was developed as the key element in VA’s integrated healthcare supply chain improvement initiative, and was designed to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and patient safety, because VA lacked sufficient internal capability to warehouse, coordinate deliveries, and consolidate supply stores. The MSPV Gen-Z Transition contracts afford VA critical benefits not available through other contract methodologies, including traditional single source supply contracts, and establishes a national strategic sourcing solution that combines a Government provided capability for ordering a wide range of medical, surgical, dental, laboratory, and environmental medical supplies via a product list with electronic cataloging and ordering capability. The MSPV Product List consists of approxima ely 70,000 supply items, 65 percent of which are supplied by Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 4

AS3-22-221

Services Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses while overall a total of 72 percent are provided by Small Businesses.

4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition: The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2) as implemented by FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

5. A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited: a. Without the award of the MSPV Gen-Z Transition 2 contracts prior to November 30, 2022, VA would lack the ability to obtain critical medical and surgical materials and equipment to support in-patient care and basic operating room procedures for all healthcare facilities. b. The work performed is integral to VA’s mission of delivering healthcare services to the approximately nine (9) million Veterans currently receiving care through our nation’s VA healthcare system. VHA requires a comprehensive contract vehicle for obtaining critical medical supplies for patient care, managing utilization and maintaining spend under management. c. VA will suffer direct financial and operational injury and mission-loss across the MSPV program. VA’s efficient, cost-effective, just-in- time ordering and distribution processes will be severely hindered as facilities will revert to non-preferred contract methods as occurred before the introduction of the national MSPV program in 2005. A program lapse would require approximately 2,000 contracting staff to attempt to process nearly 600,000 formal contracting actions (in addition to their existing workload) annually, via inefficient, ineffective, and frequently duplicative contracting actions and GPC purchases, which entail more than five times the workload burden of the MSPV ordering method. VA will also lose essential allocations of PPE necessary to support VAMCs due to supply chain disruptions created by the COVID-19 pandemic. If these allocations cannot be transferred to another Prime Vendor capable of warehousing and distributing them effectively, VAMCs will not be able to safely deliver patient care. d. No other contractors currently have the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption of or degradation to quality of care upon MSPV Gen-Z Transition contract expiration. Under the proposed contract action, VA’s healthcare facilities will be able to immediately procure their required supplies using the Government-sourced MSPV Product List. e. Failure to properly account for or make correct decisions regarding continued distribution of necessary supplies while simultaneously monitoring the full supply chain spectrum for any critical issues (i.e. medical item recalls, filtering - out non-FDA non-compliant or grey-market items or non-Buy American Act/non-Trade Agreements Act compliant items) would rapidly undermine the safety and efficiency of VHA patient care.

Control Number: 36C10X-22-AP-1244 5

AS3-22-221 f. VA’s promise to Veterans, implemented through the Maintaining Internal Systems and Strengthening Integrated Outside Networks Act (MISSION Act) of 2018, may be compromised as VA’s ability to provide Veterans with an excellent healthcare experience and delivery of the right care, at the right time, at the right place, may be impacted. Ensuring that covered veterans do not experience a lapse in care resulting from errors or delays by the Department, its contractors, or an unusual or excessive burden in accessing hospital care, medical services, or extended care services, is a priority. g. Even if VA could perform and sustain the above referenced actions, VA does not have sufficient infrastructure to stock and distribute the required quantity of medical supplies in all locations.

6. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by FAR Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies: VA met its original intent to fully compete and award a competitive action prior to the expiration of MSPV-NG Bridge contracts in the award of MSPV 2.0. Due to extenuating circumstances, and the COFC decision/injunction, competitive award of any temporary solution comparable to MSPV 2.0 is not feasible before the expiration of the MSPV Gen-Z Transition contracts on November 30, 2022. The current long-term competitive MSPV-GenZ procurement action is in the pre-solicitation phase with award not projected until mid- calendar year 2023, as discussed in Section 2 above. The need for mandatory MSPV distribution services is immediate and a lack of comparable services would cause irreparable harm to VA’s mission to provide Veteran care.

VA has also fully considered FAR 6.302-2(c)(2), which requires VA to “…request offers from as many potential sources as is practicable under the circumstances.” As stated above, VA is not aware of any other contractor(s) who currently have the required infrastructure, ordering capability, or EDI in place, for the facilities contemplated under this contract, to deliver the necessary medical supplies required to support patient care and safety without interruption or degradation to quality of care upon current MSPV contract expiration. Obtaining competition for this requirement is not feasible given the time required to complete a competitive action of this scope.

7. A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable: In efforts to increase competition in procurement of the 70,000+ unique supplies for distribution to all VHA facilities located in the United States (US) and all US Territories, VHA issued twentythree RFQs for the acquisition of the consumable commodities in support of the MSPV Program catalog on a tiered evaluation basis. These RFQs were set-aside based on an order of priority to maximize SDVOSB and VOSB participation. Likewise, the SAC issued RFP 36C10G19R0022, for the MSPV 2.0 Prime Vendor distribution requirement as a partial setaside, to maximize the participation of SDVOSB, VOSB, and other small business concerns. Prior to the close of RFP 36C10G19R0050, a bid protest was filed challenging the unrestricted basis, for full and open competition, of the acquisition. This protest was sustained, and in performing corrective action, the SAC amended RFP 36C10G19R0050 to incorporate small business set-asides for line items associated with multiple VISNs for small business concerns using a tiered evaluation approach. Considering this procurement history, the SAC is currently conducting market research through vendor engagement and RFI postings, to produce a comprehensive, competitively awarded long-term solution.

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION (OVERSEAS CONTRACTING ACTIVITIES)

1. I recommend that Embassy Kuala Lumpur use other than full and open competition for the acquisition of rental vehicles and drivers for a VVIP Visit in October 2025. The estimated cost is USD $823,216 The minimum guarantee for these services is USD $11,904.

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved. This is a new contract for vehicle services not related to any other current or previous purchase.

3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency's needs. Vehicles and drivers are needed to support a VVIP visit to Malaysia. These meetings require vehicles and drivers to transport staff from hotels to meeting locations and the airport on arrival and departure.

4. An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition. [ X] 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2: Unusual and Compelling Urgency: (Based on the available time and urgency of the requirement as detailed below) The VVIP visit will be held in late October 2025. The visit was only confirmed in September 2025. The first travelers will arrive within two weeks of visit notification. The lack of time before U.S. government travelers arrive does not allow enough time for full and open competition. Delay in award of the contract will result in greatly increased prices and cost to the government. Many of the arrangements for hotel and transportation are often not confirmed until just before the actual visit. In addition to supporting a large delegation within a short time frame, last minute and frequent changes of itineraries for supporting personnel often result in significant changes in how Posts work with the vendors. With the exception of a few trips, contracts are not permitted to be signed until the Department of State (Post) has written confirmation from all supporting agencies, which enables collection of funds from said agencies in the event of cancellation. This results in an unusual and compelling urgency in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2.

5. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable. The description should include whether a FedBizOpps notice was or will be publicized, as required by FAR 5.2, and if not, which exception under FAR 5.202 applies. GSO requested quotes from rental companies that have the capacity to support this visit. Notice need not be submitted as the compelling urgency precludes competition to the maximum extent practicable.

6. A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable. 1 October 7, 2025 Justification for Other than Free and Open Competition Embassy Kuala Lumpur As the Competition Advocate at post, I approve this justification: Date FA Ro UK KHAN Digitally signed by FAROUK KHAN Date: 2025.10.06 13:24:03 +08'00' Acting Management Counselor 3

U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE

UNICOR, Federal Prison Industries, Inc.

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION:

Authority Cited: 6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements; 10 U.S.C 3304 (c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(1) 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency; 10 U.S.C. 2304 (c)(2) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a) (2).

1. Identification of the agency and the contracting agency.

Bureau of Prisons - UNICOR - Federal Prison Industries – Allenwood, PA

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.

The UNICOR Factory at LSCI Allenwood manufactures office furniture, specifically seating. This factory needs specific parts to manufacture their product. The needed items for their product were on contract with Nightingale, however, that contract has since expired. Procurement is currently in the process of soliciting and awarding a new contract. Although the contract has expired, the Allenwood factory needs the supplies to keep the factory operating. Since these parts for seating are unique to Nightingale, I would like to request a justification for other than full and open competition to purchase from Nightingale to meet the current needs of the factory. The total cost of this bridge contract will be under $10,000,000.00.

Due to the unusual and compelling nature of this procurement, UNICOR wishes to waive other than full and open competition and negotiate with the potential vendor.

3. A description of the supplies or services required that meet the agency’s needs (including the estimated dollar amount).

DESCRIPTION: Raw materials to build the seating lines here at LSCI Allenwood. Examples are: VXO, IC2, WXO, MXO, LXO, SXO, CXO, etc. Estimated value of raw materials is $5,838,639.66, see attached excel spreadsheet for detailed information

4. Identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition.

6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements; 10 U.S.C 3304 (c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(1) 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency; 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(2) or 41 U.S.C. 3304 (a)(2). LSCI Allenwood is a high producing Office Furniture(seating) factory and we are in the middle of our busy season. We are in the process of putting out a new solicitation but due a new procurement review board process, it is taking more time than anticipated. FPI UNICOR Allenwood has a large volume of orders it must fulfill. In order to meet the mission of the factory, it has to utilize specific parts from Nightingale. Nightingale can supply the unique parts that is needed to fulfill its orders. We would like to implement a bridge contract as an avenue to continue ordering parts from Nightingale so the factory can continue to operate and fulfill orders as scheduled at a fair and reasonable price.

5. A description of effects made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practical including whether a CBD notice was, or will be, publicized as required by Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 5.202 applies.

FAR 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Due to the unusual and compelling nature of this procurement, competition will be waived, Only Nightingale can provide this unique and specific parts and material for this line of seating.

6. A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable.

LSCI Allenwood previously had a contract with Nightingale for the needed seating parts, Nightingale has agreed to keep the prices constant from the last contract. Nightingale can provide the unique parts at a fair and reasonable price. This is considered a fair and reasonable price due to past pricing.

7. A description of the market survey conducted and the results or a statement of the reasons a market survey was not conducted.

These chairs are specific to Nightingale and the only company that we can get these parts from..

8. Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition.

This bridge contract is being set up as a 6 month base with 3 each two month options. In anticipation of the solicitation being posted to award a new base with 4 option years, indefinite delivery indefinite quantity for OFG seating line.

9. A listing of sources, if any, that expressed in writing, an interest in the acquisition Nightingale Corporation, 2301 Dixie Road, Mississauga, ON L4Y 1Z9

10. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisitions for the supplies or services are required. Once a contract is awarded, LSCI Allenwood will order the needed seating parts and material from the contract.

11. Contracting Officer certification that the identification is accurate and complete to the best of the Contracting Officer’s knowledge and belief. By signing the form, the contracting officer certifies the acceptability of the document. Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION SECTION 1: IDENTIFICATION OF THE AGENCY AND THE CONTRACTING ACTIVITY

Department of State Contracting Activity ☐ Office of Acquisitions Management ☐ Foreign Service Institute ☐ Office of Foreign Missions ☐ U.S. Mission to the United Nations ☒ Overseas Post U.S. Embassy Rome, Italy Requiring Activity U.S. Embassy in Rome – GSO

SECTION 2: NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING APPROVED

Approval is requested to solicit and award, on a sole-source basis, an IDIQ contract to Queen Limousine for transportation services with drivers in support of a senior high-level USG VIP visit to Italy, as described in Section 3, on behalf of the Requiring Activity.

The authority to act under this Class Justification and Approval (J&A) expires on February 28, 2026.

This action will result in a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract.

SECTION 3: DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY’S NEEDS

The Embassy requires transportation services with drivers to support a Senior high-level USG VIP visit in connection with the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympic Games.

Services Estimated Quantity Estimated Period of Performance Transportation Services with Drivers 190 Vehicles 20 January – 15 February The estimated value for the entire period of performance is estimated at $7,584,597.43.

Task orders will be issued as required to meet operational needs and security requirements.

The contractor shall provide high-quality vehicles and drivers and operate with established, robust internal processes for financial management, quality assurance, and operational oversight to ensure all aspects of contract execution are properly monitored and controlled.

SECTION 4: IDENTIFICATION OF THE STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION

This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 41 USC 3304, as implemented by FAR 6.3 and substantiated by the following:

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE ☒ FAR 6.103-2 - Unusual and compelling urgency.

SECTION 5: DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR'S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED The contractor's unique qualifications and expertise are essential due to the scale and complexity of the event, the specific requirements to be met, and the contractor's demonstrated experience and capacity to manage such services effectively.

This assessment is further supported by the last-minute notification of VIP travel, the stringent security and operational standards to be met, and the overall critical nature of the required services, which creates an unusual and compelling urgency.

These unique senior high-level USG VIP travel requirements result in only a single, or a very limited number of, responsible sources capable of providing the required level of operational support. The proposed contractor can meet these requirements due to a strong record of past performance on similar projects.

SECTION 6. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS WERE SOLICITED FROM AS MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE, INCLUDING WHETHER A NOTICE WAS OR WILL BE PUBLICIZED AS REQUIRED BY FAR SUBPART 5.2 AND, IF NOT, WHICH EXCEPTION UNDER FAR 5.202 APPLIES A formal synopsis of the proposed procurement was not published on SAM.gov because this contract action is being made under the conditions described in FAR 6.103-2, which allows for exceptions due to unusual and compelling urgency. Market research identified a few other vendors; however, none demonstrated the experience or capacity to manage operational services of this scale.

SECTION 7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST TO THE GOVERNMENT IS FAIR AND REASONABLE The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to the Government of the services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable based on: o Rates from prior similar events SECTION 8. DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED (SEE PART 10) AND THE RESULTS OR A STATEMENT OF THE REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED This event is attended by both official and unofficial representatives from around the world. Most services have already been secured, and costs increase significantly during this period, further limiting the number of vendors capable of meeting the Embassy's transportation requirements.

The short notice, high demand, and security-sensitive nature of the requirement have limited the ability to conduct full and open market research.

Office of the Procurement Executive U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE SECTION 9. ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION The unique requirements associated with senior high-level USG VIP travel, combined with security considerations and the operational environment of the event, limit the Government’s ability to conduct a full and open competition.

The proposed contractor possesses unique qualifications that meet the Government’s security and logistical requirements. Any delay in the award may result in the unavailability of qualified transportation resources.

SECTION 10. LISTING OF THE SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED, IN WRITING, AN INTEREST

IN THE ACQUISITION

MTM Italia Srl expressed interest in providing these services. MTM Italia Srl does not, however, currently possess the experience required to support such a complex, high-profile assignment with stringent security and logistical standards.

Furthermore, due to the urgency of the requirement and the limited time available before the event, there is insufficient time to onboard and prepare a new contractor to meet the complex operational demands. Attempting to do so would pose significant risks to the successful execution of the event and could compromise both security and mission objectives.

SECTION 11. STATEMENT OF THE ACTIONS, IF ANY, THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO REMOVE OR

OVERCOME ANY BARRIERS TO COMPETITION BEFORE ANY SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITION FOR THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED

The Government recognizes the importance of fostering full and open competition for future acquisitions of similar services. The unique operational environment connected with the event, characterized by extreme demand, early block allocation, and security-driven constraints, has significantly limited the Government’ s ability to conduct meaningful competition in the immediate term.

This is a new contract for services not related to any other current or previous purchase.

Hotel services for up to 800 travelers, office space, internet lines, and parking for Senior High Level USG Principal traveling with a delegation inclusive of support elements in: Security, Communications, Logistics and Operations.

2025. The first travelers will arrive within two weeks of visit notification. The lack of time before US government travelers arrive does not allow enough time for full and open competition.

Security concerns prohibit sufficient advanced notification of VIP travel to allow for sufficient time to conduct full and open competition. The Department of State can only communicate with the staff at Posts abroad when authorization is given due to security concerns. They have an extremely short turnaround time when authorization has been granted for negotiations to commence and site selections to be finalized with both the local vendors and Posts before the actual Senior High Level USG VIP visit occurs. Security and logistical teams make determinations during the site survey as to which hotels are most suitable for the Senior High Level USG VIP and his traveling staff to remain overnight. Consideration of the Senior High Level USG Principal and the location are taken into consideration as a determining factor.

Unique requirements for communications support are under severe time limitations and always a determining factor in the selection process as its capacity to be augmented to the unique requirements necessary to support certain Senior High Level USG Principals.

Many of the arrangements for hotel and transportation are often not confirmed until just before the actual visit. In addition to supporting a large delegation within a short time frame, last minute and frequent changes of itineraries for supporting personnel often result in significant changes in how Posts work with the vendors. With the exception of a few trips, contracts are not permitted to be signed until the Department of State (Post) has written confirmation from all supporting agencies, which enables collection of funds from said agencies in the event of cancellation. This results in an unusual and compelling urgency in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2.

This proven infrastructure supports uninterrupted supply continuity and minimizes risk of delay, factors critical to meeting the Veterans’ needs. The contract requires delivery of specialized in-home hospital beds and accessories to the individual VAMCs, with free on-board (FOB) destination, in accordance with the specific delivery instructions contained within the delivery orders. The contractor shall deliver to any VAMC within the United States and its outlying Territories and areas to include the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Alaska, and Hawaii upon issuance of a delivery order. The contractor shall also provide a commercial warranty in accordance with industry standards. The contractor must guarantee their ability to provide an uninterrupted source of supply of the awarded devices to satisfy the Government’s requirements for the effective period of the contract. The current contractor has the required supply chain in place to fulfill orders on a nationwide basis. Onboarding a new vendor to fulfill this requirement and deliver the hospital beds and accessories before the expiration of the current contract is not possible and would introduce delays and increased costs that would prevent timely performance and compromise patient care and safety. A new vendor would require at least 45 days to become fully operational. Therefore, Invacare is the only responsible source uniquely positioned to fulfill orders received from VAMCs in a timely manner. Invacare has provided an uninterrupted source of supply and commercial warranty of the hospital beds and accessories since 2020 and has delivered to locations within the United States and US Territories. From July 2023 through March 2025, under the previously awarded 5-year contract 36C10G18D0018, Invacare provided over in-home hospital beds or accessories to Veterans across the nation, demonstrating the capability to fulfill both standard and large-scale orders. Invacare is immediately capable of meeting all requirements of the contract and has the required capabilities to deliver the necessary products without interruption in supply or degradation of quality of care to the Veteran. Cost Savings: Without a bridge contract, VA would lack a National Contract vehicle to provide in-home hospital beds and accessories to Veterans in the community and VAMCs will be required to purchase the items through local Network Contracting Offices (NCO’s), potentially at open market prices, which would result in major financial loss to the Government and significantly delay the time it takes for the Veteran to receive the clinically required items.

Invacare is immediately capable of meeting all requirements of the contract and has the required capabilities to deliver the necessary products without interruption in supply or degradation of quality of care to the Veteran. Cost Savings: Without a bridge contract, VA would lack a National Contract vehicle to provide in-home hospital beds and accessories to Veterans in the community and VAMCs will be required to purchase the items through local Network Contracting Offices (NCO’s), potentially at open market prices, which would result in major financial loss to the Government and significantly delay the time it takes for the Veteran to receive the clinically required items.

Attachment 1: Request for Sole Source Justification Format >SAT Revision: 04 Effective Date: 12/15/25 Acquisition ID#: 36C257-26-AP-3833

DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS

Justification and Approval (J&A) For Other Than Full and Open Competition (>SAT) Acquisition Plan Action ID: 36C257-26-AP-3833

1. Contracting Activity: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 17, at 11495 Turner Road, El Paso, TX, 79936-1372, intends to enter into a sole source contract based on this Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition for the South Texas Veterans Health Care System (STVHCS), Audie L. Murphy VA Medical Center (ALMVAMC), 7400 Merton Minter Street, San Antonio, TX 78229-4404. The purchase request number is 671-26-3066-0338.

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved: This procurement is an urgent, short-term Fixed Price (FP) contract required to maintain uninterrupted perfusionist support at the Audie L. Murphy VA Medical Center (ALMVAMC). Immediate action is necessary to ensure continuity of cardiothoracic surgical operations, which cannot safely proceed without qualified perfusionist staff. EVT, Inc., the current provider, is fully trained, credentialed, and embedded in the clinical environment and can continue performing these services without delay. This short-term action is strictly a bridge requirement to sustain patient care while the facility completes the competitive acquisition for long-term services.

3. Description of Supplies/Services Required to Meet the Agency’s Needs: The ALMVAMC requires certified clinical perfusionist services, including autotransfusion, ECMO support, and weekday, weekend, and holiday on-call coverage, to support ongoing and emergent cardiothoracic surgical procedures. Failure to secure immediate coverage would create unacceptable risk to patient safety and disrupt surgical operations.

A short-term FP contract is required to ensure continuous availability of qualified perfusionists until a fully competitive solicitation can be executed. EVT, Inc. is the only provider capable of performing without onboarding delays, training requirements, or credentialing gaps, and can immediately fulfill the full scope of perfusionist services. The estimated value for the six-month base period is $177,430.00.

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition: Unusual and Compelling Urgency per 41 USC §3304(a)(2) as implemented by RFO 6.103-2.

5. Demonstration that the Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or Nature of the Acquisition Requires the Use of the Authority Cited Above (applicability of authority): Immediate availability of qualified perfusionist support is essential to prevent risks to patient safety and continuity of cardiothoracic surgical services. EVT, Inc. is already performing at the facility, is fully trained in the ALMVAMC clinical environment, and meets all competency standards required by the VA, CDC, Department of Health, and The Joint Commission. EVT’s personnel can continue services without delay, making them the only practical and responsible source capable of meeting the urgent requirement.

36E79726D0004.text:
Justification and Approval For Other Than Full and Open Competition due to Unusual and Compelling Urgency National Acquisition Center

FAR 6.302-2

1. Contracting Activity:

Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Procurement, Acquisition and Logistics National Acquisition Center (NAC) Building 37, One Block North of 22nd Street Hines, IL 60141

2. Nature and Description of Action:

The proposed action is to award one non-competitive (sole source) Firm Fixed Price, Indefinite Delivery, Requirements-type contract for Prasugrel Hydrochloride (HCL) 5 milligram (mg) and 10mg tablets for a three-month period.

Prasugrel HCL Tablets were previously available to VA and other participating agencies via contract 36E79720D0007, which was awarded and administered by VA NAC. Contract 36E79720D0007 was awarded to Golden State Medical Supply, Inc. (GSMS) on January 16, 2020, and expired on February 20, 2025.

A solicitation, Request for Proposals (RFP) 36E79724R0024, was issued for full and open competition for Prasugrel HCL Tablets on September 13, 2024, with a due date and time for offers (extended via Amendment 0001) of October 8, 2024, at 2:30 PM Central Time. Like the expiring contract, RFP 36E79724R0024 sought award of a single Firm Fixed Price, Indefinite Delivery, Requirements-type contract with one base year ordering period and four one-year options.

Contract 36E79725D0013 was awarded to GSMS on January 27, 2025. However, this award has been protested by Cosette Pharmaceuticals, Inc., to the Court of Federal Claims, Case Number 25-279C, and a stay of performance of the new contract is in place.

A short-term contract, contract number 36E79725D0024, was awarded to GSMS on February 25, 2025, with the goal of ensuring supply until the protest regarding 36E79725D0013 was adjudicated or settled. Due to the urgent and compelling need, this requirement was not competed; a justification and approval for other than full and open competition in accordance with FAR 6.302-2 was signed by the Contracting Officer on February 26, 2025. Contract 36E79725D0024 contains an ordering period of March 3, 2025, through June 2, 2025. However, the contracting office learned that the protest case regarding 36E79725D0013 would not be heard until after the expiration of short-term contract 36E79725D0024. Therefore, another short-term contract (36E79725D0035) was awarded to ensure government agencies had access to the product until the case was adjudicated or settled. Contract 36E79725D0035 was awarded for a three-month base period and included a twoJustification & Approval – Prasugrel HCL Tablets Short Term Contract month option period, which was exercised. Contract 36E79725D0035 will expire on November 2, 2025. The contracting office understood that a ruling was expected in August 2025, but as of September 18, 2025, no ruling or further information has been received from the court. With the uncertainty regarding the timeline of the court’s decision (which may be further delayed due to the Government shutdown) and necessity to give the contractor sufficient notice to ensure stability in supply for another short-term contract, the contracting office shall prepare a new short-term contract.

Award of a short-term contract to GSMS will ensure that VA and other participating federal government agencies have access to a consistent source of supply of Prasugrel HCL Tablets until a decision is issued regarding the protest on 36E79725D0013. As GSMS is the holder of the expiring national contract 36E79720D0007, expired short-term contract 36E79725D0024, and short-term contract 36E79725D0035, a third short-term contract with GSMS ensures that the product itself will remain unchanged, thus eliminating the need for patients to receive new prescriptions and be switched to another version of Prasugrel HCL Tablets or another drug that treats the same indications.

3. Description of Supplies or Services:

The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Pharmacy Benefits Management (PBM) has identified Prasugrel HCL Tablets as uniform preferred products for standardization. VA national standardization contracts are awarded to acquire critical drug products in the package sizes and specifications required by VA and other participating agencies. National Standardization contracts require that contractors maintain an uninterrupted supply of products available with the Pharmaceutical Prime Vendors (PPVs) throughout the contract period. An uninterrupted supply is critical to ensure that patients receive the pharmaceuticals they require with consistent specifications and without delays.

The purpose of this acquisition is to ensure a continued national contract source for Prasugrel HCL Tablets for VA, Department of Defense (DoD), Bureau of Prisons (BOP), Indian Health Service (IHS), State Veteran Homes (Option 2 only), and the Federal Health Care Center until the protest regarding contract 36E79725D0013 is resolved. Prasugrel HCL Tablets are used to treat heart/blood vessel problems. The contracted items will be ordered and delivered via the VA and DoD Pharmaceutical Prime Vendor programs. The required products and estimated requirements for a three-month ordering period are below:

Item Description and Strength Package Size (Tablets per Bottle) Estimated usage, Three Months (Bottles) 1 Prasugrel HCL 10mg Tablets 30 20,066 2 Prasugrel HCL 5mg Tablets 30 1,182 Justification & Approval – Prasugrel HCL Tablets Short Term Contract The total estimated value for this contract is $122,271.12, which was calculated using the estimated requirements and awarded unit pricing.

The contractor is required to have a unique, 11-digit National Drug Code (NDC) number for all offered items. The NDC number must be specific to the contractor and to the drug being supplied. All bottles must be compatible with automated dispensing units (Baxter ATC Canisters, Optifill, etc.). All NDCs must be registered with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), First Data Bank, Medispan, and Multum. The contractor’s utilized manufacturing facilities and other places of performance must be FDA current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) acceptable for the contracted product type.

A Nonavailability Determination was issued on June 18, 2019, and approved by the Head of Contracting, as Prasugrel HCL Tablets is a product of India.

4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition:

The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2) as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Section 6.302-2 entitled, “Unusual and Compelling Urgency.” In accordance with FAR 6.304(a)(1), the Contracting Officer’s certification in Section 12 of this justification and approval (J&A) document will serve as approval of this document, as the proposed contract’s value is less than $750,000 and no VA procedures require a higher approving level.

When combined and including options, the two short-term contracts for Prasugrel HCL Tablets cover an ordering period of eight months and have a total estimated value of $326,048.24. This eight-month period is less than the one-year maximum period permitted by FAR 6.202-2(d)(ii).

5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority:

An urgent and compelling need has emerged for Prasugrel HCL Tablets. The previous national contract, 36E79720D0007, was awarded to Golden State Medical Supply, Inc. (GSMS) on January 16, 2020, and expired on February 20, 2025. A follow-on contract, 36E79725D0013, was awarded to GSMS on January 27, 2025. However, this award has been protested and a stay of performance of the new contract is in place. This short-term contract is necessary to ensure availability of Prasugrel HCL Tablets for VA and other agencies until the protest is resolved and performance of the new contract can resume.

A short-term contract, contract number 36E79725D0024, was awarded to GSMS on February 25, 2025, with the goal of ensuring supply until the protest regarding 36E79725D0013 was adjudicated or settled. Due to the urgent and compelling need, this requirement was not competed; a justification and approval for other than full and open competition in accordance with FAR 6.302-2 was signed by the Contracting Officer on February 26, 2025. Contract 36E79725D0024 contained an ordering period of March 3, 2025, through June 2, 2025. Justification & Approval – Prasugrel HCL Tablets Short Term Contract However, the contracting office later learned that the protest case regarding 36E79725D0013 would not be heard until after the expiration of short-term contract 36E79725D0024. Therefore, another short-term contract (36E79725D0035) was awarded to ensure government agencies had access to the product until the case was adjudicated or settled. Contract 36E79725D0035 was awarded for a three-month base period and included a twomonth option period, which was exercised. Contract 36E79725D0035 will expire on November 2, 2025. The contracting office understood that a ruling was expected in August 2025, but as of September 18, 2025, no ruling or further information has been received from the court. With the uncertainty regarding the timeline of the court’s decision and necessity to give the contractor sufficient notice to ensure stability in supply for another short-term contract, the contracting office must prepare a new short-term contract.

Without this short-term contract, VA and other participating agencies may not have access to an uninterrupted supply of this critical pharmaceutical. Prasugrel HCL Tablets are available on one FSS contract, but at extremely high prices (more than 40 times higher) compared to the short-term contract pricing with GSMS, the holder of expired contract 36E79720D0007. Furthermore, presence of a product on an FSS contract (or non-contract basis through the Pharmaceutical Prime Vendor) does not guarantee that the product will be in stock at any one time, let alone that an FSS contract holder can guarantee an uninterrupted supply over a sustained period.

Establishment of a short-term contract with the recently expired national contract holder under the authority at FAR 6.302-2 is in the Government’s best interest, as this contract will ensure continued availability of Prasugrel HCL Tablets and will ensure VA and other participating agencies can acquire Prasugrel HCL Tablets at fair and reasonable prices.

6. Description of Efforts to Solicit Offers from as Many Sources as Practicable:

Notice of this J&A will be publicized in accordance with FAR 6.305(b). As this acquisition is of unusual and compelling urgency, the contracting office did not have the time necessary to solicit multiple sources or publish a solicitation to SAM.gov. Contract 36E79725D0013, which was awarded on January 27, 2025, and which has a stay in performance in place until resolution of a bid protest, was competitively solicited and provided for full and open competition.

7. Fair and Reasonable Price Determination:

The unusual and compelling need requiring immediate award of this short-term contract did not allow for a competitive solicitation. Nonetheless, the Contracting Officer was able to compare proposed pricing with historically paid pricing for Prasugrel HCL Tablets, such as on the recently expired national contract 36E79720D0007. Furthermore, GSMS’s proposed pricing for Prasugrel HCL Tablets was found to be more favorable than the pricing available for comparable products from other sources, including on Federal Supply Schedule contracts and products available on a non-contract basis to participating agencies via the Pharmaceutical Prime Vendors.

In accordance with FAR 15.404-1(b)(2), the Contracting Officer has determined that prices Justification & Approval – Prasugrel HCL Tablets Short Term Contract offered by GSMS are fair and reasonable based on a comparison with historically paid pricing (FAR 15.404-1(b)(2)(ii)) and a comparison with published price list/market prices (FAR 15.404-1(b)(2)(iv)).

8. Market Research:

Due to the unusual and compelling need for this short-term contract, the Contracting Officer was unable to competitively solicit this requirement. Nonetheless, as the recently awarded 36E79725D0013 was competitively solicited, the Contracting Officer has recent data on availability of the drug in the U.S. market. Furthermore, the Contracting Officer reviewed Prasugrel HCL Tablets pricing data available to VA and other agency customers to ensure that proposed pricing for this short-term contract is fair and reasonable.

9. Other Facts:

This contract will consist of a single three-month ordering period with no options. The purpose of this short-term contract award is to ensure availability of Prasugrel HCL Tablets for VA and other agencies until the protest of 36E79725D0013 is resolved.

Without this short-term contract, VA and other participating agencies may not have access to an uninterrupted supply of Prasugrel HCL Tablets until the protest concerning 36E79725D0013 is resolved. The health of Veterans and other agency patients would be jeopardized without access to this critical pharmaceutical. Furthermore, the Firm Fixed prices secured by the Government in this short-term contract are far more favorable to the Government than any pricing available on other sources, including FSS contracts. Therefore, award of this short-term contract allows VA to serve its mission in the most cost-efficient manner possible.

10. Sources Expressing Interest:

As noted above, due to the unusual and compelling need for Prasugrel Tablets, the contracting office could not competitively solicit for this requirement. GSMS, the holder of recently expired contract 36E79720D0007 and expiring short-term contract 36E79725D0024, was interested and has immediate product availability of the same product as that on the previous national contract.

11. Actions to Remove Barriers to Future Competition:

As the purpose of this short-term contract award is to ensure availability of Prasugrel HCL Tablets for VA and other agencies until the protest of 36E79725D0013 is resolved, no barriers to future competition have been identified. Any future acquisition for Prasugrel HCL Tablets after the resolution of the current protest will maximize competition to the greatest extent practicable.

Justification & Approval – Prasugrel HCL Tablets Short Term Contract

J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 1

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION GSA LEASING SUPPORT SERVICES

1. Contracting Activity The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Building Service (PBS), Office of Leasing plans to contract by means other than full and open competition. This is a Sole Source Justification (SSJ).

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved This justification supports the award of a sole source contract for Leasing Support Services to ensure continued performance of critical services during the transition between the current GLS Plus contract and the future GLS Max contract. 47PH5426F0042.text:
J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 1

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION GSA LEASING SUPPORT SERVICES

1. Contracting Activity The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Building Service (PBS), Office of Leasing plans to contract by means other than full and open competition. This is a Sole Source Justification (SSJ).

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved This justification supports the award of a sole source contract for Leasing Support Services to ensure continued performance of critical services during the transition between the current GLS Plus contract and the future GLS Max contract. The bridge contract will be executed on a sole source basis under the authority of FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency. The justification detailing the unusual circumstances and compelling urgency precluding full and open competition, and the serious injury to the Government if there is a delay in award is detailed in this justification. The contract will provide for a base period of six (6) months, with options to extend, if necessary, to cover the gap in services anticipated due to delays in awarding the follow-on contract. The total estimated value, based on maximum net commissions for a one-year period, is $520,535,557.

3. Description of Supplies or Services Required GSA PBS is responsible for the acquisition and administration of leasehold interests and other real estate services in support of other federal agencies. As of the end of FY 2023, GSA had a total leased inventory of 7,638 leases with 177,404,648 square feet in 6,551 buildings located across the United States and territories.

Since the mid-1990s, GSA's lease acquisition workload has increased while the staffing of realty personnel has decreased. With directions to downsize and combine like efforts in the mid-1990s, GSA regional offices awarded eight (8) different real estate broker contracts to the private sector to test the feasibility of outsourcing GSA's Realty services. Over time, PBS recognized the regional contracts containing differing terms, conditions, and pricing structures. Following an Inspector General (IG) report in 2002 which identified multiple problems, GSA sought to centralize this function through the award of a national broker contract. Through various           J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 2 iterations, the national broker contract has become a critical part of fulfilling GSA’s mission to provide leased space to federal agencies.

The current contract, GLS Plus, was awarded on 13 May 2020. GLS Plus was awarded with four geographic zones and a menu of services. Each zone covers multiple regions, with the exception of the fourth zone, which covers only Region 11. Two contracts were awarded per zone, with the exception of the fourth zone which had three contract awards. The zonal awards, administered nationally, continued the consistency of services provided by the contractors within zones, and opened the national requirement to small businesses. The final option year of GLS Plus was set to expire on 15 July 2025. GLS Plus contract is currently under a three-month extension through 15 Oct 2025 under FAR 52.217-8, with option to be extended through 15 January 2026. A replacement contract, GLS Max, was in development with the solicitation set to be issued in early 2025. As the solicitation was in development, the government offered the Deferred Resignation Program (DRP) for employees wishing to exit federal service. All 1102 contracting personnel previously responsible for administering the leasing program participated in the DRP, leaving the office without qualified lease acquisition staff at a critical time. A new team was assigned to draft the GLS Max solicitation; however, unforeseen administrative challenges have delayed the procurement process for an estimated six to nine months. The Leasing Support Services contract delivers mission-critical real estate support to agencies across the Federal Government and the Department of Defense (DoD). Due to the essential nature of these services, any gap in contract coverage would result in unacceptable operational disruptions.

4. Identification of the Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. § 3204(a)(2) / 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2), as implemented by FAR 6.302-2 – Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

5. Demonstration the Nature of the Acquisition Requires Use of Authority Cited This justification is based on the urgent and compelling need to maintain continuity of missioncritical services. A lapse in Leasing Support Services would severely hinder GSA’s ability to acquire and manage leased space for Federal and DoD agencies. The current contractors are already fully mobilized, integrated into GSA systems, and have the necessary knowledge of ongoing projects, which makes them best positioned to provide seamless continuation of services under this bridge contract. GSA is currently developing the solicitation for the replacement contract, GLS Max. This effort is expected to take a minimum of six to nine months to get to award. Post-award, any new contractors will require additional time getting security requirements and training prior to being issued a notice to proceed.           J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 3

6. Description of Efforts Made to Ensure Offers Are Solicited from as Many Sources as Practicable Given the urgency of the requirement and the short timeline between the expiration of the current contract and the anticipated award of GLS Max, GSA will not have sufficient time to conduct a competitive acquisition for interim services. A new competition will take months to develop, risking a lapse in services. However, efforts will be made to ensure that the GLS Max solicitation is completed and awarded as quickly as possible. Given these circumstances, GSA plans to issue a 6-month bridge contract with option to extend services under FAR 52.217-8 for up to an additional 6-month period up to one year, not to exceed the time necessary for the agency to enter into another contract through use of competitive procedures.

7. Determination by the Contracting Officer That the Anticipated Cost to the Government Will Be Fair and Reasonable The Contracting Officer will determine the price to be fair and reasonable by utilizing price analysis techniques to include market rates, comparison with previous contract prices (including the GLS Plus rates), independent government cost estimates, and any available historical pricing data. The short duration and scope of the bridge will be limited to the minimum required to meet urgent needs, helping to ensure reasonable cost.

8. Description of the Market Research Conducted Due to the urgency and the short duration of the bridge contract, extensive market research was not feasible. Prior market research from the GLS Max acquisition effort has shown the existence of multiple capable sources. This bridge contract is only intended as a stopgap measure to allow time for a full and open competition for GLS Max.

9. Any Other Supporting Facts Ɣ The GLS Plus contract expired on 15 July 2025 and is currently operating under a FAR 52.217-8 extension, which cannot be extended beyond 15 January 2026. Ɣ All 1102 contracting personnel previously responsible for administering the GLS Plus contract participated in the deferred resignation program, leaving the office without qualified acquisition personnel at a critical time. Ɣ A new acquisition team was assigned to draft the GLS Max solicitation in April 2025. Ɣ The new team faced delays after being tasked with developing an alternate acquisition strategy that aligned with the new administration’s goals Ɣ Current and projected leasing task volumes have increased, making continued support critical. A lapse in services would result in a significant backlog in lease actions, affecting space delivery to federal agencies and possibly resulting in higher lease costs due to delays.           J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 4 Ɣ The estimated cost to the Government based on the value of lease actions that would not be acquired are $2,602,677,787

The GLS Plus award includes eight contracts; however, two contractors hold separate contracts in different geographical zones, resulting in a total of six distinct active contractors. All interested vendors will have an opportunity to compete under the full and open GLS Max solicitation once released.

11. This bridge is solely to address the gap period for the minimum amount of time required and will not be used to delay or replace a competitive acquisition.

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION GSA LEASING SUPPORT SERVICES

1. Contracting Activity The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Building Service (PBS), Office of Leasing plans to contract by means other than full and open competition. This is a Sole Source Justification (SSJ).

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved This justification supports the award of a sole source contract for Leasing Support Services to ensure continued performance of critical services during the transition between the current GLS Plus contract and the future GLS Max contract. The bridge contract will be executed on a sole source basis under the authority of FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency. The justification detailing the unusual circumstances and compelling urgency precluding full and open competition, and the serious injury to the Government if there is a delay in award is detailed in this justification. The contract will provide for a base period of six (6) months, with options to extend, if necessary, to cover the gap in services anticipated due to delays in awarding the follow-on contract. The total estimated value, based on maximum net commissions for a one-year period, is $520,535,557.

3. Description of Supplies or Services Required GSA PBS is responsible for the acquisition and administration of leasehold interests and other real estate services in support of other federal agencies. As of the end of FY 2023, GSA had a total leased inventory of 7,638 leases with 177,404,648 square feet in 6,551 buildings located across the United States and territories.

Since the mid-1990s, GSA's lease acquisition workload has increased while the staffing of realty personnel has decreased. With directions to downsize and combine like efforts in the mid-1990s, GSA regional offices awarded eight (8) different real estate broker contracts to the private sector to test the feasibility of outsourcing GSA's Realty services. Over time, PBS recognized the regional contracts containing differing terms, conditions, and pricing structures. Following an Inspector General (IG) report in 2002 which identified multiple problems, GSA sought to centralize this function through the award of a national broker contract. Through various           J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 2 iterations, the national broker contract has become a critical part of fulfilling GSA’s mission to provide leased space to federal agencies.

The current contract, GLS Plus, was awarded on 13 May 2020. GLS Plus was awarded with four geographic zones and a menu of services. Each zone covers multiple regions, with the exception of the fourth zone, which covers only Region 11. Two contracts were awarded per zone, with the exception of the fourth zone which had three contract awards. The zonal awards, administered nationally, continued the consistency of services provided by the contractors within zones, and opened the national requirement to small businesses. The final option year of GLS Plus was set to expire on 15 July 2025. GLS Plus contract is currently under a three-month extension through 15 Oct 2025 under FAR 52.217-8, with option to be extended through 15 January 2026. A replacement contract, GLS Max, was in development with the solicitation set to be issued in early 2025. As the solicitation was in development, the government offered the Deferred Resignation Program (DRP) for employees wishing to exit federal service. All 1102 contracting personnel previously responsible for administering the leasing program participated in the DRP, leaving the office without qualified lease acquisition staff at a critical time. A new team was assigned to draft the GLS Max solicitation; however, unforeseen administrative challenges have delayed the procurement process for an estimated six to nine months. The Leasing Support Services contract delivers mission-critical real estate support to agencies across the Federal Government and the Department of Defense (DoD). Due to the essential nature of these services, any gap in contract coverage would result in unacceptable operational disruptions.

4. Identification of the Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. § 3204(a)(2) / 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2), as implemented by FAR 6.302-2 – Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

5. Demonstration the Nature of the Acquisition Requires Use of Authority Cited This justification is based on the urgent and compelling need to maintain continuity of missioncritical services. A lapse in Leasing Support Services would severely hinder GSA’s ability to acquire and manage leased space for Federal and DoD agencies. The current contractors are already fully mobilized, integrated into GSA systems, and have the necessary knowledge of ongoing projects, which makes them best positioned to provide seamless continuation of services under this bridge contract. GSA is currently developing the solicitation for the replacement contract, GLS Max. This effort is expected to take a minimum of six to nine months to get to award. Post-award, any new contractors will require additional time getting security requirements and training prior to being issued a notice to proceed.           J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 3

47PH5426F0098.text:
J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 1

JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION GSA LEASING SUPPORT SERVICES

1. Contracting Activity The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Building Service (PBS), Office of Leasing plans to contract by means other than full and open competition. This is a Sole Source Justification (SSJ).

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved This justification supports the award of a sole source contract for Leasing Support Services to ensure continued performance of critical services during the transition between the current GLS Plus contract and the future GLS Max contract. The bridge contract will be executed on a sole source basis under the authority of FAR 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency. The justification detailing the unusual circumstances and compelling urgency precluding full and open competition, and the serious injury to the Government if there is a delay in award is detailed in this justification. The contract will provide for a base period of six (6) months, with options to extend, if necessary, to cover the gap in services anticipated due to delays in awarding the follow-on contract. The total estimated value, based on maximum net commissions for a one-year period, is $520,535,557.

3. Description of Supplies or Services Required GSA PBS is responsible for the acquisition and administration of leasehold interests and other real estate services in support of other federal agencies. As of the end of FY 2023, GSA had a total leased inventory of 7,638 leases with 177,404,648 square feet in 6,551 buildings located across the United States and territories.

Since the mid-1990s, GSA's lease acquisition workload has increased while the staffing of realty personnel has decreased. With directions to downsize and combine like efforts in the mid-1990s, GSA regional offices awarded eight (8) different real estate broker contracts to the private sector to test the feasibility of outsourcing GSA's Realty services. Over time, PBS recognized the regional contracts containing differing terms, conditions, and pricing structures. Following an Inspector General (IG) report in 2002 which identified multiple problems, GSA sought to centralize this function through the award of a national broker contract. Through various           J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 2 iterations, the national broker contract has become a critical part of fulfilling GSA’s mission to provide leased space to federal agencies.

The current contract, GLS Plus, was awarded on 13 May 2020. GLS Plus was awarded with four geographic zones and a menu of services. Each zone covers multiple regions, with the exception of the fourth zone, which covers only Region 11. Two contracts were awarded per zone, with the exception of the fourth zone which had three contract awards. The zonal awards, administered nationally, continued the consistency of services provided by the contractors within zones, and opened the national requirement to small businesses. The final option year of GLS Plus was set to expire on 15 July 2025. GLS Plus contract is currently under a three-month extension through 15 Oct 2025 under FAR 52.217-8, with option to be extended through 15 January 2026. A replacement contract, GLS Max, was in development with the solicitation set to be issued in early 2025. As the solicitation was in development, the government offered the Deferred Resignation Program (DRP) for employees wishing to exit federal service. All 1102 contracting personnel previously responsible for administering the leasing program participated in the DRP, leaving the office without qualified lease acquisition staff at a critical time. A new team was assigned to draft the GLS Max solicitation; however, unforeseen administrative challenges have delayed the procurement process for an estimated six to nine months. The Leasing Support Services contract delivers mission-critical real estate support to agencies across the Federal Government and the Department of Defense (DoD). Due to the essential nature of these services, any gap in contract coverage would result in unacceptable operational disruptions.

4. Identification of the Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. § 3204(a)(2) / 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(2), as implemented by FAR 6.302-2 – Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

5. Demonstration the Nature of the Acquisition Requires Use of Authority Cited This justification is based on the urgent and compelling need to maintain continuity of missioncritical services. A lapse in Leasing Support Services would severely hinder GSA’s ability to acquire and manage leased space for Federal and DoD agencies. The current contractors are already fully mobilized, integrated into GSA systems, and have the necessary knowledge of ongoing projects, which makes them best positioned to provide seamless continuation of services under this bridge contract. GSA is currently developing the solicitation for the replacement contract, GLS Max. This effort is expected to take a minimum of six to nine months to get to award. Post-award, any new contractors will require additional time getting security requirements and training prior to being issued a notice to proceed.           J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 3

6. Description of Efforts Made to Ensure Offers Are Solicited from as Many Sources as Practicable Given the urgency of the requirement and the short timeline between the expiration of the current contract and the anticipated award of GLS Max, GSA will not have sufficient time to conduct a competitive acquisition for interim services. A new competition will take months to develop, risking a lapse in services. However, efforts will be made to ensure that the GLS Max solicitation is completed and awarded as quickly as possible. Given these circumstances, GSA plans to issue a 6-month bridge contract with option to extend services under FAR 52.217-8 for up to an additional 6-month period up to one year, not to exceed the time necessary for the agency to enter into another contract through use of competitive procedures.

7. Determination by the Contracting Officer That the Anticipated Cost to the Government Will Be Fair and Reasonable The Contracting Officer will determine the price to be fair and reasonable by utilizing price analysis techniques to include market rates, comparison with previous contract prices (including the GLS Plus rates), independent government cost estimates, and any available historical pricing data. The short duration and scope of the bridge will be limited to the minimum required to meet urgent needs, helping to ensure reasonable cost.

8. Description of the Market Research Conducted Due to the urgency and the short duration of the bridge contract, extensive market research was not feasible. Prior market research from the GLS Max acquisition effort has shown the existence of multiple capable sources. This bridge contract is only intended as a stopgap measure to allow time for a full and open competition for GLS Max.

9. Any Other Supporting Facts Ɣ The GLS Plus contract expired on 15 July 2025 and is currently operating under a FAR 52.217-8 extension, which cannot be extended beyond 15 January 2026. Ɣ All 1102 contracting personnel previously responsible for administering the GLS Plus contract participated in the deferred resignation program, leaving the office without qualified acquisition personnel at a critical time. Ɣ A new acquisition team was assigned to draft the GLS Max solicitation in April 2025. Ɣ The new team faced delays after being tasked with developing an alternate acquisition strategy that aligned with the new administration’s goals Ɣ Current and projected leasing task volumes have increased, making continued support critical. A lapse in services would result in a significant backlog in lease actions, affecting space delivery to federal agencies and possibly resulting in higher lease costs due to delays.           J&A, Other Than Full and Open, GSA Leasing Support Services, Interim Contract 4 Ɣ The estimated cost to the Government based on the value of lease actions that would not be acquired are $2,602,677,787

10. Listing of Sources, if Any, That Expressed Interest in the Acquisition All current contractors under the GLS Plus IDIQ will be contacted. The GLS Plus award includes eight contracts; however, two contractors hold separate contracts in different geographical zones, resulting in a total of six distinct active contractors. GLS Plus Zone 1 47PA0520D0009 Jones Lang LaSalle, Americas, Inc. 47PA0520D0008 CBRE, Inc. Zone 2 47PA0520D0005 Savills, Inc. 47PA0520D0004 Public Properties Zone 3

47PA0520D0007

Carpenter/Robbins Commercial Real Estate, Inc. 47PA0520D0006 Cushman & Wakefield Zone 4 47PA0520D0003 CBRE, Inc. 47PA0520D0002 Public Properties 47PA0520D0001 Savills, Inc.

All interested vendors will have an opportunity to compete under the full and open GLS Max solicitation once released.

11. Actions the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome Barriers to Competition in the Future GSA is actively finalizing the GLS Max competitive solicitation, which will be issued under full and open competition. This bridge is solely to address the gap period for the minimum amount of time required and will not be used to delay or replace a competitive acquisition.
